title: Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) Cosponsors Bipartisan Strengthening Essential Manufacturing and Industrial (SEMI) Investment Act and Semiconductor Technology Advancement and Research (STAR) Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) today cosponsored two bipartisan bills to extend and expand the Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit (AMIC), continuing his work to make Upstate New York a national leader in semiconductor manufacturing.

The Strengthening Essential Manufacturing and Industrial (SEMI) Investment Act extends the AMIC through 2031 and expands eligibility for the CHIPS Act tax credit to include upstream materials. The Semiconductor Technology Advancement and Research (STAR) Act incentivizes research and chip design investments.

Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) said, “Semiconductor manufacturing will be the cornerstone of economic growth in Central New York and the Mohawk Valley. We need to continue making the right investments and advancing policies that support every part of the industry, from research and design to materials and manufacturing. The bipartisan SEMI Investment Act and STAR Act will help create jobs, strengthen our national security, and keep American innovation here at home.”

Strengthening Essential Manufacturing and Industrial (SEMI) Investment Act

The bipartisan SEMI Investment Act extends the AMIC through 2031, expands the CHIPS Act tax credit to include upstream materials, and requires annual materials qualification lists from Treasury and Commerce. Under current law, the term “materials” is not included in the AMIC, excluding domestic manufacturers of semiconductor materials from the tax credit. The gap in the credit results in companies building overseas and relying on foreign adversaries. The SEMI Act directly addresses the gap and incentivizes domestic production by including suppliers of upstream materials. The expansion of this credit will ensure America’s economic resilience and strengthen our national defense.

The SEMI Investment Act is endorsed by the following organizations:

NY SMART I-Corridor, SEMI, Entegris, CoorsTek, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Qnity Electronics, Brewer Science, the American Chemistry Council, the Compressed Gas Association, and EFC Gases & Advanced Materials.

This bill was introduced by Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA) and Brendan Boyle (D-PA) and has a Senate companion introduced by Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-TN), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Thom Tillis (R-NC), and Chris Coons (D-DE). Additional cosponsors of this legislation include Reps. Jared Golden (D-ME), Sarah McBride (D-DE), Eugene Vindman (D-VA), Joe Morelle (D-NY), Lori Trahan (D-MA), Claudia Tenney (R-NY), Blake Moore (R-UT), and Michael McCaul (R-TX).

Semiconductor Technology Advancement and Research (STAR) Act

The bipartisan STAR Act creates an investment tax credit for semiconductor design and development expenditures. The legislation ensures that the United States continues to drive technological leadership and that we close the gap in semiconductor research and development. The STAR Act also extends the AMIC for the next 10 years to ensure that domestic manufacturing continues to grow.

This bill was introduced by Rep. Blake Moore (R-UT) and is cosponsored by Suzan DelBene (D-WA), Michael McCaul (R-TX), Doris Matsui (D-CA), John Moolenaar (R-MI), Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), Claudia Tenney (R-NY), Ro Khanna (D-CA), Joseph Morelle (D-NY), Vern Buchanan (R-FL), André Carson (D-IN), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ), Terri Sewell (D-AL), Jimmy Panetta (D-CA), Joe Neguse (D-CO), Darren Soto (D-FL), James Baird (R-IN), Kristen McDonald Rivet (D-MI), Sarah McBride (D-DE), Julia Brownley (D-CA), Suzanne Bonamici (D-OR), Greg Landsman (D-OH), Eugene Vindman (D-VA), Greg Stanton (D-AZ), Thomas Suozzi (D-NY), and Dave Min (D-CA).

title: Congressional Taiwan Caucus Co-Chairs Urge Lithuanian Leaders to Continue Bold Support for Taiwan in Joint Letter
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - Today, Representatives Mario Diaz-Balart (R-FL), Ami Bera (D-CA), Andy Barr (R-KY), and Greg Stanton (D-AZ), Co-Chairs of the Congressional Taiwan Caucus sent a joint letter to the Honorable Mindaugas Sinkevičius, Prime Minister of Lithuania; Honorable Gitanas Nausėda, President of Lithuania; Honorable Juozas Olekas, Speaker of the Seimas; Honorable Kęstutis Budrys, Foreign Minister; and Honorable Robertas Kaunas, Defense Minister, requesting that Lithuania continues its courageous path of maintaining relations with Taiwan.

A PDF of the letter can be found here, or read the full text below:

Honorable Leaders of Lithuania,

As co-chairs of the Congressional Taiwan Caucus, we highly value Lithuania’s friendship and steadfast support for freedom across the globe.

Since Lithuania overturned communist rule, our countries have stood together to defend freedom and democracy in Europe, the Western Hemisphere, and the Indo-Pacific. In fact, in the face of the People’s Republic of China’s (PRC) bullying and coercion, our countries have stood together to support a free and democratic Taiwan.

We welcomed Lithuania’s decision in 2022 to withdraw from 17+1 format, an organization which was created by the PRC to divide the transatlantic alliance. Lithuania also demonstrated remarkable leadership in convincing other Baltic states to do the same. We appreciate that Lithuania has always been a strong leader among the European Union countries in opposing autocratic influences, inviting Taiwan to open its office under the name of Taiwanese Representative Office in 2021.

While we understand that the PRC continues to bully countries for maintaining any relationship with Taiwan, we respectfully urge you to consider the importance of maintaining relationships with those that share our democratic values. the PRC also continues to enable Russia’s war against Ukraine, contrary to European interests.

For these reasons, we respectfully urge you to continue the courageous path of maintaining your substantive relationship with Taiwan, which has been a trusted and reliable partner of our respective countries for decades.

Sincerely,

Mario Diaz-Balart

Member of Congress

Ami Bera

Member of Congress

Andy Barr

Member of Congress

Greg Stanton

Member of Congress

title: McCaul, Hoyer, Colleagues Introduce the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Emeritus Michael McCaul (R-Texas) and Congressman Steny Hoyer (D-Md.) introduced the bipartisan Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 alongside 16 of their colleagues. This legislation — which honors the late Senator Lindsey Graham, who worked on the bill for more than a year and secured the White House’s support — will hold major purchasers of Russian oil and gas accountable for supporting Russia’s war against Ukraine and extend sanctions that restrict funding for Iran’s energy and weapons sectors.

“Senator Graham was a national security giant, a statesman of unmatched conviction, and a personal friend and mentor. We shared a fundamental worldview: America is strongest at home when it projects strength abroad. That’s why he fought so hard for this bill, which I promised him months ago I would introduce in the House,” said Rep. McCaul. “As President Zelensky told me last month when I visited Ukraine, he is ready for a ceasefire — ready to negotiate, as he has been for years. Putin, on the other hand, consistently defies President Trump and the international community by refusing to come to the table. I can think of no better way to honor Senator Graham’s life and legacy than by passing these tough sanctions, which will help force Putin into negotiations and bring us closer to securing Lindsey’s vision of enduring peace in two critical regions of the world.”

“Democracy is presently under threat from despotism, and Congress must act to defend democracy and help Ukraine defeat Vladimir Putin’s effort to extinguish its liberty and sovereignty. Our legislation goes after multiple sources of Russian war funding, including its oil and gas sectors, shadow fleet, and financial institutions. I’m encouraged that the Senate passed the companion legislation last week with overwhelming support, and I thank former Chairman McCaul for partnering with me to facilitate action by the House. This action has been delayed too long and will, hopefully, accelerate Ukraine’s success and the ending of this war, one that was initiated illegally by Putin and that has resulted in tens of thousands of deaths of Russians and Ukrainians. I hope that we can secure bipartisan consensus in the House and enact a sanctions package that will stem the flow of money to Russia’s war machine and contribute to a Ukrainian victory," said Rep. Hoyer.

Earlier this month, an overwhelming bipartisan majority in the Senate voted to pass companion legislation, by a vote of 86-11, led by Sens. Darline Graham (R-S.C.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Katie Britt (R-Ala.), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), Chair of the Senate Armed Services Committee Roger Wicker (R-Miss.), and Chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee Jim Risch (R-Idaho). The text of the House bill is identical to the text that passed the Senate.

“This legislation was deeply important to my brother, Lindsey, and I’m grateful that it has achieved such a wide coalition of support. Lindsey was committed to achieving a peaceful resolution to this war, and I’m confident that these sanctions will pave the way,” said Sen. Darline Graham. “I’m grateful to Rep. McCaul for leading this effort in the House. The Senate came together in a strong, bipartisan fashion to pass the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, and I hope the House of Representatives will do the same. Russia has waged war against Ukraine for far too long, and this bill assists President Trump in his noble efforts to bring it to a close.”

“Representatives McCaul, Hoyer, Wilson, Kaptur, and Fitzpatrick are longtime champions of Ukraine’s cause and I am glad to have them leading our legislation in the House of Representatives. After a massive bipartisan vote in the Senate, we are eager to turn to the House as we fight to get this legislation across the finish line. There is immense urgency in getting this done – July set a record for Russia’s use of ballistic missiles, killing and wounding dozens of Ukrainians, including many children. Cutting off the source of funding – profits from oil and gas – for these deadly weapons and Russia’s war machine is essential to ending the bloodshed,” said Sen. Blumenthal.

Joining McCaul and Hoyer as original cosponsors are Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus Joe Wilson (R-S.C.); Co-Founder and Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus Marcy Kaptur (D-Ohio); Co-Chair of the House Baltic Caucus Don Bacon (R-Neb.); Rep. Jake Auchincloss (D-Mass.), House Armed Services Committee Chairman Mike Rogers (R-Ala.), Reps. Jill Tokuda (D-Hawaii), Mike Turner (R-Ohio), Gabe Vasquez (D-N.M.), Ann Wagner (R-Mo.), Josh Gottheimer (D-N.J.), Andy Barr (R-Ky.), and Ed Case (D-Hawaii); Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus Brian Fitzpatrick (R-Pa.); and Reps. Eugene Vindman (D-Va.), Nathaniel Moran (R-Texas), and Chrissy Houlahan (D-Pa.).

"Senator Lindsey Graham and I shared the belief that opposing dictators in defense of freedom and liberty is always the right thing to do. War criminal Putin is losing his invasion of sovereign Ukraine and the threat to humanity posed by the Iranian regime is dire. It is time for Congress to give President Trump the strongest tools available to choke off Russia's war machine for the good of mankind and cripple the ability of Tehran to continue sowing chaos in the region and beyond. My friend and colleague worked tirelessly in championing these critical initiatives, and I am grateful to help advance them across the finish line in the House,” said Rep. Wilson.

“Dictator Vladimir Putin’s illegal invasion of Ukraine is failing—Ukraine is battering Russian war infrastructure and the Kremlin is losing tens of thousands of troops each month. Now is the time to intensify pressure on Putin through crippling sanctions while surging support for our Ukrainian allies,” said Rep. Kaptur. “Putin will not make peace until he is forced to. I have been a supporter of every bipartisan sanctions bill on the table to pressure Russia to end its illegal full-scale invasion, and I am confident that the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 will accomplish that mission. Designed to protect our allies who aid Ukraine while squeezing Putin and the countries that enable his invasion, the sweeping sanctions and targeted tariffs in this bill are the best chance we have to get bipartisan legislation signed into law to hold Russia accountable and achieve peace.”

“Putin’s illegal war is failing, but he will not choose peace until the cost becomes too high for Russia and those helping fund his brutality,” said Rep. Bacon. “Senator Lindsey Graham was one of Congress’s clearest voices for Ukraine, understood that Putin only responds to strength, and worked until his final days to advance the toughest sanctions package yet against Russia’s war machine. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act would impose crippling pressure on Russia and those enabling Putin’s aggression, honor Sen. Graham’s commitment to Ukraine’s fight for freedom, and make clear that America stands with Ukraine.”

“Since 2022, I have called on both Biden and Trump to empower Ukraine to win this war through both strikes and sanctions on Russian oil infrastructure. The strikes are finally happening, and with this bill the sanctions are coming,” said Rep. Auchincloss.

"I am proud to join in introducing this legislation to sanction Vladimir Putin and his thugs as well as the Iran and its terrorist regime,” said Rep. Rogers. “Every dollar denied to Vladimir Putin weakens his war machine. By choking off the oil and gas revenue fueling Russia's aggression, this legislation gives President Trump powerful leverage to force Putin into serious negotiations that deliver a truly lasting peace. Including additional sanctions on Iran is equally critical given the terrorist regime’s continued threats to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and its role in enabling Russia’s war against Ukraine. This legislation strengthens America’s hand against adversaries who threaten American security, our allies, and global stability.”

"It is long past time for Congress to impose tougher consequences on Russia and those financing its illegal war against Ukraine. I'm proud to support this updated legislation, which targets major purchasers of Russian oil and gas that continue to fund the Kremlin's aggression. This war has resulted in an estimated 2 million casualties, including more than half a million deaths. The United States must continue standing with the Ukrainian people and keep the pressure on Russia to agree to a just and lasting peace that preserves a free, sovereign, and independent Ukraine,” said Rep. Tokuda.

“For more than four years, the Ukrainian people have fought courageously to defend their sovereignty, and their resolve is paying off. Lindsey Graham understood that standing with nations fighting for freedom strengthens America’s own security, and until his final days, he was pressing for stronger sanctions against Russia,” said Rep. Turner. “This legislation honors that legacy, sends a clear message to Vladimir Putin that he cannot outlast Ukraine or the free world, and gives President Trump another powerful tool to pressure Russia, bring Putin to the negotiating table, and help restore peace to the region.”

“To end Russia’s unprovoked and deadly invasion of Ukraine, we must enact maximum financial pain on Vladimir Putin and his cronies. I will not stand idly by while countless people are killed due to Putin’s doomed quest to reconstitute the Soviet Union. I am beyond proud to join my colleagues in introducing this sweeping sanctions legislation that will enact severe financial penalties against Putin, his allies, and those who choose to do business with him. The largest war in Europe since World War II must come to an end, and I am confident these measures will accelerate that process. I am also pleased this bill extends the Iran Sanctions Act to ensure all available measures are available to cripple the terrorist Iranian regime. These necessary sanctions are a fitting legacy to honor the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a friend and colleague who continually fought for freedom, democracy, and against tyrannical regimes like Russia and Iran,” said Rep. Wagner.

"Vladimir Putin and the regime in Tehran are two of the gravest threats to America and our allies. For far too long, they've bankrolled their aggression by selling oil and gas to whoever will buy it,” said Rep. Gottheimer. "This bipartisan legislation cuts off those funding streams: holding accountable anyone who fills Putin's war chest as he wages his brutal, illegal war against Ukraine, and choking off the money that fuels Iran's weapons programs and its terror proxies. I was proud to see the Senate pass this bill with an overwhelming, bipartisan majority, and now it's on the House to finish the job. I can think of no better tribute to Senator Lindsey Graham — a national security champion — than enacting the tough sanctions he fought so hard for. Standing up to tyrants isn't a Democratic or Republican issue; it's an American one."

“By targeting the energy revenues and financial networks that fuel Putin’s war machine and enable the Iranian regime’s terrorist activities, this bipartisan legislation strengthens America’s ability to impose real economic consequences on our adversaries,” said Rep. Barr. “Senator Graham understood that harnessing America’s full strength from our financial system to our military is essential to deterring aggression, defending our allies, and advancing peace. I’m proud to join my colleagues to help carry forward that legacy.”

“Senator Graham believed, as I do, that American strength remains the surest guardian of peace,” said Rep. Fitzpatrick. “That conviction guided our work together on this legislation. Putin’s war machine runs on oil, money, and the willingness of others to look the other way—and the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 attacks all three. It isolates Russia’s banks, shuts down the networks financing its aggression, and forces every government and company enabling this war to make a choice. By increasing the cost of Putin’s war and reducing his ability to sustain it, this legislation strengthens the path to a just and lasting peace—one determined by Ukraine, not imposed by Moscow. The most fitting tribute Congress can offer Lindsey is to finish the work he began, carry forward the cause of freedom he championed, and make clear that America’s resolve will endure until that peace is secured.”

“Supporting a strong, free Ukraine is imperative for the national security of our communities here at home. Sanctioning Russia and Putin sends a direct message to the world: the United States will not sit by while brutal regimes bankroll aggression against democratic nations,” said Rep. Vindman. “I am proud to be a co-sponsor of this essential legislation. We must continue to escalate the economic pressure on the Kremlin and strengthen our resolve for the Ukrainian people as they fight for their freedom, sovereignty, and security.”

"Russia is perpetrating a war of aggression, and we must keep the pressure on Vladimir Putin. This action is long overdue, but we are finally moving forward with the resolve this moment demands. These sanctions will erode Russia's war machine by cutting off the revenue that funds it. We must hold those who are fueling this war accountable. These sanctions focus on Russia but will also target dangerous Chinese entities which support the Russian defense industrial base. Peace is the goal, and these mechanisms give the President the tools to achieve that goal,” said Rep. Moran.

“For more than four years, Ukrainians have courageously defended their freedom against Putin’s brutal invasion. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act would increase pressure on the Kremlin, hold those supporting its war accountable, and strengthen Ukraine’s position in pursuit of a just peace," said Rep. Houlahan. “The bill also extends longstanding sanctions against Iran. Sanctions cannot replace a clear strategy or the President’s obligation to seek congressional authorization for war, but they remain an important diplomatic tool. I am proud to cosponsor this legislation.”

title: THOMPSON, GUN VIOLENCE PREVENTION TASK FORCE SLAM ADMINISTRATION’S PLANS TO DEREGULATE FIREARMS
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Gun Violence Prevention Task Force ChairRep. Mike Thompson led a group of 122 colleagues in urging Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco,

Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Director Robert Cekada to reverse over 30 planned deregulatory actions related to firearms.

The over 30 planned actions represent one of the most sweeping federal firearms deregulation efforts in decades. The deregulatory actions would make it easier for prohibited persons, including felons and domestic abusers, to acquire firearms; make it harder for law enforcement to identify gun traffickers, solve firearm crimes, and prevent crimes; and weaken protections to prevent the sale of handguns to children and teenagers.

ATF’s own analysis of one of the deregulatory actions admits the potential harm. ATF wrote: ““[i]n such a case, a prohibited person who obtains a firearm under the proposed rule and, hypothetically, uses that firearm to inflict mass casualties, would have been prevented under the current baseline requirement to renew the background check.”

In a letter to ATF Director Robert Cekada, the lawmakers urged the proposed actions be reversed:

“These proposals would weaken longstanding gun violence prevention policies that Congress has approved or supported through legislation, appropriations, and oversight. We are especially concerned about changes that would loosen licensing standards, allow more gun sales to be sold without background checks, create risks that more prohibited persons will be able to obtain firearms illegally, increase remote firearm sales, hinder law enforcement’s ability to trace crime guns, reduce dealer accountability, weaken oversight of National Firearms Act weapons, narrow firearm prohibitions, and create new loopholes for illegal firearm transfers and straw purchases. These rules would make communities less safe and conflict with federal law, including

provisions in the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, which Congress enacted to strengthen background checks, target gun traffickers, and make it harder for dangerous individuals to access firearms,” wrote the lawmakers.

“We urge ATF to withdraw these proposals and conduct a comprehensive review of their cumulative impact on public safety before proceeding with any additional regulatory action. We further request that ATF provide Congress with a detailed public safety impact analysis explaining how these proposals, and any future proposals would affect firearm trafficking investigations, crime gun tracing, background check effectiveness, dealer accountability, domestic violence and suicide prevention efforts, and youth access to firearms, and that the agency brief Congress on the rationale for and expected consequences of—this and any future rules, before any implementation moves forward,” they concluded.

In addition to Thompson, the following representatives signed the letter: Gabe Amo, Yassamin Ansari, Jake Auchincloss, Becca Balint, Nanette Barragán, Joyce Beatty, Wesley Bell, Donald Beyer, Suzanne Bonamici, Julia Brownley, Shontel Brown, Nikki Budzinski, Salud Carbajal, André Carson, Troy Carter, Ed Case, Judy Chu, Gilbert Cisneros, Steve Cohen, Jason Crow, Danny Davis, Madeleine Dean, Diana DeGette, Rosa DeLauro, Christopher Deluzio, Mark DeSaulnier, Maxine Dexter, Debbie Dingell, Veronica Escobar, Dwight Evans, Lizzie Fletcher, Bill Foster, Laura Friedman, Maxwell Frost, John Garamendi, Jesús García, Sylvia Garcia, Daniel Goldman, Josh Gottheimer, Al Green, Adelita Grijalva, Jahana Hayes, James Himes, Steny Hoyer, Jared Huffman, Glenn Ivey, Jonathan Jackson, Sara Jacobs, Henry Johnson, Julie Johnson, Sydney Kamlager-Dove, William Keating, Robin Kelly, Timothy Kennedy, Ro Khanna, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Rick Larsen, John Larson, Susie Lee, Ted Lieu, Zoe Lofgren, Stephen Lynch, Doris Matsui, Lucy McBath, Sarah McBride, April McClain Delaney, Jennifer McClellan, Betty McCollum, James McGovern, Analilia Mejia, Christian Menefee, Robert Menendez, Dave Min, Gwen Moore, Joseph Morelle, Kelly Morrison, Jared Moskowitz, Seth Moulton, Frank Mrvan, Kevin Mullin, Jerrold Nadler, Richard Neal, Eleanor Norton, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Johnny Olszewski, Nancy Pelosi, Scott Peters, Brittany Pettersen, Chellie Pingree, Stacey Plaskett, Mark Pocan, Mike Quigley, Delia Ramirez, Luz Rivas, Patrick Ryan, Andrea Salinas, Linda Sánchez, Mary Gay Scanlon, Janice Schakowsky, Bradley Schneider, Hillary Scholten, Robert Scott, Terri Sewell, Lateefah Simon, Adam Smith, Greg Stanton, Haley Stevens, Suhas Subramanyam, Thomas Suozzi, Shri Thanedar, Mike Thompson, Dina Titus, Jill Tokuda, Ritchie Torres, Lori Trahan, Juan Vargas, Nydia Velázquez, James Walkinshaw, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Maxine Waters, Bonnie Watson Coleman, George Whitesides, and Frederica Wilson.

“After years of declining gun crime due to strong firearm policies enacted during the Biden Administration, President Trump is systematically and methodically dismantling the very institutions, regulations, and systems that have directly led to the declines many major cities have been experiencing. The more than 30 firearms-related regulatory proposals introduced by ATF is the latest in this mass deregulation scheme, making it easier for firearms to be trafficked into communities most vulnerable to gun violence and serving the financial interests of the gun industry at the expense of public safety. Brady is grateful to the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force for speaking out against this deadly interdependent regulatory package and for the Task Force’s steadfast dedication to freeing America from gun violence,” said Kris Brown, President, Brady.

“The Trump administration’s effort to dismantle these critical ATF reforms is reckless and wrong. These rollbacks will make gun trafficking easier and put communities at greater risk. Taken together, they would weaken federal firearms safeguards, reduce gun industry accountability, limit law enforcement oversight, and arm dangerous individuals,” said GIFFORDS Executive Director Emma Brown. “At a time when communities continue to endure the devastating consequences of gun violence, federal agencies should strengthen enforcement tools and support compliance with existing law—not dismantle safeguards that keep Americans safe. GIFFORDS applauds the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force for their actions to stop the Trump administration's efforts.”

"Months after calling himself part of the gun industry at an NRA convention, Todd Blanche stood alongside gun lobbyists to roll out more than 30 ATF rules that pad industry profits and, by ATF's own admission, make mass casualty events more likely. The House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force is standing up for the vast majority of Americans who don’t think public safety should be for sale, and we’re thankful for their continued leadership,” said John Feinblatt, President of Everytown for Gun Safety.

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

The Honorable Robert Cekada

Director

Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives

99 New York Avenue, NE

Washington, DC 20226

Dear Director Cekada:

As members of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force, we write to express our deep concern regarding the Department of Justice (DOJ) and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives’ (ATF’s) April 2026 series of more than 30 firearms-related regulatory proposals.

Together these proposals would significantly alter longstanding federal laws and policies governing firearm sales, transfers, recordkeeping, dealer accountability, and background checks, as well as the regulation of National Firearms Act (NFA) weapons and the enforcement of firearms trafficking laws. Collectively, they constitute one of the most sweeping federal firearms deregulation efforts in decades.

We are highly concerned that these proposals would undermine public safety by reducing accountability for Federal Firearms Licensees (FFLs) — including dealers, manufacturers, and importers—expanding opportunities for firearms trafficking and making it easier for prohibited individuals to obtain firearms.

These proposals would weaken longstanding gun violence prevention policies that Congress has approved or supported through legislation, appropriations, and oversight. We are especially concerned about changes that would loosen licensing standards, allow more gun sales to be sold without background checks, create risks that more prohibited persons will be able to obtain firearms illegally, increase remote firearm sales, hinder law enforcement’s ability to trace crime guns, reduce dealer accountability, weaken oversight of National Firearms Act weapons, narrow firearm prohibitions, and create new loopholes for illegal firearm transfers and straw purchases.

These rules would make communities less safe and conflict with federal law, including

provisions in the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, which Congress enacted to strengthen background checks, target gun traffickers, and make it harder for dangerous individuals to access firearms.

As you know, gun violence is the leading cause of death for American children and teens, as well as for law enforcement officers killed in the line of duty. Critically, ATF’s own analysis acknowledges the potential harm of its proposed rules, stating in one case, “[i]n such a case, a prohibited person who obtains a firearm under the proposed rule and, hypothetically, uses that firearm to inflict mass casualties, would have been prevented under the current baseline requirement to renew the background check.” ATF’s rule changes should not be considered in isolation, as the rules interact in ways that magnify the negative impacts of the proposed changes. When evaluated altogether, it becomes clear that this series of proposed rules will have a catastrophic impact on public safety, enabling firearm trafficking and widespread violence.

We therefore raise serious concerns with the following changes that make our communities less

safe:

ATF has proposed changes to make it easier for prohibited persons, including felons and domestic abusers, minors, and other dangerous persons to illegally acquire firearms:

ATF proposes allowing fully remote online gun sales, allowing dangerous people to skip the gun store and ship firearms directly to their home.

ATF proposes creating a new “spousal” firearm trafficking loophole by allowing the sale of firearms to couples without any requirement to check that both partners are legally eligible to access a firearm.

ATF proposes rewriting longstanding mental health regulations such that individuals currently prohibited from gun possession for mental health reasons will now be allowed to possess firearms.

ATF proposes redesigning the background check form, making it harder for customers, especially prohibited purchasers, and responsible FFLs to understand the legal restrictions to accessing firearms.

ATF proposes weakening the federal requirement for a background check on firearm sales at FFLs in states without NICS-equivalent background check standards for firearm licenses.

Americans overwhelmingly agree that people who are a danger to themselves or others should not be able to access firearms, but ATF’s proposed rules eviscerate the federal background check system, which is the first line of defense against gun trafficking and prohibited purchasers from accessing firearms.

ATF has proposed changes that will make it harder for law enforcement to identify gun

traffickers, solve firearm crimes, and prevent crimes:

ATF proposes eliminating the requirement that local law enforcement are notified whenever a community member applies for a NFA weapon.

ATF proposes narrowing the requirement that the owner of an NFA weapon obtain approval from ATF before bringing the weapon across state lines.

ATF proposes destroying gun transfer records after a period of 20 or 30 years, making it nearly impossible to trace older guns used in crimes.

By proposing to keep law enforcement in the dark about the sale of highly regulated firearms and by destroying records needed to trace guns used in crimes, law enforcement will have less information and fewer tools to keep our communities safe.

ATF has proposed weakening protections to prevent the sale of handguns to children and teenagers.

ATF proposes eliminating the requirement for FFLs to post signage and provide written notice to all handgun purchasers that it is unlawful to provide or allow juveniles unsupervised access to handguns.

Handguns are used in the vast majority of youth firearm crimes, and providing a written notice at the time of a handgun sale is an inexpensive and reasonable requirement that increases awareness of a major public safety risk.

ATF has proposed changing the legal standard for determining whether an FFL’s license can be revoked for willfully violating the Gun Control Act (GCA).

ATF proposes raising the threshold for what constitutes a “willful” violation of firearms law that would prompt ATF to consider suspending or revoking a FFL’s license or imposing other civil penalties.

The DOJ estimates that less than five percent of FFLs are responsible for selling 90 percent of firearms recovered at crimes. This change will make it more difficult for ATF to hold the small number of FFLs engaging in reckless and illegal business practices accountable for their actions.

ATF’s mission is to protect the public from gun crime and to enforce our nation’s federal firearms laws. We are extremely concerned that these regulatory proposals would move the agency away from that core mission and instead enable further gun crime, trafficking, and violence to be committed.

We urge ATF to withdraw these proposals and conduct a comprehensive review of their

cumulative impact on public safety before proceeding with any additional regulatory action. We further request that ATF provide Congress with a detailed public safety impact analysis explaining how these proposals, and any future proposals would affect firearm trafficking investigations, crime gun tracing, background check effectiveness, dealer accountability, domestic violence and suicide prevention efforts, and youth access to firearms, and that the agency brief Congress on the rationale for—and expected consequences of—this and any future rules, before any implementation moves forward.

We trust you will treat this matter with the urgency it demands and look forward to your prompt response.

Sincerely,

title: Rep. Dave Min’s Bill Passes Out of the Senate,  Bipartisan Legislation to Address Benefit Claims Backlog for Injured and Fallen Public Safety Officers
text:
Washington, D.C. — Representative Dave Min announced that the bipartisan Officer John Barnes and Chief Michael Ansbro Public Safety Officers' Benefits Program Expansion Act of 2026 has passed the U.S. Senate.

Originally introduced by Reps. Dave Min and Randy Weber (R-TX-14), alongside companion legislation from Sens. Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Ted Cruz (R-TX), the legislation reforms the Public Safety Officers’ Benefits (PSOB) Program to speed up benefit determinations and reduce claims backlogs.

“This is an incredibly meaningful milestone, and I’m proud that this bill is focused on keeping our promise to the law enforcement officers and first responders who risk their lives to keep our communities safe,” said Rep. Min. “For too long, families and injured officers have been trapped in bureaucratic limbo waiting years for the benefits they earned through extraordinary sacrifice. This bipartisan bill helps ensure that when first responders answer the call without hesitation, the federal government does too. I’m grateful for our partners in the Senate for their work to move this bill forward, and the House must do the same – our law enforcement officers are counting on us.”

Congress established the U.S. Department of Justice’s Bureau of Justice Assistance’s (BJA) Public Safety Officers’ Benefits (PSOB) Program in 1976 to provide death benefits to survivors of officers who have died in the line of duty. Since then, PSOB has been amended several times to provide disability and education benefits and to expand benefit eligibility.

Despite these amendments, beneficiaries often experience delayed adjudication of death and disability claims.

This legislation is endorsed by over 35 organizations and unions, including: International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP), National Association of Police Organizations (NAPO), United States Deputy Sheriff's Association (USDSA), National Narcotic Officers' Associations' Coalition (NNOAC), Major County Sheriffs of America (MCSA), Fraternal Order of Police (FOP), Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association (FLEOA), American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees (AFSCME), the Peace Officers Research Association of California (PORAC), California Narcotics Officers’ Association (CNOA), Police Chiefs' Association of Orange County, Riverside Sheriffs' Association, California Association of Highway Patrolmen (CAHP), & Orange County Sheriff’s Department.,

A full list of endorsements and quotes can be found here.

title: Rep. Min Joins Planned Parenthood Town Hall to Discuss  H.R. 1 Medicaid Cuts, Advocates for Quality and Affordable Healthcare
text:
Irvine, CA — Rep. Dave Min (CA-47) joined Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties, health care providers, and community leaders for a town hall examining the impact of H.R. 1 on healthcare access in Orange County. The discussion focused on the law’s cuts to federal Medicaid funding, its temporary prohibition on Medicaid reimbursements for services provided by Planned Parenthood health centers, and the barriers Orange County families may face in maintaining their health coverage.

“We knew that H.R. 1 would force Planned Parenthood health centers to close and force millions of Americans to go uninsured or see their health care costs skyrocket,” said Rep. They are real people who rely on Medicaid to make sure their families receive the health care they need. As we fight to reverse these attacks we must do all we can to make sure those still eligible for Medicaid can keep their healthcare.”

Rep. Min recently joined his colleagues in raising concerns with Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz about new Medicaid work-reporting requirements that could impose undue burdens on people with serious health needs and cause eligible enrollees to lose coverage. He also met with representatives from CalOptima Health to discuss its efforts to educate Orange County Medi-Cal recipients about the new requirements.

Panelists included Krista Hollinger, President and CEO of Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties; Dr. América Bracho, Founder and CEO of Latino Health Access; and Cevadne Lee, Director of Health and Policy at the Orange County Asian and Pacific Islander Community Alliance. title: CONGRESSMAN JOE MORELLE REINTRODUCES BILL TO KEEP KIDS FED AND LEARNING ALL SUMMER LONG
text:
(Rochester, N.Y.)—Today, Congressman Joe Morelle reintroduced the Summer Meals and Learning Act, legislation he authored to help children continue learning while ensuring they have access to nutritious meals during the summer months. The bill would establish a new federal grant program supporting reading programs at schools that serve as summer meal sites, helping students stay engaged academically even after the school year ends.

"Summer break should never mean a child falls behind in school or goes without a healthy meal," said Congressman Joe Morelle. "For too many families, that's exactly what's happening. This bill is a simple idea with a real impact: keep kids connected to books, keep school libraries open, and make sure they have healthy meals while they're there. I'm proud to partner with Senator Merkley once again to give more children the support they need to learn, grow, and succeed."

For many children, school provides far more than classroom instruction. It's where they can find books to read, adults who encourage them to keep learning, and dependable access to healthy meals. When summer arrives, too many of those supports disappear—especially in communities where families have fewer opportunities to fill the gap.

Research has shown the consequences can last well beyond the summer months. By fifth grade, students without access to summer learning opportunities can be as much as two years behind their peers.

The Summer Meals and Learning Act would establish a grant program through the U.S. Department of Education to help State libraries partner with schools on summer reading programs. Schools would qualify if they:

Operate a summer meal program; and

Serve student populations where at least 50 percent of children are reading below grade level or are at risk of reading below grade level.

By bringing books and meals together in one place, the legislation would help more children return to school in the fall healthy, engaged, and ready to learn.

To learn more about the Summer Meals and Learning Act, read the full text of the legislation here.

title: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Joins Legislation to Ban ICE from Using TSA Data
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) co-sponsored the No TSA Data for ICE Act, introduced by Rep. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), that would prevent the two agencies from coordinating to enforce the Trump administration’s mass deportation agenda. In a dramatic violation of privacy rights, the Transportation and Security Administration is sharing passenger names, birth dates, and other data with Immigration and Customs Enforcement, leading to a surge of arrests at airports. ICE agents are targeting immigrants in the process of changing status, including those waiting for visa extensions, with employment authorization documents, or recently married to a U.S. citizen.

A Freedom of Information Act lawsuit obtained an information-sharing agreement between TSA and ICE from May 2025, exposing that acting TSA Administrator Ha Nguyen McNeill lied in her testimony before Congress.

“TSA is complicit in ICE expanding its chaos and cruelty to target our communities in our airports and has been openly lying about it,” said Tlaib. “Through an information-sharing agreement signed in 2025, TSA is readily offering up our immigrant residents to suffer at the hands of ICE agents so they can fulfill their daily arrest quota. One source from ICE even said it makes for ‘easy targets’ at airports—a disgusting exploitation of immigrants in status limbo. Immigrants should be able to safely fly in this country without the fear of arrest or deportation.”

The bill would also prevent the Department of Homeland Security from retaliating against critics of ICE and the Trump Administration by revoking their status in trusted traveler programs, including TSA PreCheck and Global Entry. DHS is currently being sued by three U.S. citizens who lost Global Entry status after filming ICE activity.

“When people fly, they should be able to trust that TSA won’t divulge their sensitive information or use it for political retaliation,” said Tlaib. “TSA has broken that trust in a gross violation of people’s First Amendment rights. This data sharing should terrify all of us. It does nothing to make us safer, but rather endangers the basic rights of all Americans and worsens our mass surveillance crisis.”

Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) said:

“Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, the world’s busiest and most efficient airport, is the gateway to the world. That’s only possible when every traveler has confidence in our aviation system. The TSA should play no part in Trump’s and ICE’s terror campaign. It’s exploitative, dangerous, and a violation of people’s privacy. I’m proud to co-sponsor Rep. Tlaib’s No TSA Data for ICE Act to help protect people’s privacy, restore accountability, and ensure our government agencies are focused on keeping travelers safe—not serving as tools for ICE.”

The No TSA Data for ICE Act is cosponsored by 24 other members of Congress: U.S. Reps. Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), André Carson (IN-07), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Sylvia R. Nunn Secures $2 Million to Expand Des Moines River Access Through ICON Water Trails
text:
“Des Moines grew up around two rivers, and we haven’t done enough to make them part of how families experience our city,” said Rep. Nunn. “This $2 million builds the access at Birdland and Prospect Park that changes that — safer, easier ways down to the Des Moines River for the families, kayakers, and anglers who use it. A riverfront people actually use fills the restaurants, hotels, and shops around it, turning more visitors into more customers and more economic growth across Central Iowa.”

Rep. Nunn secured the funding through the FY2026 Community Project Funding (CPF) process. The award, funded through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s Economic Development Initiatives account, will support access improvements at both parks. The City of Des Moines will administer the dollars as part of the broader ICON Water Trails initiative.

The award funds public access and site improvements at both parks. The work will make it easier and safer to get to the water, improve the park space around each access point, and support the clean water and conservation priorities in the ICON plan.

The investment builds on more than $103 million that local, state, federal, philanthropic, and private partners have already committed to ICON Water Trails. The City of Des Moines alone has put more than $7 million into Birdland Park and $6 million into Prospect Park. Created in 2016, the initiative spans roughly 150 miles of central Iowa creeks and rivers.

In 2024, Rep. Nunn delivered $1 million for improvements at the Fleur Drive Dam, including dam remediation and new river access for kayakers and anglers. Today’s award brings his total to $3 million in Community Project Funding for the ICON network.

Local leaders praised the investment and its impact on the community.

“The Community Project Funding awarded to the City of Des Moines clearly illustrates how support from federal funding results in long-term economic growth for local governments,” said Mayor Connie Boesen. “With the $2 million award, the City of Des Moines will be able to work alongside ICON to make much-needed improvements to Birdland and Prospect Park, furthering the development of the water trails system. The water trails and new state-of-the-art features at both parks will draw tourism while bolstering the quality of life for our residents.”

“We are grateful to Congressman Nunn for his continued leadership and support of projects that expand access to outdoor recreation and improve quality of life across our region,” said Stephanie Oppel, Executive Director, ICON Water Trails. “Prospect Park will revitalize an important community space while serving as the future starting point of the Downtown Run, creating new opportunities for people to experience and enjoy the Des Moines River.”

“Investments in the ICON Water Trails network continue to build on one of Greater Des Moines’ defining competitive advantages: our quality of life,” said Tiffany Tauscheck, President & CEO, Greater Des Moines Partnership. “By enhancing access points like Birdland Marina and Prospect Park, we’re creating more opportunities for residents and visitors to experience all that our region has to offer. This investment reflects the power of partnership and the importance of continuing to advance projects that create lasting economic impact for our region.”

“Outdoor recreation is a growing driver of tourism,” said Trina Flack, President & CEO, Catch Des Moines. “These projects position Greater Des Moines as a premier destination for on-water and riverfront experiences while generating significant economic benefits for our local businesses.”

title: Congresswoman Ilhan Omar Demands Answers About the Presence of an Undercover HSI Agent Outside her Town Hall Meeting
text:
MINNEAPOLIS – Congresswoman Ilhan Omar (D-MN) sent an oversight letter to Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) demanding a response as to why an undercover HSI agent was stationed outside of her monthly town hall meeting in Richfield. Following nationwide concerns about the Trump Administration’s use of ICE and DHS to intimidate Americans who oppose their political agenda, this action raises serious concerns about the purpose of HSI’s presence at the Congresswoman’s public event.

It also raises concerns about practices at HSI and ICE more broadly. It calls into question the level of training agents are receiving before being sent out into the field, given the agent claimed to have been conducting an undercover criminal operation with no prior coordination with local law enforcement near the Congresswoman’s event. Importantly, it indicates that HSI is continuing to use mismatched license plates on vehicles, in violation of state law and in contradiction to earlier commitments HSI made to Rep. Omar.

“HSI's actions yesterday evening put an entire community at risk,” said Rep. Omar. “Instead of monitoring the area for those who might wish harm to me and my constituents, Richfield Police were required to devote time to investigating why an HSI agent was outside of a Congressional event in a vehicle with mismatched plates. It also raises serious and uncomfortable questions about the purpose of HSI's presence outside of my event. At best, your agent was unable to assess that the parking lot of a community center hosting a Congressional event wasn’t the best place to conduct a drug operation. At worst, it emphasizes many Americans’ growing concern that the Trump administration uses ICE to surveil political opponents and may interfere with our democracy.”

Congresswoman Omar is demanding answers to the following questions:

Please explain why an agent was detailed to Richfield Community Center on the evening of Thursday, August 6, 2026.

Please explain when and how the HSI agent and her supervisors became aware I was hosting a town hall at this location and what action that knowledge prompted.

Please provide an overview of the training the agent had completed prior to her assignment at this location, as well as how long she has served as an HSI agent.

Richfield Police Department reported that they had received no advance communication of an undercover operation from HSI that would have allowed them to ensure the safety of the officer and the community, as well as support HSI's broader work to combat drug trafficking. Please explain what steps you take to coordinate undercover criminal operations with local law enforcement, and why in this instance there was no prior coordination with Richfield Police Department.

Please share details of any meetings or events I have hosted in my official capacity as a Member of Congress that HSI agents may have been assigned to observe and why. Please share whether HSI agents have observed any other activity being undertaken in an official capacity by any other local, state, or federal officials in Minnesota this year.

title: Pallone, NJ Delegation Urge Approval of New Jersey’s Appeal for Federal Disaster Assistance After Initial Request Was Denied
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Frank Pallone, Jr. (NJ-06) joined members of the New Jersey congressional delegation in urging President Donald J. Trump to approve Governor Mikie Sherrill’s appeal of FEMA’s denial of the State’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration following the devastating February 22–23, 2026, winter storm. New Jersey submitted its original request for federal disaster assistance on April 7, 2026, and FEMA denied that request on July 2, 2026.

“According to data from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, approximately 24 inches of snow fell in less than 24 hours across eastern and central New Jersey, and eight of the State’s 21 counties recorded record or near-record snowfall totals and qualify as ‘core counties’ as laid out by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) in the Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG). Another four counties met the ‘contiguous county’ requirements for snow assistance outlined in the PAPPG,” wrote the lawmakers.

The lawmakers’ latest appeal follows a bipartisan April 21 letter from the delegation pressing the Administration to approve the State’s initial request, citing the storm’s deadly impacts, widespread outages affecting more than 127,000 customers, hundreds of accidents, and nearly $100 million in statewide damages. The February storm claimed 12 lives across nine counties, caused extensive power outages, and inflicted significant damage to homes, businesses, and critical infrastructure—costs that New Jerseyans should not be forced to shoulder alone.

Preliminary damage assessments for Public Assistance teams documented significant emergency work and damage to public facilities and infrastructure across 19 counties. The storm further strained New Jersey’s emergency response capacity, which was already stretched after the State responded to a major snow and ice storm just weeks earlier and managed six active federal disaster declarations.

“A careful review of the State of New Jersey’s appeal demonstrates that this request far exceeds all Stafford Act statutory and regulatory thresholds. The extent of the damage, the operational burden throughout the State, and the cumulative impacts of recent and related extreme weather all provide overwhelming evidence that New Jersey’s request must be granted,” wrote the lawmakers.

In addition to Pallone, the letter was signed by Senators Booker and Kim, New Jersey U.S. Representatives Donald Norcross (D-NJ-1), Herb Conaway Jr. (D-NJ-3), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5), Robert Menendez (D-NJ-8), Nellie Pou (D-NJ-9), LaMonica McIver (D-NJ-10), Analilia Mejia (D-NJ-11), and Bonnie Watson Coleman (D-NJ-12).

title: Rep. Panetta, Local Leaders Stand United at  Monterey Bay Aquarium Against Offshore Oil  and Gas Drilling on the Central Coast
text:
Monterey, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) convened local officials, environmental advocates, and business leaders at the Monterey Bay Aquarium to reaffirm their united opposition to the Administration’s proposal to expand offshore oil and gas leasing. Rep. Panetta and local leaders highlighted the potential threats that offshore drilling poses to the marine environment, coastal economy, and communities on California’s Central Coast.

The Administration’s current Draft Proposed Program includes 34 potential lease sales nationwide, including two in the Central California Planning Area in 2027 and 2029. Rep. Panetta encouraged Central Coast residents and stakeholders to remain engaged when the Administration releases the next version of the proposal, which will be subject to a required 90-day public comment period.

“When it comes to protecting our coastline from offshore oil and gas drilling, we must stand united in the face of the chaos or craziness coming out of this Administration,” said Rep. Panetta. “We stand here as stewards of our ocean as we stand for an economy and a community built on our beauty and our bounty. When the Administration releases its updated plan for public comment, we must make our voices heard, stay united, and stand ready to go toe-to-toe for our coastline and our way of life in California’s 19th Congressional District.”

The waters off the Central Coast support one of the most biologically diverse marine ecosystems in the world, as well as vibrant hospitality, tourism, recreation, fishing, and other coastal industries. Local officials, environmental advocates, and business leaders emphasized that the region’s economy and identity depend on a healthy coastline and that expanded offshore drilling would put both at risk.

“California is a leader in the protection of the ocean, this community has worked tirelessly to make sure we’re keeping the coastline safe so that kids growing up here know they can live in an environment with whales and dolphins and sea otters. That doesn’t happen by chance, now is an important time to come together for the health of the beautiful Monterey Bay, our ocean and its amazing marine life, and our thriving coastal communities,” said Dr. Jenny Gray, Chief Executive Officer, Monterey Bay Aquarium.

“Drilling for oil and gas off the Central Coast is reckless, unnecessary, and out of step with our community’s values. We should be investing in the future of our coastline—not putting the Monterey Bay, our economy, and our way of life at risk. From repairing Wharf 2 to preparing for sea level rise, we have real infrastructure challenges that demand our attention and investment. I’m proud that our community is standing together to protect the Monterey Bay for generations to come,” said Tyller Williamson, Mayor, City of Monterey.

“The Central Coast has a long history of standing up to offshore oil drilling, and that fight continues today. Community members, environmental organizations, businesses, and elected leaders are once again coming together to protect the coast from new drilling threats,” said Katie Thompson, Executive Director, Save Our Shores.

Rep. Panetta has worked throughout the federal planning process to organize and amplify the Central Coast’s opposition to offshore drilling. Following the leak of the Administration’s draft proposal in October 2025, he joined several of his colleagues in calling on the Administration to halt its plans to drill along the California coastline. In February 2026, he convened local community and environmental leaders to discuss ways to oppose the proposal and protect the Central Coast. Rep. Panetta also mobilized constituents throughout the 19th Congressional District and hosted a telephone town hall during the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management’s (BOEM) first public comment period to help residents submit comments opposing the Administration’s leasing plan.

Rep. Panetta also continues to carefully monitor the Administration’s involvement in oil drilling off California’s coast. In 2019, after the Trump Administration’s first attempt to open up oil drilling on the Central Coast, he introduced the Central Coast of California Conservation Act to prevent new leasing for the exploration, development, or production of oil or natural gas in the Central California Planning Area, spanning the entire coastline of California’s 19th Congressional District. He also led his colleagues in a multistate effort to ban offshore drilling along thousands of miles of U.S. coastline, citing the negative impacts of oil-related disasters and accidents on climate change and natural ecosystems.

title: PASSED OUT OF COMMITTEE: Pappas’s Bipartisan Bill to Honor Fallen Law Enforcement, Strengthen Officer Safety
text:
The National Law Enforcement Remembrance, Support, and Community Outreach Act, introduced byCongressman Chris Pappas (NH-01), Congressman Troy E. Nehls (TX-22), and Congressman Jimmy Panetta (D-CA-19), passed out of the House Committee on Natural Resources.

This bipartisan legislation would establish a formal program within the U.S. Department of Interior (DOI) to support and enhance the community outreach, public education and officer safety and wellness programs of the National Law Enforcement Museum through grants to the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Fund (NLEOMF). These programs would memorialize and honor law enforcement, compile data on law enforcement fatalities and injuries, increase public understanding of and support for law enforcement, enhance and improve law enforcement officer safety and wellness, and bring law enforcement closer to the communities they serve.

“Every day our law enforcement answers the call to serve and keep our communities safe, putting their lives on the line to do so. We must always support their critical work and honor those that give the ultimate sacrifice,” said Congressman Pappas. “This bipartisan legislation would support efforts to honor law enforcement officers killed in the line of duty, commemorate their legacies of service and sacrifice, and strengthen officer safety and wellbeing. I remain committed to supporting our law enforcement and the important work they do for Granite Staters.”

The National Law Enforcement Remembrance, Support and Community Outreach Act is supported by NLEMOF’s board member organizations, including the Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association, Fraternal Order of Police, Fraternal Order of Police Auxiliary, International Brotherhood of Police Officers, International Union of Police Associations/AFL-CIO, Motorola Solutions, Verizon, National Association of Police Organizations, National Sheriffs’ Associations, COPS, DuPont, National Black Police Association, National Organization of Black Law Enforcement Executives, National Policing Institute, National Troopers Coalition, Police Executive Research Forum, Police Unity Tour, and the United Federation of Police Officers.

Created by an Act of Congress in 1984, NLEOMF operates the National Law Enforcement Museum and the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial. NLEOMF’s mission is to honor fallen law enforcement officers, tell the story of our nation’s law enforcement officers, and make it safer for law enforcement.

title: Amata Leads Foreign Affairs CODEL to Colombia Presidential Inauguration, City Struck by Devastating Earthquake After Departure
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Uifa’atali Amata, traveling at the request of the House Foreign Affairs Committee (HFAC), led the Radewagen CODEL with Ranking Member Gregory Meeks (D-NY) over the weekend to Colombia for the new President’s inauguration, ensuring that the Committee was appropriately represented there.

Congresswoman Amata and Ranking Member Meeks at the ceremonies in Colombia

Just hours after their arrival back in Washington, D.C., that region of Colombia was struck by a major 7.4 magnitude earthquake, causing many injuries, 111 deaths as of the early news reports, and the destruction of at least 20 buildings just in Cali alone.

“My deepest condolences to the people of Colombia as they mourn, rescue and then face the long recovery effort from this severe disaster,” said Congresswoman Amata. “It’s a shock to see them go from their welcoming greetings to us and their celebratory occasion just a day before, to this major natural disaster and loss of life. They will need prayer and support.”

Congresswoman Amata and Congressman Meeks attended the inauguration of President Abelardo de la Espriella in the city of Cali, near the Pacific coast in the western part of the country. Congressman Meeks is the Committee’s Democratic leader, who has built seniority, serving since 1998, and is on track to be Dean of the New York House delegation in 2027. Also in attendance were other U.S. officials including newly confirmed Attorney General Todd Blanche, who was officially sworn in Monday after the trip.

Inauguration in Colombia

“Colombia is a $50 billion trade partner with the United States, as they import U.S. refined oil and corn, and export coffee and crude oil,” said Congresswoman Amata. “They are part of the Pacific Alliance economic integration, and as a Pacific coastal country, are located at one edge of the vast Indo-Pacific region that is essential to U.S. and worldwide commercial and security measures.”

While there, Congresswoman Amata took part in a roundtable with Mayor of Cali Alejandro Eder, and the Civil Society at the Universidad Santiago de Cali, where she gave a statement.

Amata’s Remarks in Colombia

Talofa lava and good morning to you all. Thank you, Mr. Mayor, for graciously hosting us in your beautiful city of Cali.

My name is Aumua Amata Coleman Radewagen, Congresswoman in the U.S. House of Representatives.

I’m proud to represent my home of American Samoa, a beautiful group of seven islands in the Pacific Ocean.

Many people do not know that, just like Colombia, the United States of America stretches into the Southern Hemisphere. American Samoa is in fact the only American soil south of the equator.

Our two countries share something else in common, as well. Both the USA and Colombia have long and proud histories of democratic institutions, constitutional government, and peaceful transfers of power.

This shared commitment is a large part of why Congress considers Colombia to be one of our closest Latin American allies—if not the closest.

It is such a deep honor to visit Colombia on the special occasion of the Presidential Inauguration—alongside my colleague and good friend Gregory Meeks, the Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

I want to congratulate President De La Espriella and his administration on his election and inauguration.

And I want to express my sincere congratulations for the successful exercise of your democratic rights. Colombia’s long and notable tradition of republican self-government continues!

When a new government is sworn in, as we had the pleasure of witnessing yesterday, it heralds a promising new opportunity for our countries to work together on shared challenges.

Perhaps the most important shared challenge the U.S. and Colombia face is, of course, on the security front.

We know Colombia is facing a difficult moment, where violence caused by armed drug trafficking organizations and terrorist groups continues to take the lives of innocent people. This concerns us greatly. Our heart goes out to you.

And this is not only a problem for Colombia or for the region. Rather, it is directly linked to the United States—because every year tens of thousands of Americans die of cocaine overdoses.

This is a deep tragedy for both countries. And it has served as the basis for our incredibly close security cooperation since the 1990s.

Although the previous administration had at times a turbulent relationship with the United States, the strong institutional ties between our two nations endured.

In January, the U.S. Congress enacted a foreign assistance bill, which contained nearly 200 million dollars earmarked solely for Colombia. Much of this will go toward building up Colombia’s security forces to better combat the armed groups who profit off illegal drug trafficking.

There is still much we can do is to improve our security coordination—not only at the national level, but also especially at the sub-national level. Mayors and municipal leaders like yourselves are on the very front lines. You know best what the solutions are to your security challenges.

As this distinguished group knows well, firm government action against criminals and armed organizations is necessary, but so too is the critical work of civil society.

This includes alleviating poverty, creating economic opportunity for those in need, conducting prevention programs for youths that are at risk of gang recruitment, and ensuring the human rights of all Colombians are protected.

These are essential things. I commend your good work on this front. The United States stands ready to help. A large portion of our foreign assistance to Colombia is designated for just this—in particular, for Indigenous and Afro-descendent communities whose regions are often suffering the brunt of criminal violence.

Before I close, let me mention another shared challenge. For the first time in a long time, Venezuela stands on the precipice of a new prosperity future. If our two countries work together, I fully believe that we can help Venezuela achieve a true transition to democracy and prosperity.

This would benefit not only the millions of Venezuelans residing in this country, which Colombia has so generously welcomed in, but the entire region.

Like Colombia, the United States can be very politically polarized. But as you can see by the bipartisan nature of this Congressional Delegation, both Republicans and Democrats in Congress place a very high value on the U.S.-Colombia relationship.

It is a relationship that has lasted two centuries. May it continue to prosper for another 200 years!

Thank you, or as we say in American Samoa, Fa’afetai tele lava. May God bless America, and may God bless the Republic of Colombia.

title: Amata Welcomes Senate Passage of Government Funding Extension
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Uifa’atali Amata is welcoming Senate passage of a government funding extension bill to keep the federal government open when the fiscal year ends at midnight after September 30. The Senate’s version, passed 90-6, would fund the government across the board at current rates until December 11, one week longer than the House version, which was passed in late July.

Congresswoman Amata pictured recently recording remarks

“Senate passage with a large bipartisan vote is good news, and I am optimistic Congress can avoid a shutdown,” said Congresswoman Aumua Amata. “I appreciate the major effort that went into writing and passing both bills, and I support prompt final passage of a bill to prevent a shutdown, which is the highest priority for a short-term extension.”

Amata continued, “I also strongly support passage of full-year appropriations for 2027 to lock in two of my requests for next year that are already in the bill – $1 million additional for our American Samoa operations through OIA, and $1 million for port infrastructure that I supported along with Governor Pulaali’i and Director Barney Sene.”

The December extension still requires final passage of a compromise reconciling the two bills, or for either house to take up the other house’s bill. Both versions of the extension continue current funding until December, allowing more work on 2027 appropriations. The House has completed committee work on all 12 appropriations bills, but bicameral passage of all 12 will not be completed before the September 30 deadline.

Congresswoman Amata has voiced support for a recent House Appropriations Committee hearing focused on much-needed possible reforms to prevent shutdowns or make them uncommon in the future by examining procedural improvements.

title: Ramirez, Casar Lead Call For Congressional Hearings With AI CEOs
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Congresswoman Delia C. Ramirez (Il-03), Ranking Member of the House Homeland Security Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection, and Congressman Greg Casar (D-TX) led 17 members of Congress calling on Speaker Mike Johnson (LA-04) to immediately schedule open hearings with the CEOs of America’s largest AI companies.

In a letter to Johnson, the members wrote: “Advanced AI models pose a clear risk to the safety and security of the American people. [...] At the same time, Artificial Intelligence threatens to displace millions of American workers. [...] Unfortunately, Congress has so far completely failed to respond to the threats posed by AI development. That must change. The CEOs of the largest AI companies should answer questions under oath, and Americans should have a chance to hear from independent experts on the dangers posed by this technology. We urge you to work with the committees of jurisdiction to schedule hearings immediately.”

The letter comes on the heels of leading AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta, announcing that their models escaped test environments to hack other organizations. The members write: “The American people deserve clear answers about the causes of these incidents, what failures or potential negligence at the companies led to them, and the types of regulation required to make sure they never happen again,” the letter says.

The letter is cosigned by U.S. Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Becca Balint (VT-AL), Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Jesús G. "Chuy" García (IL-04), Sylvia R. Garcia (TX-29), Adelita S. Grijalva (AZ-07), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), April McClain Delaney (MD-06), Valerie P. Foushee (NC-04), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Summer L. Lee (PA-12), Stephen F. Lynch (MA-08), Jennifer L. McClellan (VA-04), James P. McGovern (MA-02), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), and Nydia M. Velázquez (NY-07)
