title: RELEASE: After Attacks in Jersey, Gottheimer Announces Bipartisan Federal Actions to Protect Water, Electric Systems, and Families from Cyber Attacks
text:
Above: Gottheimer announces federal action to defend critical infrastructure.

PARK RIDGE, NJ — Today, Wednesday, August 12, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) announced his bipartisan Critical Infrastructure Security Plan, a package of federal actions to bolster American critical infrastructure following a wave of attacks that targeted New Jersey municipal water systems and others in at least a dozen states across the country.

Watch Gottheimer’s full remarks here.

“Every morning, folks in this town wake up, turn on the faucet, and clean water comes out. You flip a switch and your lights come on. Nobody thinks twice about it. Nobody should have to,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “I’m standing here because in towns just like this one, all over the country, that deal we have with our utility companies has been put in real jeopardy, and if we don’t get out ahead of it, it could mean a disaster.”

Over the past two weeks, hackers have targeted water systems in New Jersey and at least a dozen other states. In Cape May County, two municipal systems were hit, forcing operators to manually turn valves and run pumps after the digital controls they rely on every day were wrenched away from them. The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is investigating incidents in at least seven states, and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), and the FBI issued a joint advisory urging the entire water sector to immediately lock down its systems. Investigators have pointed to Iranian-affiliated actors, while examining whether other adversaries are copying the same playbook.

There are roughly 150,000 public water systems in the country, and 97 percent of them serve small communities such as Park Ridge, often with just a handful of employees and no full-time cybersecurity team. Many were built decades ago for reliability, not for cybersecurity, leaving older controllers and outdated software exposed to anyone who knows where to look.

Gottheimer announced three federal actions to close that gap:

The bipartisan AI Cyber Defense Act, which he is introducing with Rep. Don Bacon (NE-2), Rep. Zach Nunn (IA-3), Rep. Hilary Scholten (MI-3), and Rep. Greg Landsman (OH-1) would give America’s critical infrastructure operators free access to the most powerful, cyber-capable AI models. Today those tools are mostly used by the people trying to break in, not the people trying to keep them out. The bill would let a small water utility in New Jersey use the same caliber of AI a foreign intelligence agency might deploy against it, and turn it around to find the open door before an adversary does and patch the vulnerability before it becomes a headline.

The bipartisan Securing Our Critical Infrastructure Act, which he is introducing with Rep. Don Bacon (NE-2), Rep. Zach Nunn (IA-3), Rep. Hilary Scholten (MI-3), and Rep. Greg Landsman (OH-1) would create a dedicated rapid-response and threat notification service at CISA, built specifically for small and medium water and electric utilities. It would establish one clear point of contact to notify utilities the moment there is an active threat and give real support for the most resource-constrained systems.

Gottheimer is also sending a letter to CISA, the EPA, and the FBI demanding they immediately surge incident response teams and technical assistance to every water and wastewater utility hit by this campaign, especially the small and rural systems that can least afford to go dark. The letter also calls on the agencies to build lasting protection for the water sector, including guidance specific to water systems and a standing rapid-response framework, before the next campaign hits.

Gottheimer was joined by New Jersey Cybersecurity and Communications Integration Cell (NJCCIC) Director Michael Geraghty, Bergen County Prosecutor Mark Musella, Bergen County Chief of Detectives Jeff Angermeyer, Senator Holly Schepisi (R-District 39), Park Ridge Mayor Keith Misciagna, Park Ridge Councilman Will Fenwick, and Park Ridge Councilman Bruce Goldsmith.

Below: Gottheimer announces federal action to defend critical infrastructure.

Gottheimer’s remarks as prepared for delivery:

Thank you to everyone here with us. I’m grateful for all of your work on the ground to protect our essential services.

Thank you all for being here in Park Ridge, right in front of the tanks that serve drinking water to Park Ridge and nearby Woodcliff Lake.

I’ve stood right here before when we announced steps the Park Ridge Water Department was taking to get lead and PFAS out of their drinking water. Today, we are here to discuss a different, looming, and potent threat to this critical infrastructure system, and ones like it across our state and country — cyber terrorism. I’m talking about cyber attacks like the ones in South Jersey two weeks ago and those who attempt to infiltrate our water, electric, and other essential systems — what we call our critical infrastructure — every day in America.

With the explosion and advancement of AI, those threats have become even more common and deadly, and, unfortunately, far too easy to access for those who seek to do us harm. Enemies like Iran, Russia, and China.

I’m not here to scare you. As a Member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on National Security Agency and Cyber, I want us all to be aware of, and prepared for, this reality that we are facing here at home.

Today, I am proud to announce my Critical Infrastructure Security Plan — to give towns, counties, and states the tools they need to protect our families and the water, electric, and other critical infrastructure systems that they rely on from cyber attacks.

Every morning, folks in this town wake up, turn on the faucet, and clean water comes out. You flip a switch and your lights come on. Nobody thinks twice about it. Nobody should have to. That’s the deal. You pay your water bill, the water shows up. You pay your electric bill, your power works.

Unfortunately, those bills are too expensive these days, but that’s a separate issue. I’m standing here because in towns just like this one, all over the country, that deal we have with our utility companies has been put in real jeopardy, and if we don’t get out ahead of it, it could mean a disaster.

Picture this: you wake up tomorrow, you go to make the coffee or take a shower before work, and nothing comes out of the tap. Or, you flip on the lights, and the power just isn’t there. Imagine that across a major city. No power to hospitals, businesses, schools, or our homes.

That’s not some doomsday scenario I’m cooking up. That is what almost happened to Jersey families just two weeks ago.

Here’s what’s actually going on. For the past two weeks, water systems across this country have been under attack. Not “could happen someday.” It’s happening right now, as we’re standing here.

It started in Minnesota in late July, when hackers hit roughly thirty water systems in a single 48-hour window. Then it spread to Michigan, New Jersey, Minnesota, Georgia, South Dakota, and five other states.

The FBI is investigating these incidents right now, and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, or CISA, the FBI, and the EPA had to put out a joint advisory telling the entire water sector to immediately lock down its systems.

In the same campaign, two municipal water systems in Cape May County, the City of Cape May and the Borough of Woodbine, got hit. The attack limited their operators’ ability to monitor and manage their own equipment. Real people, Jersey families, could have lost water service — which could mean no clean drinking water or fire hydrants running dry in an emergency.

Staff had to run out into the field and turn valves and run pumps manually because the digital controls they rely on every single day had been hacked — their control had been wrenched away from them. Although our power systems weren’t impacted in this attack, many of our energy and power grid sectors utilize the same hardware and remote management protocols that were compromised.

Thankfully, both Jersey towns got things hardened and back under control fast, working with the state’s cyber team and our federal partners, and service was not interrupted this time.

But let’s not kid ourselves and call that luck. That was a warning for us all, and we can’t just sit here and wait for the next attack. Because, by the way, Minnesota wasn’t so lucky — the city of Braham [BRAM] had to shut down its well and water treatment plant for several hours.

In 2023, a Chinese state-sponsored actor named Volt Typhoon hacked into a small municipal utility in Massachusetts that serves 15,000 people and infiltrated its systems for nine months, waiting for the right time to sabotage it. In 2015, Russia hit an electric utility in Ukraine, cutting power to 225,000 consumers.

A 2023 cyberattack in Aliquippa, Pennsylvania targeted the same systemsthat were attacked this summer and resulted in the operators needing to temporarily halt pumping. And a 2024 Muleshoe, Texas attack saw the pumps turned on — out of the operators control — and caused the tank water level to overflow.

Let’s be straight about who led this latest twelve state attack on our country. Reporting and government advisories have linked the cyber attacks to Iranian-affiliated actors, though officials are also looking into whether our other enemies are involved. This isn’t some kid in a basement messing around.

According to public reporting, this is potentially an enemy of our country, using state-backed hackers, testing whether they can reach out and shut off the water and power to American families, hospitals, farmers, and emergency services.

This also isn’t an isolated incident. Over the last few years, attackers have targeted — albeit unsuccessfully — water systems and other critical infrastructure in California, Florida, Maine, Nevada, Kansas, and right here in New Jersey, where an undisclosed water system detected ransomware in its systems in 2020.

And, they’ll keep trying, especially with the latest AI frontier models — they make it even easier to launch cyber attacks.

Foreign governments now have access to powerful AI tools that can scan the internet, find potentially weaker utility systems, hand adversaries a target list, and help them exploit the vulnerabilities in our systems. The same technology that can help a small town’s IT guy find and patch a gap in security can help a hostile government find a hundred more it hasn’t even discovered yet. AI didn’t create this threat, but it is accelerating it, and our defenses have to keep up. And it’s only getting easier for them.

In these latest attacks in our state and across the country, the hackers found pumps and treatment equipment plugged directly into the internet; they logged in, and locked the real operators out. It worked because a lot of our water systems, especially the smaller ones, were built decades ago and not exactly with the most sophisticated systems to protect against cybersecurity. Many of these controllers have little to no built-in protections and run on outdated software. In other words, they’re sitting wide open, vulnerable to anybody who knows where to look.

Now, systems like Park Ridge aren’t sitting on the internet – they operate offline, on their own closed system, making them less vulnerable to these types of cyber attacks. But, many of our smaller systems are sitting right in the bullseye. And, we have a lot of critical infrastructure systems out there.

There are roughly 150,000 public water systems in this country, and 97 percent of them serve small and mid-sized communities, just like here in Park Ridge. New Jersey itself has more than 600 community water systems that provide drinking water to approximately 87 percent of the state’s population.

Nationwide, there are more than 900 rural electric cooperatives and 2,000 publicly owned utilities that deliver electricity to almost 100 million Americans. These are systems with a handful of employees, limited cybersecurity resources, and vulnerable systems.

Believe it or not, CISA found that more than 1 in 10 water systems have a critical cybersecurity vulnerability, and more than 80 percent of those vulnerabilities included software flaws discovered before 2017.

CISA’s work is absolutely critical to identifying and combating these threats, but the Trump administration has been slashing it to the bone. Since Trump took office, it’s lost almost a third of its workforce, had their budget cut by $134 million, and the Administration has announced plans to cut another $700 million in the coming year and an additional 860 staff.

The North American Electric Reliability Corporation has identified similar weaknesses — the number of vulnerabilities hackers could exploit is rising by roughly 60 per day. If this isn’t a screeching red alarm, I don’t know what is.

I should add, when I say critical infrastructure, I’m not just talking about water or energy systems. In 2023, a ransomware attack forced two New Jersey hospitals — Hackensack Meridian Mountainside Medical Center and Hackensack Meridian Pascack Valley Medical Center — to temporarily divert ambulances and reschedule elective procedures.

The systems took weeks to restore and affected thousands of patients.

Here’s the part that should worry you the most: this isn’t just a big-city problem with big-city budgets and full-time cybersecurity teams standing guard. Right now, federal funding for critical infrastructure cybersecurity has an uncertain future, and it has to compete for scraps against other infrastructure priorities. That’s not fair to the people running these systems on a shoestring budget, and it’s definitely not safe for the families here in Jersey depending on them.

That’s why today, as part of my Critical Infrastructure Security Plan, I’m announcing three bipartisan federal actions with Congressman Don Bacon of Nebraska, Congressman Zach Nunn of Iowa, and Congressman Greg Landsman of Ohio.

First, I’m introducing the bipartisan AI Cyber Defense Act. This new bipartisan legislation will give America’s critical infrastructure operators free access to their most powerful, cyber-capable AI models to secure their systems. Right now, those tools exist. They’re being used, but they’re often way too expensive for these small towns and facilities to afford what they really need.

This bill will provide that funding, allowing a small water utility or power station, like ones right here in Bergen County, to use the same caliber of AI a foreign intelligence agency might use against them. With those resources, the facilities can take this cutting-edge technology and turn it around to secure their own systems first. They’ll find the open door and lock it before someone tries to break in. They’ll patch the vulnerability before it ever becomes a headline. This is about getting our defense to catch up to their offense, and making it free for the towns that need it most.

A resource-constrained public works department in rural New Jersey should never have to outbid a nation-state just to protect itself. This bill will support the efforts of companies like Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google to get these powerful tools in the hands of those who need it most.

Second, I’m introducing the bipartisan Securing Our Critical Infrastructure Act. This new bipartisan bill will create a dedicated rapid response and threat notification service at CISA, specifically for small and medium-sized water and electric utilities.

Right now, if you’re a small town utility and something looks wrong on your network, you might not have anyone to call, or you might not even know who to call in the first place. This commonsense legislation creates one clear point of contact within the federal government that will notify these utilities the moment there’s an active threat or a sign that someone’s already inside their systems, with extra support built in for the utilities that are stretched the thinnest. It will also give them a clear point of contact, so they’re not running around trying to figure out who to call.

Third and finally, I’m sending a letter to CISA, the EPA, and the FBI demanding they immediately surge incident response teams and technical assistance to every water and wastewater utility hit by this campaign, including here in Jersey, especially the small and rural systems that can least afford to go dark. But, I’m not just asking for a band-aid. I am also urging these agencies to build real, lasting protection for the water and energy sectors, including guidance specific to water and electric systems and a standing rapid-response framework, so that before the next campaign hits — because there will be a next one — our utilities are prepared.

My cybersecurity package works together to protect our towns and families. The legislation gives our utilities the tools to find their own weaknesses before an adversary does. The rapid response service makes sure small towns aren’t fighting this alone. And, the federal surge makes sure the agencies whose job this is actually show up when it matters. There is nothing partisan about it. It’s about as red, white, and blue as it gets.

We also need to make sure our states have the resources to support our local systems. That’s why I’m calling on the Senate to pass the PILLAR Act, which I was proud to have helped pass through the House. This critical piece of legislation will reauthorize the State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program through 2033. These are dollars that towns can request and receive to build out and strengthen their existing cybersecurity systems. Unfortunately, this critical program has not received new funding in more than a year, and it’s putting our local utilities at risk.

I’m also supporting efforts in the Senate to pass legislation to reauthorize the Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity program, which I also helped pass through the House, which directly helps rural electric cooperatives and municipal utilities strengthen their cybersecurity defenses. I’m also proud to have helped move the SECURE Grid Act through the House, which would ensure states are fully prepared to prevent and respond to the risks posed to the electric grid by cyberattacks, extreme weather, natural disasters, and other threats.

We can’t afford to leave our state and local governments out to dry — we must instead empower our local leaders, like the New Jersey Cybersecurity and Communications Integration Cell, to help operators harden their systems.

Finally, the cyber attacks over the last weeks must be a wake up call to every utility – water, power, or otherwise — that’s part of our critical infrastructure. Park Ridge’s systems weren’t hit in this attack. But, in a rare move, the town hasn’t waited around to get lucky. Over the past year, on their own initiative, they’ve been upgrading their systems to put in place stronger protections and give better oversight.

Water and power systems across the country need to follow suit and implement tamper-resistant controls, update and patch systems as soon as they are able, build end-to-end encryption, use secure networks, create authentication and access control procedures, test their systems regularly, and train their employees. But, I recognize that it’s not easy — it’s expensive — and they need our help. That’s what the actions I’m taking today are all about. They need the federal support behind them to actually make it happen.

Again, keeping the water running and the lights on isn’t a Democratic issue or a Republican issue. It’s the most basic American obligation we have to the people we serve, and it should never, ever be partisan. When a parent in Park Ridge turns on their kitchen faucet, she doesn’t care which party controls Congress. They just want clean water to come out.

We caught this attack. And, I know that if we take the right action, we can get ahead of this. But, if we sit on our hands, we might not be so lucky next time. But, I’m confident that when we invest in the people protecting our infrastructure, and give them modern tools instead of asking them to fight modern threats with yesterday’s equipment, we will win.

If we keep working together to protect our friends and neighbors, in the greatest country in the world, I know that our best days will always be ahead of us. Thank you, God bless you, and may God continue to watch over and bless the United States of America.

title: Grothman Leads Entire Bipartisan Wisconsin Delegation in Urging FEMA to Assess Fox Valley Tornado Damage
text:
Congressman Glenn Grothman (R-WI) led the entire bipartisan Wisconsin Congressional delegation in support of Wisconsin’s request that the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) conduct a Joint Preliminary Damage Assessment (PDA) with Wisconsin Emergency Management following the devastating EF3 tornado that struck the Fox Valley on July 27.

The tornado caused widespread destruction across Appleton, Menasha, Neenah, and Fox Crossing. It remained on the ground for more than 20 minutes, traveled approximately 12 miles, reached nearly one mile in width, and produced estimated winds of 136 to 165 miles per hour. More than 30,000 homes and businesses lost power.

The members wrote, “The tornado ripped roofs from homes and businesses, hollowed out houses, reduced some structures to little more than their exterior walls, overturned vehicles, snapped trees, and brought down utility poles and power lines. Debris was scattered across neighborhoods and highways, roadways became impassable, families were displaced, and more than 30,000 homes and businesses lost power.”

The Members emphasized the importance of a timely assessment, writing, “Conducting a timely Joint Preliminary Damage Assessment is an essential first step in securing the federal support needed to help affected families, local governments, and communities recover and rebuild.”

The letter urged FEMA to “begin work in partnership with Wisconsin Emergency Management as soon as possible so that this process can move forward without delay.”

Governor Evers has declared a state of emergency, while Neenah, Menasha, and the Town of Grand Chute have issued local emergency or disaster declarations.

title: Congressman Rogers, State Leaders Deliver Over $30 Million for Infrastructure Projects in Eastern Kentucky
text:
HAZARD, KY – U.S. Rep. Harold “Hal” Rogers (KY-05) joined state and local leaders at Hazard Community and Technical College on Wednesday to deliver more than $30 million in federal funding for infrastructure projects in nine counties across southeastern Kentucky.

Congressman Rogers secured the federal funding for four of the projects through the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Section 531 Infrastructure Program. He created the funding source in 1996 to improve access to clean water and reliable wastewater resources exclusively in Kentucky’s Fifth Congressional District.

“This funding is the first step to job creation, economic development, flood recovery and even educational opportunities. Clean water and wastewater systems are the cornerstones that we build from in our communities,” said Congressman Rogers, a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee. “Infrastructure in the mountains comes with a hefty price tag, and this funding will help relieve the burden from our rural counties as they continue to revitalize and rebuild after the 2022 flood. I’m also thankful for the strong partnership with our state leaders who have secured match money and additional funds to make our region stronger.”

Congressman Rogers secured federal funding for five of the projects through the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Rural Development and the Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) to strengthen the infrastructure in Eastern Kentucky, particularly where communities continue to rebuild after the devastating flood in July 2022.

“Water infrastructure is so important to rural Kentuckians, and it’s a priority for this administration. Today’s announcements mark the latest investments we’ve made to help Eastern Kentucky rebuild after the horrific flooding of 2022,” said Travis Burton, State Director for USDA Rural Development. “Thanks to the leadership of President Trump and Secretary Rollins, we will continue working with water systems on projects big and small that will improve the quality of life and economic prosperity in rural Kentucky.”

Kentucky Senate President Robert Stivers and State Senator Scott Madon also delivered state funding for three infrastructure projects in Letcher County.

“I can’t emphasize the importance of the having this partnership between the federal, state and local levels enough. We have been able to match federal money with state funds for some of these projects to ensure they make it over the finish line,” said Sen. Stivers. “Our mountain communities are stronger today, thanks to the continued support of Congressman Rogers and his willingness to work with us on projects that strengthen our entire region.”

“This funding is a game changer for southeastern Kentucky, and I was proud to help secure state funding for three projects in Letcher County to advance job creation, tourism and economic development,” said Sen. Madon. "When we need help moving projects forward in southeastern Kentucky, we know we can always count on Congressman Rogers to get the job done at the federal level."

The funding delivered, includes:

$1 million for Morehead State University’s Sewer and Water Rehabilitation Project – Phase I: The U.S. Army Corps project will repair the entire system, serving 8,000 students and 800 faculty and staff, on and off campus.

$3 million for the Elliott County Fiscal Court’s Water Tower Project: The U.S. Army Corps project includes a 2.5 million gallon water tower for the Little Sandy Correctional Facility.

$900,000 for Elkhorn City’s Stillhouse Water Storage Tank in Pike County: The U.S. Army Corps project includes a new water tank with greater capacity to serve 500 homes and 35 businesses in Elkhorn City.

$2 million for the City of Jenkins’ Wastewater Treatment Plant Expansion: The U.S. Army Corps project will increase capacity to support 115 new homes and up to eight new businesses. It will also improve reliable service for more than 600 homes and nearly 60 businesses that are currently on the system.

$5.4 million for the City of Fleming-Neon in Letcher County: The USDA-RD project will replace nearly 37,000 linear feet of waterlines and fixtures.

$10.9 million for the City of Jackson: The USDA-RD project will help replace the existing wastewater treatment plant that was damaged in the July 2022 flood.

$4.6 million for the Knott County Water and Sewer District: The USDA-RD project will provide in-kind replacement of the wastewater treatment plant and sewer lines that were damaged during the July 2022 flood.

$1.5 million for the City of Hazard: The USDA-RD project, funded through and ARC grant, will help replace 20 miles of water lines from Buckhorn to Chavies and construct a 250,000-gallon storage tank.

$1.275 million for the City of Beattyville: The USDA-RD project, funded through an ARC grant, will renovate three existing water storage tanks throughout the distribution system.

STATE FUNDING: $1 million for the City of Jenkins: Local match for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Section 531 Project.

STATE FUNDING: $1.5 million for the Letcher County Fiscal Court: The funding will help provide waterline extensions to Thunder Mountain in Letcher County.

STATE FUNDING: $438,000 for the Southeast Road Resurfacing Project in Letcher County.

For more information about Congressman Rogers’ work in Washington and at home in Kentucky, visit halrogers.house.gov and follow him on social media.

title: Congressman Smith: Trump Administration Continues to Deliver Permanent Relief for Small Businesses
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – The U.S. Treasury Department’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) recently issued a final rule permanently ending the requirement for U.S. companies and individuals to report beneficial ownership information under the Corporate Transparency Act. Beneficial ownership information identifies the individuals who actually own or control a company, generally anyone holding 25 percent or more of a business or exercising substantial control over it. This is a reporting mandate small business owners have long identified as a costly, confusing paperwork burden that fell hardest on mom-and-pop shops and family-owned businesses rather than the criminal networks it was meant to target.

Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08), Chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee, released the following statement:

“For years, small business owners have been buried under a reporting mandate that treated every family-owned shop and farm like a suspect in a financial crime. The Trump Administration has thankfully put an end to that for good. Now a small business owner in Missouri or anywhere else in the country can spend more of their time running their business instead of filing paperwork with the federal government just to prove they own it. Cutting red tape like this is exactly what America’s small businesses need, and I’m glad Secretary Bessent and President Trump delivered it.”

title: Smith Visits Meert Tree Farm in Jefferson County
text:
JEFFERSON COUNTY, Mo. – Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08) visited Meert Tree Farm in Jefferson County last week, touring the operation and meeting with the Meert family to discuss the challenges facing Missouri’s specialty crop producers and multi-generational family farms.

Congressman Smith said, “The Meert family has spent more than 60 years building something special here. Every fall and winter, thousands of families make the trip out to start a holiday tradition, cutting their own Christmas tree down with a handsaw, and that’s a testament to what the Meerts have built. I know firsthand what it means to fight to keep a family farm going — I bought my own grandparents’ farm while I was in law school so it could stay in our family, and I understand the sacrifice that takes.

“Families like the Meert’s are exactly who I was fighting for when I authored the Working Families Tax Cuts. By permanently doubling the small business expensing threshold and locking in 100 percent immediate expensing, farms like this one can keep reinvesting in their operation. I’ll keep fighting for policies that support family farms because they’re the backbone of rural Missouri and deserve every opportunity to thrive.”

Meert Tree Farm was founded in 1963 by Domien Meert and his father, expanding to its current 150-acre Festus location in 1980. The farm is now managed by second- and third-generation family members following the passings of founders Domien and Eileen. Meert Tree Farm grows Scotch Pine, White Pine, and Norway Spruce across roughly 80 planted acres, with trees taking five to eight years to mature before they’re ready for sale. The farm draws visitors from across the region and allows customers to cut their own trees using only a handsaw, and the Meert family expects to sell 3,000 trees this season. In addition to its Christmas tree operation, the farm also features a pumpkin patch and corn maze spanning 15 to 18 acres.

During the visit, the Meert family discussed rising input costs such as fuel, and the challenges of navigating regulatory and liability requirements as a specialty crop producer.

The Working Families Tax Cuts, which Congressman Smith authored, made permanent 100 percent immediate expensing, the small business deduction, and doubled small business expensing thresholds, while also renewing the Opportunity Zone program to target investment toward rural communities like Jefferson County. Congressman Smith also highlighted USDA Farm Service Agency programs, including Farm Ownership Loans and Beginning Farmer and Rancher programs, that can help multi-generational farm families access the financing they need to keep operations like Meert Tree Farm running for generations to come.

title: Kaptur Announces Over $32 Million US EPA Award for Lower Maumee River Sway Bridge Project
text:
Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Co-Chair of the bipartisan House Great Lakes Task Force and Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water, announced that the Toledo-Lucas County Port Authority has been awarded $32,343,000 through the United States Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) Great Lakes Restoration Initiative (GLRI) to complete remediation of the Lower Maumee River Sway Bridge Project. Congresswoman Kaptur has championed the GLRI since before its creation, and has worked with Presidents of both parties to ensure its continued funding levels. She continues to lead legislation to reauthorize the GLRI including the GLRI Act of 2025.

“As the largest tributary to the Great Lakes, the Maumee River is a precious natural resource that we must strive to cherish and protect for the generations to come,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). “With this major Federal investment, we return taxpayer dollars back home to Northwest Ohio to allow us to continue our role as stewards of the Great Lakes ecosystem and our mighty Maumee River. The health of our fresh water sources is vital, including that of the Maumee River which is the largest tributary in the entire the Great Lakes region. This is both an environmental and economic priority for our region, as our Great Lakes are home to thousands of unique plant and animal species and generate over $82 Billion in wages and 1.5 million jobs for the Great Lakes Nation on both sides of our northern border.”

"We are proud to partner with the US EPA, Ohio EPA, the US Army Corps of Engineers, the City of Toledo, and the Great Lakes National Program Office on this transformational project," said Thomas J. Winston, President and CEO of the Toledo-Lucas County Port Authority. "This investment demonstrates a continued commitment to restoring one of our region's greatest natural resources while strengthening the Port of Toledo's working waterfront.”

The award will be used to support the removal of tens of thousands of cubic yards of sediment from the Lower Maumee River between the Seneca Petroleum Marine Terminal and the Ironville Marine Terminal. This will be one of the largest sediment remediation efforts in Northwest Ohio. All dredged material will be disposed of within the Port Authority’s Confined Disposal Facility. The site has been designated as a priority for remediation efforts due to high levels of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and other contaminants. Produced both naturally and by human activity, PAHs have been linked to cancer, cardiovascular issues, and developmental defects. The Ohio EPA will also be contributing $1.75 Million to the project.

The Maumee Area of Concern was designated in 1987 and spans across nearly 1,900 miles of streams and 45 miles of Lake Erie shoreline. Industrial and municipal development in the area has led to contamination entering the water, making it less safe for wildlife, recreation, and fresh drinking water. Federal, state, and local partners have joined hands on several projects to advance remediation and restoration efforts.

Through her position as ranking member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water, Congresswoman Kaptur has secured millions of dollars of funds each year for Northwest Ohio wetlands and shorelines. In 2026 alone, this includes $17.6 Million for harbor dredging in Northwest Ohio, $3.4 Million for the Sawmill Creek Wastewater Treatment plant, and $795,152 for the University of Toledo’s research on harmful algal blooms (HAB). Congresswoman Kaptur remains committed to bringing new funds and Federal investment back home, to ensure your tax dollars uplift our communities.

title: Common Dreams: New Inflation Numbers Prove ‘Catastrophic Mismanagement of Our Economy’ by Trump
text:
As Americans continue to struggle with the cost of gasoline, groceries, healthcare, housing, and more under President Donald Trump, congressional Democrats and economists on Wednesday used his own government’s latest inflation figures to call out the Republican’s handling of the US economy.

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics announced that the consumer price index—a measure of goods and services bought by households—increased 0.1% on a seasonally adjusted basis in July after falling 0.4% in June. The annual inflation rate was 3.4% before seasonal adjustment.

The brief reprieve for American consumers in June was tied to Trump’s illegal Iran War cooling off a bit, so the new numbers were expected, given the ramped-up hostilities that followed and persist. The conflict and its various consequences are expected to hurt Republicans in the November elections.

“Prices started climbing again in July, and Trump’s catastrophic mismanagement of our economy means more spikes in the months ahead,” warned Alex Jacquez, a former Obama administration official who is now senior vice president of policy and advocacy at Groundwork Collaborative, in a statement.

“The president said it himself: He is only ‘semi-negotiating’ an end to the war, all while slapping new tariffs on 99% of our imported goods,” noted Jacquez. “Trump is not serious about bringing much-needed relief to working families who are weary of higher prices at the pump and on the shelves, and who are pessimistic about an economy that is bleeding jobs.”

US Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) said Wednesday that “as inflation continues to spiral out of control and gas prices remain well above $4, this is how Donald Trump is spending your taxpayer dollars. $900 million for a gilded ballroom at the White House. $0 to lower your costs. The Trump White House in a nutshell.”

House Budget Committee Ranking Member Brendan Boyle (D-Pa.) recalled when Trump was asked in May how much “Americans’ financial situations” were on his mind as he tried to negotiate an end to the Iran War, and the president replied, “Not even a little bit,” then returned to his misleading talking points on nuclear weapons.

“Month after month, Donald Trump continues to prove that he doesn’t ‘think about Americans’ financial situation,’” Boyle said. “Over the last year and a half, Trump and Republicans in Washington have ripped healthcare away from millions of Americans, forced families to pay expensive tariff taxes, and started a disastrous war with Iran.”

“Today’s report is yet another reminder that Trump’s promise to lower costs on ‘Day One’ was a lie,” the congressman added. “American families deserve better.”

House Minority Whip Katherine Clark (D-Mass.) declared on social media Wednesday, “Donald Trump’s economy is a disaster.”

“His war is spiking gas costs. Wages are down. Inflation is up,” she said, looking to the midterms. “In November, Democrats will take back the House and fight for an affordable America.”

—

title: The Center Square: House Democrats to hold congressional field hearing on ICE shooting in Maine
text:
U.S. House Democrats will be holding their second field hearing next week to address fatal shootings committed by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

U.S. Rep. Chellie Pingree, D-ME, has organized the hearing, “Seeking Justice in Biddeford” to conduct oversight of ICE’s use of force after the July 13 ICE fatal shooting of Colombian national Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, in Biddeford, Maine.

The hearing will be held at 11 a.m. Aug. 17 at Biddeford High School’s Little Theater.

It’s the second congressional field hearing in less than a month after members of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and U.S. House Homeland Security Committee, all Democrats, held a hearing in Houston, Texas. The hearing addressed the July 7 ICE fatal shooting of Mexican national Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston. Less than a week later, another ICE agent shot and killed Guerrero in Biddeford.

In both cases, the men weren’t persons of interest that ICE agents were looking for during targeted enforcement operations, officials said. In both cases, the Department of Homeland Security said in separate statements that both men drove their vehicles toward ICE agents who fired in self-defense, killing them.

In both cases, witnesses and family members dispute the claims made by DHS and ICE, arguing the men didn’t “weaponize” their vehicles and were unarmed. Multiple investigations are ongoing into both shootings. Maine’s bipartisan delegation called for the DHS Inspector General to conduct a comprehensive, transparent and expedited investigation. A state AG investigation is also underway.

At the Houston hearing, Hispanic Caucus Chair U.S. Rep. Adriano Espaillat, D-NY, said eight people, including two U.S. citizens, have been killed by ICE agents so far during the second Trump administration, The Center Square reported.

Next week, scheduled speakers include Biddeford Mayor Liam LaFountain, Guerrero family legal representative Ben Gideon, Immigrant Legal Advocacy Project executive director Sue Roche and Maine Immigrants’ Rights Coalition executive director Mufalo Chitam.

U.S. Rep. Bennie Thompson, D-Miss., ranking member of the U.S. House Committee on Homeland Security will co-lead the hearing as he did in Houston. Democratic Whip Katherine Clark, D-Mass., and other Democratic members of Congress will also participate, according to an announcement from Pingree’s office.

No Republican members have yet to announce their attendance. However, LaFountain said he hopes that Republican members of Congress will attend “because this is an issue that deserves serious attention and oversight from across the political spectrum,” Maine Morning Star reported. “Federal authority must come with federal accountability, and Congress has an important role to play in providing that oversight when the exercise of federal authority results in the death of a member of our community.”

On Tuesday, more than 150 people protested outside of U.S. Sen. Susan Collins’ Biddeford office, holding “ICE OUT!” signs. The protest was organized by Maine People’s Alliance and Center for Popular Democracy, Maine Morning Star reported.

Collins, running for reelection to her sixth term, has recently dropped in the polls. Her challenger, Democrat Troy Jackson, is ahead by 4 points, according to the polling.

House Democrats began holding field hearings after assaults against ICE agents are up 1,300% since the Biden administration. Vehicular attacks against ICE agents are up 3,200%; death threats are up by 8,000%, The Center Square reported.

The hearings are also being held as U.S. citizens continue to raise concerns about ICE agent actions.

In a video posted on social media on Tuesday, a recorded altercation with ICE agents in Virginia appears to show one ICE agent pointing a gun in the face of a U.S. citizen while she’s seated in her car. He and other agents are recorded shouting and swearing and threatening to “lock her up,” according to the video.

U.S. House Democrats posted the video to social media stating, “An ICE agent pointed a gun inches from a U.S. citizen’s face. This agency is dangerously out of control. If ICE is not held accountable, they will kill another innocent person.”

U.S. Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-VA, said he’d been in contact with her and “she’s a U.S. citizen and lives in my district.”

“How many more videos like this will we need to see, with Americans having guns pulled on them by Trump’s untrained ICE agents, before we get real accountability from ICE? I will be demanding answers and consequences,” he said.

title: Congresista Mario Diaz-Balart asiste a la ceremonia de renombramiento de la escuela primaria de Hialeah en memoria de su hermano, el Congresista Lincoln Diaz-Balart

title: Congressman Mario Diaz-Balart Attends Ceremony Renaming School After His Late Brother, Former Congressman Lincoln Diaz-Balart
text:

I am grateful that the Lincoln Diaz-Balart Hialeah Elementary School will stand as a lasting tribute to his legacy, reminding us all of the power that each one of us has to make a difference in the lives of others.

title: Reps McClain Delaney and Lieu Introduce The Congressional Authorization for Federal Building Names Act
text:
In September 2025, Trump ordered the Department of Defense to be renamed the “Department of War.” However, FY27 appropriations requests and bills continue to refer to the agency as the Department of Defense because the change has not been enacted in statute. This renaming attempt could cost taxpayers up to $125 million. Later in December, Trump ordered the John F. Kennedy Center to be renamed the “Donald J. Trump and John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts,” and directed the U.S. Institute of Peace to be renamed the “Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace.” The Administration has physically changed the names of these buildings, effectively defacing them.

“The names on our federal buildings are not any President’s to give away. They belong to the American people, and only Congress can change them. This bill puts that in statute — with real penalties for appointees who ignore it,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney.

“Presidents should not be able to unilaterally put their own name on federal property,” said Congressman Lieu. “Not only is this practice self-centered, it also carries a large price tag for the American people. Renaming federal property should respect the history, spirit, and purpose of the property as opposed to catering to the ego of the president.”

title: McGovern Tells Secretary Rubio: Prioritize Human Rights in Engagement with Central Sahel
Miller-Meeks Welcomes Treasury Secretary Bessent to Iowa for Vermeer Tour
text:
PELLA, IOWA — Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks (IA-01) welcomed U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to Iowa's First District for a tour of Vermeer, one of the district's premier manufacturers, to see Iowa manufacturing firsthand.

"It was an honor to welcome Secretary Bessent to Iowa's First District for a firsthand look at Vermeer," said Congresswoman Miller-Meeks. "Iowa doesn't just talk about American manufacturing, we build it, and Secretary Bessent saw that up close. He heard directly from Vermeer's workforce about how the Working Families Tax Cuts are already helping expand American manufacturing and create good-paying jobs right here at home."

“President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts created the certainty and conditions necessary for durable, private-sector growth. Great to join Congresswoman Miller-Meeks and the National Association of Manufacturers at the Vermeer Corporation facility in Pella, Iowa to hear directly from farmers and manufacturers how America First pro-growth policies are translating into investment and opportunity across America’s heartland.” - Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent

During the visit, Secretary Bessent toured Vermeer's facility and heard directly from workers about how recent tax relief is supporting expansion and job growth at the company.

The Working Families Tax Cuts made permanent several pro-manufacturing provisions that are fueling investment across the country, including 100% bonus depreciation, allowing manufacturers to immediately deduct the full cost of new equipment and machinery; full expensing for the construction of new factories; and permanent, immediate expensing for domestic research and development, reversing a 2022 rule that had forced companies to spread those deductions out over five years. According to the Tax Foundation, these provisions are giving manufacturers more tax relief than any other industry in the country, fueling new plant construction, equipment upgrades, and job creation nationwide.

"This is exactly the kind of investment in American workers we need more of," said Congresswoman Miller-Meeks. "I'm grateful the Secretary took the time to see Iowa's manufacturing strength for himself."

title: Neguse Succeeds in Urging NSF to Restore Full Funding for Quantum Center at CU Boulder
text:
Lafayette, CO — Today, Colorado Congressman Joe Neguse announced that the National Science Foundation (NSF) has reversed its planned 22% reduction to the University of Colorado Boulder’s JILA Physics Frontiers Center (JILA-PFC), restoring the center’s full award. For more than twenty years, JILA-PFC has been foundational to quantum research and training, helping cement Colorado’s position as a leader in quantum science and innovation. The proposed reduction would have exacerbated the quantum industry’s talent shortage, not only in Colorado, but across the nation, and undermined the nation’s competitiveness in quantum science.

Rep. Neguse and his office contacted NSF in early July to oppose the proposed cuts and urge the agency to fully fund the center. NSF has since informed CU Boulder that it will provide the full amount of funding for the grant's upcoming fourth year.

“Colorado’s research institutes and laboratories are central to the fabric of our state and our nation, and I’m proud to see the NSF heed our calls and follow through on their commitment to provide critical funding for CU Boulder’s barrier-breaking JILA Physics Frontiers Center. The hardworking scientists, researchers, and students at this institution have made groundbreaking advances in quantum that drive not only our state’s economy, but also America’s standing on the global stage. We must continue to support their work—for the development of the next generation of scientists and to ensure that the benefits of their discoveries reach every American,” said Congressman Neguse.

“CU Boulder is grateful to Congressman Neguse and Colorado's congressional delegation for their leadership in supporting the JILA Physics Frontier Center and sustained investment in quantum research,” said Massimo Ruzzene, senior vice chancellor for research and innovation and dean of the institutes. “For more than two decades, the JILA Physics Frontier Center has advanced the frontiers of quantum science while training the scientists, engineers and entrepreneurs who are shaping the future of this critical field. This restored funding will strengthen that mission by supporting pioneering research and the development of the quantum workforce that Colorado and the nation need.”

Congressman Neguse has forcefully worked to protect Colorado’s scientific institutions, including opposing plans to dismantle the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) in Boulder and successfully protecting funding for vital programs at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

title: Nunn Hosts Treasury Secretary Bessent, House Leaders as Trump Accounts Reach 7 Million Children
text:
“Iowa’s small businesses and community banks are the backbone of our state’s economy, and today’s conversation made clear that the Working Families Tax Cuts are delivering for the families and businesses they serve,” said Rep. Nunn. “We wrote this law to reward hard work, put more dollars in the pockets and paychecks of hardworking Iowans, and give families new ways to save for the future. Secretary Bessent has been a true partner in making that vision a reality. With this week’s guidance, Iowa employers can now contribute directly to their employees’ children’s accounts, while parents can save for their kids’ futures straight from their paycheck.”

“In Iowa, I joined Congressman Nunn, House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, Ways and Means Committee Chairman Jason Smith, Iowa Superintendent of Banking James Johnson, the Iowa Bankers Association, and local banking leaders to discuss how President Trump’s economic agenda is delivering for American families and Main Street,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “From providing certainty through the Working Families Tax Cuts and supporting financial literacy with Trump Accounts to fighting financial crime and cutting unnecessary regulatory burdens, this Administration continues to encourage investment, unlock capital, and ensure community banks can serve the families, entrepreneurs, and small businesses that drive the American economy.”

“I worked closely with Zach Nunn to pass the Working Families Tax Cuts to help make life more affordable not just for American families today, but for the next generation,” said House Majority Leader Steve Scalise. “With 7 million children already enrolled in Trump Accounts, parents across the country have a new opportunity to start saving and building wealth for their children. I appreciate Congressman Nunn bringing us together with Secretary Bessent and Chairman Smith here in Iowa to discuss how we can build on that progress and create more opportunities for hardworking families. That’s what the American Dream is all about: working hard, building a better life, and giving your children even greater opportunities than you have.”

“Two years ago, the Ways and Means Committee became the first committee to hold an official committee hearing at the Iowa State Fairgrounds to hear directly from Iowa families, farmers and small business owners, who were Republicans’ number one priority when writing the Working Families Tax Cuts,” said Chairman Smith. “Congressman Nunn spoke at that hearing about his interest in families getting tax relief from an expanded child tax credit, Iowa farmers benefitting from an extended biofuels tax credit, small businesses benefitting from the same tax treatment that large corporations receive, and adoption being made more affordable for working families. We achieved all of those things in our tax bill, thanks in part to Congressman Nunn’s leadership. I was also proud to join Congressman Nunn for a telephone town hall in June where we spoke directly with thousands of Iowans about the new tax relief available. Congressman Nunn fought to deliver this tax relief for the people he represents, and he’s fighting just as hard to make sure folks know about the results: permanent relief for family farms facing the Death Tax, a small business deduction, full, immediate expensing to help Main Street businesses grow and hire, and more of every paycheck staying in workers’ pockets through No Tax on Tips and No Tax on Overtime. None of that happens without a Congressman like Zach Nunn, who’s never been afraid to break from the pack in Washington and keeps advocating for the people of Iowa.”

“Iowa’s banking leaders appreciated the opportunity to meet with Secretary Bessent and Congressman Nunn to thank them for their leadership in financial services policy, to discuss the impacts of the Working Families Tax Cuts, to share our insights on the Iowa economy, and to provide suggestions on how to continue to improve the regulatory environment,” said Adam Gregg, President & CEO, Iowa Bankers Association. “The accessibility of both of these leaders is remarkable and appreciated.”

The roundtable came as the Administration advances new policies designed to help build wealth, strengthen community banks, and reduce unnecessary red tape for America’s small businesses. Earlier this week, the Treasury Department also issued new guidance allowing employers to contribute to Trump Accounts and permanently ended burdensome federal beneficial ownership reporting requirements for America’s small businesses.

Building Savings for the Next Generation

Trump Accounts, created by the Working Families Tax Cuts, officially launched on July 4, 2026. Every child born from 2025 through 2028 is eligible for a $1,000 federal contribution, and 7 million children have enrolled nationwide since the program launched, according to the Treasury Department.

New guidance issued this week gives families and employers additional ways to build on that foundation. Employers can contribute up to $2,500 per year, tax-free, to an employee’s child’s Trump Account, while parents can direct pre-tax dollars from their paychecks into the children’s accounts.

At today’s roundtable, Iowa banking and financial services leaders discussed how Trump Accounts can help families establish a culture of saving, strengthen financial literacy, and give the next generation a stronger financial foundation.

Cutting Red Tape for Iowa’s Small Businesses

The Treasury Department’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) also finalized a rule this week permanently ending beneficial ownership information (BOI) reporting requirements for American companies and U.S. citizens, and committed to deleting information previously filed by U.S. persons. Foreign entities registered to do business in the United States remain subject to reporting requirements.

Rep. Nunn led the legislative response to the BOI mandate, authoring the Protect Small Businesses from Excessive Paperwork Act, which passed the House 408-0 in February 2025.

The legislation addressed a federal reporting requirement that subjected small business owners to daily fines and up to two years in prison for failing to complete paperwork many business owners were unaware they were required to file. According to the National Federation of Independent Business, 80% of its members were unaware of the requirement, while the National Small Business Association estimated first-year compliance costs of roughly $8,000 per business. By FinCEN’s own accounting, ending the mandate eliminates more than 91 million hours of annual paperwork and approximately $9 billion in annual compliance costs nationwide.

Rep. Nunn’s Financial Services Agenda

Rep. Nunn has advanced four bills through the House Financial Services Committee this Congress, with three also passing on the House floor. At today’s roundtable, he highlighted three priorities for strengthening Iowa’s financial economy:

Bringing capital to the heartland. Rep. Nunn’s ELEVATE Act makes it easier for growing companies to access public markets by allowing them to provide two years of audited financial statements, rather than three, when going public, and permitting confidential draft registration. The bipartisan legislation passed the House by voice vote in June 2025 and was later incorporated into a broader bipartisan capital formation package that passed the House 302–123 in December.

Protecting Iowans from financial fraud. The GUARD Act gives state, local, and tribal law enforcement the tools and resources to combat elder financial fraud and “pig butchering” scams, and authorizes federal agencies to share blockchain tracing tools. The bipartisan legislation advanced unanimously, 52-0, through the Financial Services Committee in May.

Cutting red tape for independent financial advisors. The Clarity for Compensation Act gives independent financial advisors the same ability to route compensation through their own business entities that lawyers, accountants, and insurance agents already have. The bipartisan legislation passed the Financial Services Committee unanimously in June.

title: Pallone Presses U.S. Airlines for Answers on Surveillance Pricing
text:
Washington, D.C. – Energy and Commerce Committee Ranking Member Frank Pallone, Jr. (D-NJ) requested details from the eight major U.S. airline companies as part of the Committee’s ongoing inquiry into corporate surveillance pricing practices.

“I am very concerned about companies potentially using Americans’ personal data to determine what prices they see and pay, and I am continuing an inquiry into just how widespread this practice is,” Pallone wrote. “Consumers deserve to know if businesses are using their personal information to manipulate the prices they pay or experiment with algorithms to set the prices they see.”

In May, Pallone launched a Committee inquiry into surveillance pricing with an initial round of letters to 25 major corporations, including information on whether they’re using surveillance pricing based on consumers’ personal data to charge customers different prices for the same goods, particularly for online shopping.

The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) defines surveillance pricing as a form of personalized dynamic pricing where companies use a consumer’s online data—location, demographics, browsing history, shopping habits, or device type—to set individualized prices, often charging higher amounts based on an inferred willingness to pay.

“The airline industry specifically has faced several public allegations of surveillance pricing,” Pallone continued. “One study found that an airline boosted its own revenue by as much as six percent by leveraging AI pricing based on consumer information, an increase that comes at the expense of consumers. Lawsuits have been filed against airlines alleging the use of consumers’ information to set prices and in 2025, an airline came under scrutiny after appearing to announce that they were implementing artificial intelligence to assist with pricing.”

Ranking Member Pallone wrote to the following companies and requested answers by August 25, 2026:

Alaska Airlines

American Airlines

Delta Air Lines

Frontier Airlines

Hawaiian Airlines

JetBlue Airways

Southwest Airlines

United Airlines

title: Rep. Panetta Announces Federal Funding for Martial Cottle Park
text:
San Jose, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) brought together Santa Clara County officials and community partners to announce $250,000 in federal funding that he secured for the Martial Cottle Park Improvements Project. The community project funding, provided through the Department of Housing and Urban Development’s Economic Development Initiative, supports the implementation of Phase I of the park’s 31-acre Historic Ranch Site Plan.

“Here in the Silicon Valley, we’re very proud of our innovation and technology, but we’re also proud of our roots in agriculture and the hard work that has defined the Santa Clara Valley. There is no greater place to experience that heritage than Martial Cottle Park, which embodies both the beauty and the bounty that make the 19th Congressional District so special,” said Rep. Panetta. “The significant federal funding secured will carry forward the Cottle family’s legacy by helping repurpose historic buildings, expand opportunities for agricultural education and recreation, and strengthen the park as a gathering place for the entire South San Jose community.”

“With Congressman Panetta’s leadership in securing $250,000 in federal funding, we open a new chapter in honoring the agricultural legacy of the Martial Cottle Park Deed through the implementation of Phase I of the Martial Cottle Historic Ranch Site Plan,” said Supervisor Sylvia Arenas, Vice President of the Santa Clara County Board of Supervisors representing District 1. “This project is a testament to our efforts to preserve Santa Clara County’s agricultural roots and farms while expanding agricultural education and agritourism for future generations.”

“The Santa Clara County Parks Department is looking forward to celebrating the completion of Phase I of the Cottle Lester Historic Ranch project and opening of the perimeter trail with the public in November,” said Julie Andersen, Deputy Director of Planning, Development, and Land Stewardship. “This project is a significant milestone in preserving the agricultural heritage of the Santa Clara Valley, and the Department thanks Congressman Panetta for the generous funding contribution that helped make this project possible.”

The funding is helping repurpose historic ranch buildings and create educational spaces, outdoor classrooms, community gathering areas, reservable picnic areas, accessible pathways, restrooms, and a large outdoor event space. The full Historic Ranch Site Plan will transform the 31-acre site while preserving its agricultural character and historic structures. The project carries forward the Cottle family’s decision to preserve the ranch for public use, education, and future generations, while creating new opportunities for residents and visitors to learn about the region’s agricultural heritage.

Rep. Panetta worked for this federal funding to be included in the most recent appropriations package. For FY 2026, he secured $3.75 million in community project funding for local projects across Santa Clara County, and a total of over $15 million to fund 14 local projects in California’s 19th Congressional District.

title: Rep. Panetta Convenes Local Leaders to Discuss Impacts of the Administration’s Mass Deportation Policy
text:
Aptos, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) convened education, housing, health care, food assistance, and law enforcement professionals from Santa Cruz and Monterey counties for a roundtable discussion at Cabrillo College on the local impacts of the Administration’s mass deportation policies. Participants discussed how federal enforcement actions are affecting access to and use of essential services, trust in law enforcement, and the daily lives of families throughout the Monterey Bay region.

The discussion also focused on the more than $200 billion increase in federal funding for immigration enforcement, the need for commonsense guardrails and accountability, and the Administration’s continued attacks on constitutional rights and lawful immigration programs. Rep. Panetta addressed his opposition to unchecked funding for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and his support for demands to reform federal immigration enforcement and commonsensical immigration reform. He also highlighted his efforts to protect Dreamers, oppose the potential ICE facility near Gilroy, and safeguard birthright citizenship.

“Our discussion made clear that this Administration’s mass deportation policies are affecting our communities, from schools, health care, and housing to public safety and the rule of law,” said Rep. Panetta. “I support a strong and secure border, but that does not require mass deportations, unchecked funding for immigration enforcement, unaccountable federal agents, or unconstitutional attacks on Americans. Congress must impose guardrails, oversight, and accountability while pursuing commonsense reforms to improve our asylum system, protect Dreamers, and provide earned legalization for hardworking immigrants. I will continue working in Congress and with our local partners to protect those who contribute so much to our communities.”

“Cabrillo College stands firmly with all of our students and we will continue to prioritize safety, support and access to education. We want every family in Santa Cruz County to know that Cabrillo campuses in Aptos and Watsonville remain safe and welcoming where student privacy is protected,” said Jenn Capps, Ph.D., President/Superintendent, Cabrillo College.

“Every child, regardless of immigration status, has a fundamental right to a free public education in an environment where they feel safe, protected, and supported. Our schools are sanctuaries of learning and stability, and immigration enforcement concerns should never compromise a student’s ability to attend class, grow, and thrive. We are proud to stand with Representative Panetta to reaffirm our unwavering commitment to keeping our campuses safe, protecting our students, and ensuring our schools remain places of hope and opportunity for every family,” said Deneen Guss, Ed.D., Monterey County Superintendent of Schools, Monterey County Office of Education.

“Every student deserves to come to school feeling safe, welcomed, and supported. Our schools remain committed to creating environments where every child can learn without fear or distraction. We will continue to provide our students, families, and staff with accurate information and timely resources regarding immigration enforcement activities in and around our school communities, while ensuring that our focus remains on the safety, well-being, and success of every student,” said Dr. Ernesto Vela, Assistant Superintendent, Monterey County Office of Education.

“Public safety depends on trust. Whether someone is experiencing domestic violence, a child is missing, or a family is facing a crisis, no one should be afraid to call for help because of their immigration status. Our undocumented residents are part of our communities, and when they call for help, we are here to help them. Our public safety professionals are here to protect everyone we serve. I appreciate Congressman Panetta bringing us together to strengthen that trust,” said Monterey County Sheriff Tina Nieto.

“HUD’s proposal to require every resident in federally assisted housing to establish citizenship or eligible immigration status would be devastating for families and could have profound consequences for housing stability in our communities. Mixed-status families are families, and when we put one member of a household at risk of losing access to housing assistance because of their immigration status, we put the stability of the entire family at risk, including U.S. citizen children. At a time when housing is already out of reach for far too many families, we should not be creating additional barriers that could push people into displacement and homelessness. Housing is the foundation of family and community stability, and our policies should reflect that,” said Elaine Johnson, Executive Director, Housing Santa Cruz County.

“At Santa Cruz Community Health, we care for everyone who walks through our doors, regardless of language spoken, personal identity, or ability to pay,” said Anita Aguirre, CEO, Santa Cruz Community Health.

Last year, Rep. Panetta opposed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which provided more than $75 billion to ICE and $65 billion to CBP. In June, the Secure America Act provided nearly $70 billion more for ICE, CBP, and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) immigration enforcement operations through Fiscal Year 2029. Rep. Panetta voted against the Secure America Act and has voted at least seven separate times this Congress against providing ICE and CBP with additional funding without meaningful guardrails, oversight, or accountability.

Rep. Panetta has supported Democratic demands to require federal immigration agents to wear body cameras and clearly display identification, prohibit non-tactical masks that conceal their identities, strengthen warrant requirements, establish enforceable standards for the use of force and de-escalation, and ensure independent investigations of serious incidents, among other reforms. He is supporting the No Secret Police Act and the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act, which would restrict immigration enforcement at schools, hospitals, houses of worship, courthouses, and other sensitive locations.

In July, DHS briefly paused most vehicle stops by ICE deportation officers after agents fatally shot two men during separate operations in Houston, Texas, and Biddeford, Maine, while searching for other individuals. The White House overturned that pause the following day before the agency completed its review and additional training. Rep. Panetta joined nearly 200 House lawmakers in calling for independent investigations into both deaths, protection for witnesses, and the immediate deployment of body cameras to ICE and CBP agents. The three men traveling with Lorenzo Salgado Araujo when he was shot and killed in Houston each filed for U Visa protection. Rep. Panetta’s Immigrant Witness and Victim Protection Act would strengthen the U Visa program for immigrant survivors and witnesses of serious crimes who cooperate with law enforcement. The legislation would lift the cap on U Visas, protect eligible applicants from detention and deportation while their cases are pending, and allow them to work during the application process.

Earlier this year, Rep. Panetta joined Bay Area lawmakers in a letter to DHS and ICE opposing the proposed immigration detention and processing facility near Gilroy and demanding information about the project. Following the lawmakers’ calls, construction at the site was temporarily paused while legal challenges proceed. Rep. Panetta also joined a letter to DHS and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services demanding an explanation for the spike in delays affecting Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) renewal applications and urging the agencies to accelerate processing. The delays have caused Dreamers to lose employment authorization, miss work, and face disruptions to their income and daily lives despite filing timely renewal requests.

In February, after the Department of Housing and Urban Development attempted to override the intent of Congress by taking federal housing benefits away from mixed-status homes, Rep. Panetta joined his colleagues from the Congressional Asian, Black, and Hispanic Caucuses to assert Congressional intent and oppose this misguided rule. Congress has made it clear that federal housing benefits should be prorated for any eligible residents in a unit, and forcing people to choose between their eligible benefits and their loved ones would only cause further turmoil in California’s 19th District.

title: Congressman Patronis Fights to Defend the Second Amendment
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On Tuesday, Congressman Jimmy Patronis (R-FL) joined nearly 50 of his Republican colleagues in Congress in signing a bicameral letter led by Congressman Andrew Clyde and Senator Steve Daines urging Attorney General Todd Blanche and the Department of Justice (DOJ) to defend a landmark victory for the Second Amendment.

The lawmakers are calling on the Department of Justice to stand with the Constitution and not appeal a major Second Amendment victory. On August 5, a federal court in Texas ruled that the federal government can no longer require registration of suppressors, short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns, and certain other firearms after Congress eliminated the related National Firearms Act taxes. The lawmakers are urging the DOJ to let the ruling stand nationwide, end unnecessary federal red tape, and protect the constitutional rights of gun owners.

“Law-abiding Americans shouldn’t have to beg the federal government for permission to exercise a constitutional right,” said Congressman Patronis. “This is consistent with everything I’ve fought for in Congress, from national reciprocity for concealed carry to repealing the Hughes Amendment. The Second Amendment ‘shall not be infringed,’ and I’ll continue fighting every day to stop Washington from putting unnecessary restrictions on our rights. The DOJ should respect the Constitution and let this historic ruling stand.”

Congressman Patronis remains committed to fighting federal overreach and to ensuring the constitutional rights of Americans are protected.
