title: Merkley, Schumer, Top Senate Democrats with Jurisdiction Over Trump’s Gilded Ballroom Boondoggle Call on Watchdog to Conduct a Full Audit of the Project
text:
Dear Acting Comptroller General Williams Brown:

Many of us in Congress have watched with alarm as the Trump administration unilaterally made the decision to demolish the East Wing of the White House—an historic and symbolic structure—without congressional authorization, meaningful public engagement, or following long-established practice for government facilities modernization and historic preservation. The subsequent construction of a new White House ballroom represents one of the most sweeping alterations to the White House complex in modern history. The scale of this project, the destruction of historic architecture, the opaque and unorthodox combination of public funds with private funding sources, and the absence of standard federal review processes raise serious concerns about transparency, accountability, and stewardship of this national landmark.

Congress has neither authorized nor appropriated funding for the “East Wing Modernization Project,” nor has Congress been provided any planning details or justifications that would allow for informed consideration of the White House’s plans that would be a prerequisite for authorization or appropriation of funds. The lack of congressional authorization has been central to the ongoing litigation challenging the ballroom project, National Trust for Historic Preservation in the United States v. National Park Service. This month, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit affirmed that President Trump lacks the legal authority to construct a White House ballroom without congressional authorization. Simply put, no president has the authority to unilaterally demolish and remodel the country’s White House in such a significant manner without congressional approval.

President Trump repeatedly claimed that the demolition of the East Wing and construction of a dramatically expanded gilded ballroom would be carried out solely using private donations, and that no taxpayer funds would be used. Despite those assurances, the administration first tried and failed[1] to secure $1 billion in federal funding for the ballroom through a partisan Republican reconciliation bill, then shifted tact to inappropriately and illegally pay for over half of the $600 million ballroom with previously appropriated funding not intended for this project. It has also been reported that the Trump Administration is utilizing a $500 million no-bid contract to fund the construction of the ballroom—funding that Congress did not approve.[2]

The Trump administration has not provided transparency into the use of federal funds for the East Wing project, and they have limited congressional oversight, meaningful public input, and adherence to established federal processes.

To support Congress’s oversight responsibilities, we request that GAO conduct an audit and assessment of the White House ballroom project and related documentation, including the following:

Planning, Review and Approval Processes: What design, review, and construction approval processes are being applied to the ballroom project? How do these processes and timelines compare to those used for other similar federal construction efforts involving the White House, other historic properties, executive facilities, or national security sensitive sites? Please assess whether required architectural, preservation, environmental, and interagency reviews were conducted and whether any were bypassed, abbreviated or ignored. What documents, if any, were filed with required approval entities prior to initiation of work?

Funding Sources and Cost Transparency: How is the project being funded, including appropriated funds, reconciliation funds, transfers, reprogramming actions, or donated materials and services? Was an initial cost estimate prepared and if so, by what agency or entity and what were the projections from that estimate? What are the total estimated project costs, how much has been obligated and expended to date, and what is the anticipated timeline for completion? What cost control measures were specified for use under this project? Are the funds that were transferred from U.S. Secret Service account to a “White House Repair and Restoration” account within the Executive Residence at the White House, as reported by the Office of Management and Budget, intended for use in the East Wing Modernization Project? Have any federal agencies involved in the East Wing Modernization Project included funding for this project in spend plans submitted to the Office of Management and Budget?

Security Related Components and Interagency Roles: Which elements of the project have been designated as national security related, what criteria were used to make those determinations, and what funding sources are being used for those components? How have appropriate congressional committees been updated on cost and design planning considerations? What is the role of the U.S. Secret Service, the White House Military Office, the White House Communications Agency and the Department of Defense in planning, approving, and coordinating construction activities (including facility communications upgrades and installation of security equipment and other non-construction features), and how are these agencies collaborating among themselves and with other federal entities?

Public Input and Transparency: What opportunities, if any, were provided for public input, expert consultation, or stakeholder engagement prior to demolition of the East Wing and initiation of the ballroom project? Please assess whether federal agencies followed standard public notice and comment practices for major alterations to historic federal properties, whether relevant preservation and advisory bodies were consulted, and how the level of public transparency compares to similar federal construction projects involving historic or iconic sites.

Contractor Donations, Potential Corruption, and Safeguards: Recent public reporting indicates that several contractors and donors associated with the ballroom project have subsequently received substantial federal contract awards, reportedly totaling more than $50 billion. Please assess what safeguards, if any, federal agencies applied to prevent conflicts of interest, preferential treatment, or corruption related to contractors who donated materials, services, or funds to the project. Specifically, what controls exist to ensure that contributions to the project did not influence contract award decisions, and how do these safeguards compare to standard federal procurement integrity requirements? What evaluation criteria were used in identifying and selecting contractors for this effort? Please evaluate whether agencies documented their rationale for contract awards to donor contractors and whether any deviations from standard competitive procedures occurred.

Given the scale, visibility, and long-term implications of this project, an independent GAO review is essential to ensure accountability, transparency, and responsible management of federal resources and historic assets. We request that you provide an update on your proposed plan for this audit by no later than December 1, 2026, with subsequent updates and a final report to be provided at a mutually agreed upon date.

Sincerely,

title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Hosts Back to School Expo for Florida Families Showcasing New Ways to Invest in Children’s Futures and Protect Kids from Online Threats
text:
ORLANDO, Fla.—Senator Ashley Moody hosted the Florida Families First Back to School Resources Fair at Valencia College, bringing valuable resources directly to Florida families. The fair connected families with local, state, federal and community partners offering information and resources about children’s health, education, finances, and safety. Senator Moody, as one of the few mothers to a school-aged child in the Senate, is delivering new ways to jumpstart the American Dream for Florida youth and protect kids against online threats.

“It’s back-to-school time for millions of Florida families, and we want to make sure our children are happy, healthy, and safe. I hosted a Florida Families First Back to School Resources Fair today in Central Florida, bringing together local, state, and federal partners to provide parents valuable information about children’s health, safety, and education—and highlight the important victories we secured to jumpstart the American dream for Florida youth,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

BACKGROUND:

To view Senator Moody’s full remarks, click here.

Joining Senator Moody at today’s event include: Florida Representative Erika Booth, Kissimmee Police Chief Charles “Chuck” Broadway, Florida Department of Education Senior Chancellor Paul Burns, Valencia College President Dr. Kathleen Plinske, Chef Justin Timineri, Pastor Tim Grosshans and Jonathan Cajigas, from Step Up for Students.

Senator Moody championed the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, signed into law last year. The package created child-owned investment accounts designed to give the next generation a real jumpstart on the American Dream. More than 5.5. million child-owned investment accounts have been opened nationwide so far, with 1.4 million eligible for the $1,000 pilot program contribution.

For every baby born from 2025 through 2028 whose parents open one of these accounts, the U.S. Treasury will invest $1,000.

If that initial investment is left untouched, it could grow to nearly $8,000 by the time the child turns 18.

And if they leave it invested until retirement, it could potentially grow into hundreds of thousands of dollars, depending on market returns.

Parents can sign up today at IRS.gov/TrumpAccounts.

Through the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, Senator Moody also fought to double the enhanced Child Tax Credit. 40 million families have taken advantage of the expanded credit.

The Working Families Tax Cuts Act also expanded school choice options nationwide – similar to what Florida has accomplished and to what Senator Ashley Moody supported while as Florida’s Attorney General.

The Working Families Tax Cuts Act includes a provision for a federal tax credit scholarship that could help as many as 2 million students access a school or educational service of their parents’ choice.

Senator Moody is a fierce fighter for school choice. Earlier this year, Senator Moody introduced the FLEX Act, which will cut red tape around Charter School Program grants to be used more effectively based on educational needs, not bureaucratic limitations.

Senator Moody has also fought to strengthen Florida’s education system through co-sponsoring the Educational Choice for Children Act to allow parents to choose the best school for their children.

Another one of Senator Moody’s efforts includes introducing the Home School Graduation Recognition Act to fight for home-schooled students to be officially recognized as graduates.

Senator Moody is championing the Kids Online Safety Act, which is now headed to the Senate floor. The measure aims to guard youth from harm on the internet such as online predators, drug dealers, and addictive algorithms.

title: Sen. Moran Announces Over $1 Million in Federal Resources for Kansas Providers
text:
Moran worked to establish the Rural Health Transformation Program last year

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Jerry Moran (R-Kan.) today announced more than $1 million in federal investments for seven Kansas rural health care providers through the second round of funding from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services’ (CMS) Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program, administered by the Kansas Department of Health and Environment.

Sen. Moran worked to establish the federal program in last year’s reconciliation legislation, also known as the Working Families Tax Cut. The program was created to help identify the root challenges facing rural health providers and invest in solutions to improve outcomes for struggling providers.

“These resources are critical to make certain Kansans living in rural communities have access to high-quality care close to home,” said Sen. Moran. “Last year, I worked with my colleagues to create the Rural Health Transformation Program to help rural providers address the unique challenges in their communities and to give them the resources they need to provide quality care to patients. I will continue working with our rural health care providers and state leaders to find innovative solutions that improve care and strengthen rural communities in Kansas.”

Recipients of the second round of federal resources will use the funding to expand Community Health Worker (CHW) and Accountable Food is Medicine (AFIM) programs, increasing access to community health services and nutritional intervention services and structures.

Recipients:

Hutchinson Regional Medical Center, Inc. – $150,000

Hospital District No. 6 of Harper County, Kansas – $150,000

Great Plains of Smith County, Inc. – $150,000

Hospital District No. 1 of Dickinson County, Kansas, DBA Memorial Health System – $150,000

CommonSpirit Kansas, Inc. – $149,960

Citizens Foundation – $146,476

Newman Memorial County Hospital – $110,716

title: NEW: DHS Deploys Freshly Acquired Jets to Shuttle Trump Officials—including Kash Patel & Tom Homan—Around in Luxury
text:
Murray and Murphy Blast Wasteful Spending, Demand Answers

Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senators Patty Murray (D-WA),Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, and Chris Murphy (D-CT), Ranking Member of the Homeland Security Subcommittee, wrote a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin blasting DHS’ acquisition of 12 new planes—including 5 new luxury jets—and its plans to use those aircraft to ferry Trump administration officials around.

They also sent the letter to the DHS Inspector General, noting that the acquisition and use of the planes merits investigation by his office.

“It has come to our attention that the Department of Homeland Security is effectively running an in-house private jet service for Trump administration officials with a slew of new luxury jets and other airplanes it has acquired and begun providing to officials over the last year,” Murray and Murphy write to Mullin. “This includes providing jet services not only for DHS officials like yourself, but also for White House Border Czar Tom Homan, other administration officials, members of the first family, and even the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Kash Patel.”

The lawmakers blasted the wasteful use of funds and noted that the acquisitions of the planes is almost certainly unlawful, as well: “The Department’s purchase of these airplanes to shuttle administration officials around the globe demonstrates a remarkable disregard for American taxpayers who work hard and expect government officials to responsibly manage their tax dollars, not burn them on extravagant luxury jets. These acquisitions also raise serious legal concerns, as Congress has not provided the necessary legal authorization for DHS to purchase these planes, much less run a private jet service for government executives.”

Murray and Murphy write that Republicans in Congress have delivered over a quarter of a trillion dollars to DHS through two partisan reconciliation bills, but note that: “instead of using the staggering amount of funding provided to DHS to actually improve the lives of Americans by requiring basic compliance with the Fourth Amendment, acquiring and deploying body-worn cameras to every law enforcement officer in the field, mandating minimum officer identification, or properly training new hires, this administration has lit taxpayer dollars on fire by acquiring new and unnecessary planes to jet Trump officials around in extreme luxury.”

They ask for basic information about the acquisitions and plans for the planes and conclude by urging Secretary Mullin to sell the planes and work with Congress to steer the funds to more important priorities: “[W]e hope that you will sell off these unnecessary luxury jets and airplanes acquired by DHS and return the funding to American taxpayers. We would be happy to work with you and our colleagues in Congress to return those dollars to the Treasury and put them to better use making sure Americans can afford health care, rent, and groceries.”

Full text of the letter is available HERE and below:

Markwayne Mullin

Secretary

U.S. Department of Homeland Security

2707 Martin Luther King Jr. Ave., SE

Washington, D.C. 20528

Secretary Mullin,

It has come to our attention that the Department of Homeland Security (“Department” or “DHS”) is effectively running an in-house private jet service for Trump administration officials with a slew of new luxury jets and other airplanes it has acquired and begun providing to officials over the last year. This includes providing jet services not only for DHS officials like yourself, but also for White House Border Czar Tom Homan, other administration officials, members of the first family, and even the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Kash Patel. In total, DHS has acquired 12 new aircraft, including 5 extravagant new luxury jets, using funds provided in the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act” (OBBBA). These jets were acquired and provided for officials’ use, even though no authorization was ever provided by Congress to buy any airplanes, much less to support executive travel.[1]

The Department’s purchase of these airplanes to shuttle administration officials around the globe demonstrates a remarkable disregard for American taxpayers who work hard and expect government officials to responsibly manage their tax dollars, not burn them on extravagant luxury jets. These acquisitions also raise serious legal concerns, as Congress has not provided the necessary legal authorization for DHS to purchase these planes, much less run a private jet service for government executives.[2]

Over the last year, Republicans in Congress have, on a party-line basis, delivered the Department a remarkable windfall totaling over a quarter of a trillion dollars outside of the annual appropriations process. Republicans first approved $190 billion for DHS in the OBBBA last summer. Then, after refusing to enact basic reforms to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Border Patrol following rampant abuses, including the killings of Renée Good and Alex Pretti, they voted to deliver DHS another $70 billion in funding this summer,[3] which was largely earmarked for ICE and Border Patrol and came with no strings attached.

But instead of using the staggering amount of funding provided to DHS to actually improve the lives of Americans by requiring basic compliance with the Fourth Amendment, acquiring and deploying body-worn cameras to every law enforcement officer in the field, mandating minimum officer identification, or properly training new hires, this administration has lit taxpayer dollars on fire by acquiring new and unnecessary planes to jet Trump officials around in extreme luxury that the vast majority of Americans will never experience.

For example, in the midst of last fall’s government shutdown, your predecessor spent nearly $200 million of OBBBA funds provided for the Coast Guard to acquire:

Two Gulfstream 700 luxury business jets, a model Gulfstream describes as “the pinnacle of business aviation excellence,” which boasts “the most spacious cabin in the industry.”[4] The jets were acquired despite the fact that DHS already owns two Gulfstream jets to support executive travel and despite the fact that DHS had never raised the need for any additional jets in any of its annual budget requests. The Department stole money that should have been used to support modernization of the Coast Guard’s fleet, meet operational needs, and improve military readiness to instead purchase two new luxury jets to shuttle the DHS Secretary and Deputy Secretary around the globe.

DHS also spent OBBBA funds provided for ICE to acquire 10 additional aircraft. To justify the purchases, DHS previously claimed they would all be used to support removal operations in some way.[5] Now, it says these planes are being used for the following purposes:

Two Gulfstream G650 luxury business jets, ultra-long-range aircraft that seat up to 15 passengers. One of the G650s has already been leased to the FBI for 12 months to support Director Patel’s travel—despite the fact that the FBI already has its own jets to support the Director’s travel. The other G650 is currently being retrofitted for deployment to support Border Czar Homan and undisclosed DHS officials’ travel, according to the Department.

One Boeing 737-8 MAX business jet, a modified ultra-luxury jet that DHS acquired fully equipped with a bedroom and other luxury amenities like a shower, kitchen, bar, and flatscreen TVs—amenities that even Air Force Two lacks. Despite these features, DHS claimed the jet would “serve dual missions—both as ICE deportation flights and for cabinet level travel.”[6] Now, DHS has informed us the bedroom is being removed, and the plane will remain in ICE’s ownership but be loaned to the Department of Defense (DOD) to fly undisclosed cabinet-level officials. It has also been reported the jet will be used to fly the First Lady around.[7]

Seven Boeing 737s, a commercial aircraft that can seat upwards of 200 passengers. DHS claims four of these aircraft will be used to support Congressional Delegations (CODELs) but has not provided information on why it is necessary or a permissible use of funds for DHS to purchase these aircraft. DHS states three of the aircraft will soon support ICE deportation flights. Top former DHS officials and industry experts have noted that these acquisitions waste tax dollars,[8] and we remain alarmed by how ICE may use these planes to support the administration’s lawless immigration enforcement campaign. One aviation industry executive said that: “It’s hard to see this as anything but a waste of public money.”[9]

The American people deserve a full accounting of this gross misuse of their tax dollars, and Congress needs more information to conduct sorely-needed oversight and to appropriately craft this coming year’s funding bill for the Department. The misuse of these funds also merits investigation by DHS’s Inspector General, and we have copied him on this letter to make him aware of our concerns.

Instead of extending tax credits to lower Americans’ health care costs or investing to help families afford child care and housing, Republicans in Congress chose to make historic cuts to health care and nutrition assistance in order to cut taxes for the ultra-rich and provide DHS with more money for immigration enforcement than the budget of nearly every military in the world. We fought Republicans’ backward legislation to supercharge DHS’s budget, but we believe every lawmaker should at minimum agree that Americans’ tax dollars should not be wasted on lavish new jets to shuttle DHS officials, the FBI director, and an undisclosed number of other Trump officials and family members around the globe in extraordinary comfort.

DHS has repeatedly noted that as Secretary you are focused on being “the best possible steward of taxpayer dollars.”[10] Accordingly, we ask that you furnish the information requested below, and we hope that you will sell off these unnecessary luxury jets and airplanes acquired by DHS and return the funding to American taxpayers. We would be happy to work with you and our colleagues in Congress to return those dollars to the Treasury and put them to better use making sure Americans can afford health care, rent, and groceries.

Please provide the following by August 26, 2026:

Contract details for the purchase of each plane;

Contracts for any/all retrofitting and missionization of each plane;

Cost analysis for the operations and maintenance of each plane for the life cycle of the plane;

Flight logs to date, including the names and titles of passengers, origination, destination, and purpose of travel;

A copy of the lease agreement with the FBI for the G650 jet;

A copy of the loan agreement with DOD for the Boeing 737-8 MAX business jet; and

The legal justifications for the purchase, operation, and maintenance, as well as planned uses, of these aircraft.

Sincerely,

###

title: Padilla, Schiff, Congressional Democrats Demand FTA and OMB Stop Holding Blue State Infrastructure Funding Hostage
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff (both D-Calif.) joined Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and 39 Democratic colleagues in demanding the Trump Administration stop delaying the advancement of public transportation projects funded by the Capital Investment Grants (CIG) program. Currently, the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) has access to more than $1.9 billion in unobligated and unallocated funds ready to be spent. However, the Trump Administration continues to hold up significant projects in blue states while red states’ projects move ahead.

In a letter to FTA Acting Deputy Administrator Mathew Cahill and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Administrator Russel Vought, the lawmakers expressed concern over delays that have created a backlog in transit projects and called out the Administration for potentially holding up funding for political reasons. Last month, the Trump Administration admitted to terminating funding for projects in states that did not vote for the President.

“We have watched for months as the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) have stonewalled the progress of worthy transit projects while President Trump and Department of Transportation Secretary Duffy are proclaiming a commitment to a ‘golden age of transportation,’” wrote the lawmakers.

“The growing backlog of projects in limbo due to FTA and OMB inaction is unacceptable,” continued the lawmakers.“We are very concerned that delaying the CIG project pipeline, while advancing only the Utah project, is potentially rooted in partisan political considerations, which could further violate statutory requirements.”

“Every $1 invested in transit generates $5 in long-term economic value. Conversely, failing to deliver on long-promised transit investment carries serious economic consequences,” wrote the lawmakers. “Should this egregious trend continue, 11 projects in 10 states…that anticipate signing a CIG grant agreement this year could be subjected to senseless delay.”

The lawmakers concluded by reminding the administrators of the historically bipartisan nature of CIG-funded projects and demanded that their agencies immediately advance the stalled projects — regardless of a state’s 2024 election results.

Padilla and Schiff have long been advocates for investment in California transportation infrastructure and have fought against the Trump Administration’s harmful intentional delays on transportation projects. Last month, Padilla and Schiff announced $53.8 million from the Department of Transportation (DOT) to repair highways and roads across California. Last year, Padilla announced over $258 million for nine transportation infrastructure projects across California through the DOT’s Rebuilding American Infrastructure with Sustainability and Equity (RAISE) Grant Program, the Reconnecting Communities Pilot (RCP) Grant Program, and the Rural Surface Transportation Grant (Rural) Program.

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear Director Vought and Acting Deputy Administrator Cahill,

We write to express deep concern regarding reports that your agencies are delaying the advancement of public transportation projects within the Capital Investment Grants (CIG) pipeline. As members of the Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs and House Transportation and Infrastructure Committees and as members of the House and Senate representing affected projects, we have an obligation to ensure that the CIG program is carried out in accordance with statutory requirements that have been enacted to ensure that taxpayer resources are not wasted as a result of delay by the federal government. We have watched for months as the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) have stonewalled the progress of worthy transit projects while President Trump and Department of Transportation Secretary Duffy are proclaiming a commitment to a “golden age of transportation.” We would like to remind you that such a vision is woefully incomplete if it does not include delivering CIG projects that will provide fast, frequent and reliable transit service across the nation.

The growing backlog of projects in limbo due to FTA and OMB inaction is unacceptable. Since last fall, your agencies have neglected to advance the Boston Green Line Transformation project, the Los Angeles Southeast Gateway Line and the Salt Lake City region’s Frontrunner 2X project into the CIG Engineering phase—without justification for the delay. Last week, FTA moved the Utah project into Engineering, a welcome development, but the two other projects remain stalled.

This delay is occurring despite the fact that FTA currently has access to more than $1.9 billion in unobligated and unallocated funds that are available to support CIG projects, and Congress has consistently appropriated new funds each year to the CIG program. The Frontrunner 2X project has already been allocated $594 million of CIG funding, and based on FTA’s commitment at Engineering entry last week, the project will need only $693 million of additional CIG program funds.

We wish to remind you that the projects in Boston, Los Angeles and Salt Lake City have all completed a comprehensive rating process pursuant to the CIG program guidance that was most recently updated by FTA in November of 2025, under President Trump’s administration. Each of the three projects received an overall project rating that qualified them to enter the Engineering phase and later receive a Full Funding Grant Agreement. In fact, the projects in Boston and Los Angeles received an overall higher rating of “medium-high,” compared to the “medium” overall rating of the Utah project.

FTA and OMB should advance all projects that meet statutory criteria, and your agencies should not impose any further delays. Under the most recently enacted appropriations law and prior appropriations laws, FTA, OMB and the Administration are prohibited from using any federal funds to “impede or hinder project advancement or approval for any project seeking a Federal contribution from the capital investment grants program of greater than 40 percent of project costs,” which includes the delayed projects. We are very concerned that delaying the CIG project pipeline, while advancing only the Utah project, is potentially rooted in partisan political considerations, which could further violate statutory requirements.

We are frustrated by reports that OMB is partially responsible for these avoidable and costly delays. As a result of these stalling tactics, there has not been a single new CIG grant agreement signed since this Administration took office. Should this egregious trend continue, 11 projects in 10 states (California, Florida, Maryland, Minnesota, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina, Utah, Washington and Wisconsin) that anticipate signing a CIG grant agreement this year could be subjected to senseless delay. No Administration since 1993 has failed to sign a single CIG grant agreement in the first year: we urge you not to set a new record by failing to sign CIG grant agreements for two years in a row.

Unnecessary delays are not only frustrating; they are economically short-sighted. Transit is an excellent investment. Every $1 invested in transit generates $5 in long-term economic value. Conversely, failing to deliver on long-promised transit investment carries serious economic consequences. Project sponsors and taxpayers will end up footing the bill for delay-induced cost increases. The construction workforce and the broader transportation supply chain are left waiting for critical job-creating investments. In the interim, people have fewer choices to get around their community. The impact of trips not taken to work, to school, or to the doctor undermines economic growth.

Transportation policy is generally bipartisan, and we are proud of this reputation. Through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, Congress re-committed to a multimodal federal transportation program. Every year, Congress reiterates a bipartisan commitment to CIG through the annual appropriations process. We stand ready and willing to continue making robust federal investments in infrastructure on the scale that our country desperately needs. However, any effort to impede or hinder CIG projects does serious harm to the bipartisan coalition that supports federal infrastructure investment. Congress must be confident that the CIG program will be executed in accordance with the law. Any delay or hindrance in delivering CIG projects further undermines our confidence that this Administration will faithfully execute the law.

Many of us represent communities with CIG projects that are currently impacted or could soon be impacted by your agencies’ actions. We request that you immediately advance the two stalled projects in California and Massachusetts into Engineering and prevent further program obstruction or delays. Please respond in writing, not later than August 18, 2026, with your timeline to advance the two projects into the next phase of CIG. Going forward, we request that you expeditiously approve projects that are eligible for a Full Funding or Small Starts Grant Agreement, including the 11 projects seeking grant agreements later this year. Investing in transit projects through the CIG program is essential to building a transportation system that works for everyone.

Sincerely,

###

title: Padilla, Warren, Colleagues Press Trump Administration on CMS Guidance that Could Threaten Nursing Home Residents’ Right to Vote
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Rules and Administration Committee, and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) led 11 of their Senate colleagues in urging the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Mehmet Oz to repeal new guidance that threatens nursing home residents’ right to vote. In California, more than 400,000 nursing home residents would be impacted by the new guidance.

“We write with concern that the recent guidance issued to nursing homes by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services may intimidate nursing home staff from helping residents exercise their constitutional right to vote and ultimately prevent nursing home residents from voting,” wrote the Senators.

Last month, CMS issued new guidance regarding the responsibilities of nursing home staff in the voting process. Previous CMS guidance, including under the first Trump Administration, provided nursing home staff with a list of specific ways nursing homes can make it easier for residents to vote, like assisting with absentee and mail-in voting or transporting residents to polling locations and ballot drop-off boxes. However, the new guidance eliminated these recommendations, replacing them with language warning nursing home staff not to “violate federal or state voting laws” and telling staff that “they cannot engage in inappropriate coercion or other violations of residents’ rights.”

“[This memo] appears to be an attempt to intimidate nursing home staff from assisting residents in the voting process,” continued the Senators.

To reiterate this threat of investigation or prosecution, CMS’s July 2026 memo mentions two investigations of supposed election fraud occurring at nursing homes. However, no fraudulent votes were cast in either of these cases, and there is no evidence of any systemic or significant voter fraud or coercion in nursing homes.

The Senators also raised concerns that the Trump Administration’s decision to highlight examples of prior voter fraud investigations and threaten criminal penalties may be an attempt to intimidate legal immigrants who work in nursing homes, who have already been targeted by the Administration’s policies.

“Ultimately, we are concerned that the changes to CMS’s guidance will result in the disenfranchisement of nursing home residents,” wrote the Senators. “The right to vote is guaranteed by the Constitution to all adult Americans, including nursing home residents…In order to protect nursing home residents’ voting rights, we request that you immediately rescind the July 2026 memo and reinstate the 2020 and 2024 guidance.”

In addition to Padilla and Warren, the letter was signed by Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Angus King (I-Maine), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Mark Warner (D-Va.), Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.), and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.).

As California’s former Secretary of State, Padilla knows first-hand the importance of taking proactive steps to protect the fundamental right to vote. Last week, Padilla led his Senate colleagues in once again defeating MAGA Republicans’ efforts to advance a provision of the anti-voter SAVE Act that would require eligible voters to provide strict photo identification when voting, including in their mail and absentee ballots. Last month, Padilla introduced the SHIELD Our Elections Act, legislation that would provide state Attorneys General and voters with the ability to enforce federal election protections and protect voters’ ballots from seizure. In June, together with U.S. Senator Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.), Padilla reintroduced the Right to Vote Act, legislation to create the first-ever affirmative federal voting rights guarantee for all eligible citizens.

Full letter is available here or below:

Dear Administrator Oz:

We write with concern that the recent guidance issued to nursing homes by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) may intimidate nursing home staff from helping residents exercise their constitutional right to vote and ultimately prevent nursing home residents from voting. The nation’s 1.2 million nursing home residents face unique problems in obtaining access to the voting booth, and must not be denied their rights because they are disabled, elderly, lack transit, or face difficulties in obtaining a ballot or voting in person.

In October 2020, during the first Trump Administration, CMS issued a memo titled “Compliance with Residents’ Rights Requirement related to Nursing Home Residents’ Right to Vote.” The memo reminded nursing homes that CMS regulations require them to “support a resident in the exercise of their right … to vote, such as assisting with absentee or mail-in voting, or transporting residents to polling locations or ballot drop boxes in a safe manner.” The memo listed programs that nursing homes may operate in order to enable their residents to vote, and cited the specific CMS regulations articulating nursing homes’ responsibility to protect and facilitate residents’ right to vote by mail. The memo also stated that nursing homes must ensure residents voting by mail “have the right to receive and send their ballots via the U.S. Postal Service, or other authorized mechanism allowed by the State or locality.”

The Biden Administration renewed this guidance in September 2024. In the updated memo, CMS “reinforc[ed] the regulatory expectations” that nursing homes “affirm and support the right of residents to vote,” reiterated nursing homes’ responsibility to ensure residents can vote by mail, and cited the specific CMS regulations related to vote by mail.

However, on July 20, 2026, CMS issued a memo that appears to be an attempt to intimidate nursing home staff from assisting residents in the voting process. The newly released memo, titled “Protecting the Voting Rights and Autonomy of Vulnerable Residents in Long-Term Care (LTC) Facilities,” replaces language from CMS’s 2020 and 2024 guidance aimed at ensuring that facilities helped residents to vote with language threatening nursing home staff with prosecution for voter fraud. Specifically, the new memo removes suggestions of the specific ways nursing homes can facilitate voting and the references to CMS regulations related to voting by mail and instead baselessly emphasizes the risk that staff may exert “undue influence” on residents. The memo warns nursing home staff not to “violate federal or state voting laws” and reminds staff that “they cannot engage in inappropriate coercion or other violations of residents’ rights.” To reiterate this threat of investigation or prosecution, the July 2026 memo discusses two investigations of supposed election fraud occurring at nursing homes. However, no fraudulent votes were cast in either of these cases, and there is no evidence of any systemic or significant voter fraud or coercion in nursing homes.

CMS’s release of this memo is just the latest in a series of actions the Trump Administration has taken to restrict vote by mail and undermine the right to vote based on unfounded allegations of voter fraud tied to the President’s denial of prior valid election results. We are concerned that by highlighting examples of prior voter fraud investigations and threatening criminal penalties on nursing home staff—many of whom are legal immigrants who have already been targeted by Trump’s immigration policies—CMS’s July 2026 guidance may intimidate nursing home staff from helping residents with the voting process. And the removal of guidance on vote by mail procedures, combined with specific threats to investigate nursing home staff for assisting residents who are exercising their right to vote, may deter nursing homes from assisting residents with voting by mail. Ultimately, we are concerned that the changes to CMS’s guidance will result in the disenfranchisement of nursing home residents.

The right to vote is guaranteed by the Constitution to all adult Americans, including nursing home residents. And CMS regulations require that each nursing home resident “be supported by the facility in the exercise of his or her rights.” While CMS’s 2020 and 2024 guidance assisted nursing homes in carrying out that responsibility, we are concerned that CMS’s new guidance will hinder their ability to do so. In order to protect nursing home residents’ voting rights, we request that you immediately rescind the July 2026 memo and reinstate the 2020 and 2024 guidance.

Sincerely,

###

title: Reed & Amo Visit RI Builders Assoc. to Celebrate Housing Affordability Reform Law
text:
CENTRAL FALLS, RI – Today, U.S. Senator Jack Reed and Congressman Gabe Amo visited the Rhode Island Builders Association for a tour of its Residential Construction Training Facility and to celebrate passage of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (P.L. 119-101).

This law is the biggest housing package passed in decades, containing over 40 provisions to increase housing supply, lower housing costs, reduce barriers to construction, and unlock homeownership for more hardworking families.

“President Trump’s policies are making life unaffordable for many Americans who are getting squeezed by the high costs of homeownership and rent. The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act is a smart, overdue step toward lowering housing costs. It meets the scale of the housing crisis with urgency and takes critical steps to boost housing supply and reward communities that prioritize housing affordability best practices. This law is not a one-size-fits-all policy, nor should it be, because Rhode Island’s needs are different than Iowa’s, which are different from New York City’s needs. This law provides tools and incentives to help states and communities of all sizes tackle their respective housing challenges and enact smart housing policies while modernizing essential programs,” said Reed, a member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, who helped craft key portions of the landmark bipartisan housing legislation.

The ‘ROAD Act’ became law on July 11, 2026 – without President Trump’s signature – following passage and repassage from both the U.S. House of Representatives and U.S. Senate. President Trump allowed the measure to become law without his signature in protest of Congress’ failure to adopt his voter suppression ploy known as the so-called ‘SAVE Act.’

During today’s event, Senator Reed outlined several key benefits of the new housing law for Rhode Island and discussed the next steps of implementation and how it can advance housing opportunities locally. Reed noted key benefits for Rhode Island include streamlining federal regulations; increasing flexibility in federal grant programs such as CDBG and HOME that are allocated directly to local governments; and new benefits and support for communities working to ease their zoning and permitting rules.

Given the fact that Rhode Island features some of the oldest housing infrastructure in the country, Reed noted the bill also contains provisions to help families struggling with rising home-maintenance costs.

“President Trump’s tariffs have increased housing construction costs. Reversing them is one needed step. The ROAD Act also includes several bipartisan provisions I supported to expand housing supply, modernize the housing finance system, make homeownership more attainable, and limit the corporate buy-up of single-family units,” noted Reed, who had two of his bipartisan bills included in the law: the Property Improvement and Manufactured Housing Loan Modernization Act (S.964) that he wrote with Sen. Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) and the Helping More Families Save Act (S.970) that he led with Sen. Katie Britt (R-AL).

The ROAD Act also includes language Reed has long championed that kicks Wall Street out of the single-family home market – ensuring single-family homes are bought by families and local landlords, not deep-pocketed investors.

According to the National Association of Realtors’ (NAR) latest monthly report on home sales, due in large part to a dearth of housing supply, the median sales price of existing homes in the U.S. grew to $440,600, a record high. In Rhode Island, the median sale price is $550,000.

The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act would advance market-driven, local solutions to promote affordability by:

Providing technical assistance and competitive grants to help communities streamline zoning and permitting and build more housing;

Preventing Wall Street investors from buying up single-family homes that could go to families instead;

Creating an innovation fund for communities increasing housing supply;

Helping families living in federally-assisted housing build more savings and achieve greater economic independence;

Supporting housing opportunities for veterans, among other things;

Updating HUD’s HOME Investment Partnership Program, which hasn’t been reauthorized since 1992.

“The ROAD Act offers a ‘build more, preserve more, help people save more’ housing affordability blueprint. But it still requires a lot of work by communities to develop effective residential development strategies and housing solutions that meet their local needs. Here in the Ocean State, we must build more homes and apartments at price points Rhode Islanders can afford. This new law will help, but we must also continue to take a multi-faceted approach,” said Reed.

Over the past six years, Senator Reed has helped direct over $3.2 billion in federal funding to Rhode Island to address housing, including three key programs Reed helped create: the Housing Trust Fund, Capital Magnet Fund, and the State and Local Fiscal Recovery Fund, which the state used to pour $330 million into housing and homelessness programs.

title: Reed Statement on DOD Civilian Casualty Report
text:
WASHINGTON, DC—This week, the Department of Defense submitted to Congress its Section 1057 report, an annual accounting of civilian harm connected to U.S. military operations. In its 2025 report, the Department detailed civilian casualty incidents to include three strikes in Yemen — in Sanaa, at the Ras Isa fuel port, and near Saada — that killed 153 civilians and injured 243 more, with the April 17, 2025 strike on the Ras Isa terminal alone accounting for up to 80 deaths and 171 injuries.

These strikes in Yemen represented the deadliest U.S.-caused civilian casualty incidents in decades, until the Minab school strike in Iran in February 2026, where credible reports indicate at least 175 people, most of them children, were killed.

A copy of the DOD 1057 Report for 2025 is available here.

In response to this report, U.S. Senator Jack Reed (D-RI), the Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, issued the following statement:

“I am disturbed by this report and by the pattern it represents under Secretary Hegseth’s leadership. Under his watch, the Department of Defense killed at least 153 civilians and injured 243 more in the poorly conceived Yemen campaign in 2025.

“This did not happen in a vacuum. During his tenure, Secretary Hegseth has gutted the Civilian Protection Center of Excellence, pushed out senior JAG officers who advise commanders on the laws of war, and boasted about discarding what he calls ‘stupid rules of engagement.’ The same Yemen campaign that produced these casualties is the one where the DOD Inspector General found Secretary Hegseth shared classified strike details over Signal, putting the pilots flying that mission at risk.

“The Department has delayed this report for months and still has not submitted a separate accounting for the Minab school strike. Congress and the American people have waited long enough. I am demanding Secretary Hegseth appear before Congress to explain these incidents, account for the dismantling of civilian harm mitigation infrastructure across the Department, and commit to a firm date for the Minab report.

“Accountability for these losses is required by law and basic decency. Secretary Hegseth owes the families of these victims, our service members, and the American people a direct and honest reckoning.”

title: Ricketts Introduces Legislation to Improve Wildfire Response Efforts
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. –U.S. Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NE) recently introduced the Pilot for Regional Emergency Prepositioning of Aerial Resources and Equipment (PREPARE) Act. This legislation would establish prepositioned aerial resources during early-season conditions. It would increase preparedness and improve firefighting response efforts.

“When it comes to wildfires, response time matters,” said Senator Ricketts. “We must do more to protect our communities, ranches, and farms. Nebraska experienced devastating losses due to historic wildfires this year. This legislation would ensure aerial firefighting resources are ready to respond before fire strikes. It would limit response time and prevent damages to our farms, livestock, and communities. I will continue to fight to protect Nebraskans.”

The PREPARE Act would establish a pilot program for seasonal prepositioning protocols. This includes aerial suppression resources for early-season fine fuel wildland fires. The program would be directed at improving wildfire management response efforts. This would apply to Nebraska, Colorado, Kansas, South Dakota, and Wyoming.

The Nebraska Forest Service endorsed this legislation.

“Over the past several years, Nebraska has experienced some of the most challenging wildfire seasons in recent history,” said John Erixson, Nebraska State Forester. “Early-season grassfires, prolonged drought, and extreme fire weather have demonstrated that wildfires no longer respect traditional fire seasons. The PREPARE Act recognizes this reality by helping ensure aerial firefighting resources can be strategically positioned where they are needed most before conditions become critical. Investing in preparedness is one of the most effective ways to protect lives, communities, working lands, and natural resources.”

Recently, Senator Ricketts visited Fort Robinson State Park. He saw the wildfire damage that devastated Nebraska this year. He also met with the Crawford Volunteer Fire Department. He took the opportunity to thank firefighters for protecting our communities. They discussed opportunities to work together to provide the resources they need.

Watch highlights of Senator Ricketts’ visit here.

Background:

In early 2026, Nebraska experienced record-breaking wildfires—the worst we have seen in our state’s history. These devastating fires destroyed over a million acres of farmland in Nebraska.

title: Ricketts Supports the Protect College Sports Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Recently, U.S. Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NE) joined the Protect College Sports Act. This legislation would end the disorder facing college athletics by establishing nationwide standards for name, image, and likeness (NIL), transfers, eligibility, and enforcement.

“The Protect College Sports Act is a good step forward for athletics,” said Senator Ricketts. “This bipartisan bill addresses issues that were causing chaos in college sports, like eligibility requirements and NIL. These improvements will better support student athletes while preserving the tradition of college sports.”

In addition to Senator Ricketts, this bipartisan legislation is supported by Senators Cruz (R-TX), Cantwell (D-WA), Schmitt (R-MO), Coons (D-DE), Capito (R-WV), Hickenlooper (D-CO), and Welch (D-VT).

A national survey found that 81% of Americans believe the Protect College Sports Act would do more to protect student-athletes and preserve women’s and Olympic sports programs.

With the recent endorsement from the Big Ten, the Protect College Sports Act now has the backing of 28 collegiate athletic conferences, more than 370 colleges and universities across all 50 states and Washington, D.C, historically black colleges and universities, hundreds of thousands of student athletes, and President Trump.

title: Ahead of the High Holidays, Rosen Meets with Las Vegas Rabbis to Discuss Synagogue Security, Rising Antisemitism
text:
LAS VEGAS, NV – Ahead of the Jewish High Holidays next month, U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) met with rabbis from Southern Nevada to discuss the security issues impacting religious institutions. A report by the Anti-Defamation League (ADL) found that 2025 represents the third-highest year for antisemitic incidents, as well as the highest year for physical assaults against Jews since the ADL began tracking them in 1979. Many houses of worship, including synagogues, religious community centers, and other at-risk institutions, rely on FEMA’s Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) to pay for critical security upgrades. Senator Rosen recently introduced the bipartisan Jewish American Security Act (JASA), which would authorize $1 billion for the NSGP.

“Over the years, there has been an alarming and sharp increase in attacks on Jewish institutions and individuals — and the holiest time of year shouldn’t also be the scariest,” said Senator Rosen. “I’m grateful to the rabbis from across Southern Nevada who met with me to discuss how critical the Nonprofit Security Grant Program is for their congregations’ safety and security ahead of the High Holidays. I’ll keep pushing to increase funding for this critical program and for passage of my Jewish American Security Act.”

As co-founder and co-chair of the Senate Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism, Senator Rosen has been a leader in combating antisemitism and protecting Jewish American communities. She, along with Senator Lankford (R-OK), recently introduced the bipartisan Jewish American Security Act (JASA), a comprehensive bill to strengthen federal efforts to fight antisemitism – including in U.S. academic settings, at Jewish communal institutions, and online. Last year, Senator Rosen successfully pushed the Coast Guard to reverse course on a policy change that would have downgraded the classification of swastikas from hate symbols to “potentially divisive,” and reintroduced bipartisan legislation with Senator Lankford to strengthen Holocaust education at public schools and increase awareness of Holocaust educational resources available to local communities.

title: Rosen Helps Introduce Legislation to Better Connect Veterans with Benefits
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) joined Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV) in introducing legislation to make it easier for states to contact veterans about the benefits for which they may be eligible. The Empowering States to Serve Veterans Act would require the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to provide state veterans agencies with contact information for veterans residing in that state.

“States should be able to reach out directly to the veterans they serve so they can fully provide supplemental benefits and services parallel to those offered by the VA,” said Senator Rosen. “This bill will tackle administrative hurdles and streamline processes, making it easier for state and federal agencies to work together effectively and get our veterans the support they need.”

Senator Rosen has consistently fought for Nevada’s veterans, ensuring that they have access to the resources and benefits they have earned. Senator Rosen is leading the charge in Congress to secure benefits for veterans who served at the Nevada Test and Training Range during the nuclear testing era and were exposed to toxins, but have been denied benefits despite their civilian counterparts receiving support. Earlier this year, she successfully pushed the Trump Administration to reverse a rule that could have decreased benefits for disabled veterans. Senator Rosen has also helped introduce bipartisan legislation to cut red tape and streamline the process for medical practitioners who work with both the Department of Defense and VA to help eliminate delays in patient care.

title: NEWS: Schiff, Padilla & Congressional Democrats Demand FTA and OMB Stop Holding Blue State Infrastructure Funding Hostage
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.) joined Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and 39 Democratic colleagues in demanding the Trump Administration stop delaying the advancement of public transportation projects funded by the Capital Investment Grants (CIG) program. Currently, the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) has access to more than $1.9 billion in unobligated and unallocated funds ready to be spent. However, the Trump Administration continues to hold up significant projects in blue states while red states’ projects move ahead.

In a letter to FTA Acting Deputy Administrator Mathew Cahill and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Administrator Russel Vought, the lawmakers expressed concern over delays that have created a backlog in transit projects and called out the Administration for potentially holding up funding for political reasons. Last month, the Trump Administration admitted to terminating funding for projects in states that did not vote for the President.

“We have watched for months as the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) have stonewalled the progress of worthy transit projects while President Trump and Department of Transportation Secretary Duffy are proclaiming a commitment to a ‘golden age of transportation,’” wrote the lawmakers.

“The growing backlog of projects in limbo due to FTA and OMB inaction is unacceptable,” continued the lawmakers. “We are very concerned that delaying the CIG project pipeline, while advancing only the Utah project, is potentially rooted in partisan political considerations, which could further violate statutory requirements.”

“Every $1 invested in transit generates $5 in long-term economic value. Conversely, failing to deliver on long-promised transit investment carries serious economic consequences,” wrote the lawmakers. “Should this egregious trend continue, 11 projects in 10 states…that anticipate signing a CIG grant agreement this year could be subjected to senseless delay.”

The lawmakers concluded by reminding the administrators of the historically bipartisan nature of CIG-funded projects and demanded that their agencies immediately advance the stalled projects — regardless of a state’s 2024 election results.

Schiff and Padilla have long been advocates for investment in California transportation infrastructure and have fought against the Trump Administration’s harmful intentional delays on transportation projects. Last month, Schiff and Padilla announced $53.8 million from the Department of Transportation (DOT) to repair highways and roads across California.

The full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear Director Vought and Acting Deputy Administrator Cahill,

We write to express deep concern regarding reports that your agencies are delaying the advancement of public transportation projects within the Capital Investment Grants (CIG) pipeline. As members of the Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs and House Transportation and Infrastructure Committees and as members of the House and Senate representing affected projects, we have an obligation to ensure that the CIG program is carried out in accordance with statutory requirements that have been enacted to ensure that taxpayer resources are not wasted as a result of delay by the federal government. We have watched for months as the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) have stonewalled the progress of worthy transit projects while President Trump and Department of Transportation Secretary Duffy are proclaiming a commitment to a “golden age of transportation.” We would like to remind you that such a vision is woefully incomplete if it does not include delivering CIG projects that will provide fast, frequent and reliable transit service across the nation.

The growing backlog of projects in limbo due to FTA and OMB inaction is unacceptable. Since last fall, your agencies have neglected to advance the Boston Green Line Transformation project, the Los Angeles Southeast Gateway Line and the Salt Lake City region’s Frontrunner 2X project into the CIG Engineering phase—without justification for the delay. Last week, FTA moved the Utah project into Engineering, a welcome development, but the two other projects remain stalled.

This delay is occurring despite the fact that FTA currently has access to more than $1.9 billion in unobligated and unallocated funds that are available to support CIG projects, and Congress has consistently appropriated new funds each year to the CIG program. The Frontrunner 2X project has already been allocated $594 million of CIG funding, and based on FTA’s commitment at Engineering entry last week, the project will need only $693 million of additional CIG program funds.

We wish to remind you that the projects in Boston, Los Angeles and Salt Lake City have all completed a comprehensive rating process pursuant to the CIG program guidance that was most recently updated by FTA in November of 2025, under President Trump’s administration. Each of the three projects received an overall project rating that qualified them to enter the Engineering phase and later receive a Full Funding Grant Agreement. In fact, the projects in Boston and Los Angeles received an overall higher rating of “medium-high,” compared to the “medium” overall rating of the Utah project.

FTA and OMB should advance all projects that meet statutory criteria, and your agencies should not impose any further delays. Under the most recently enacted appropriations law and prior appropriations laws, FTA, OMB and the Administration are prohibited from using any federal funds to “impede or hinder project advancement or approval for any project seeking a Federal contribution from the capital investment grants program of greater than 40 percent of project costs,” which includes the delayed projects. We are very concerned that delaying the CIG project pipeline, while advancing only the Utah project, is potentially rooted in partisan political considerations, which could further violate statutory requirements.

We are frustrated by reports that OMB is partially responsible for these avoidable and costly delays. As a result of these stalling tactics, there has not been a single new CIG grant agreement signed since this Administration took office. Should this egregious trend continue, 11 projects in 10 states (California, Florida, Maryland, Minnesota, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina, Utah, Washington and Wisconsin) that anticipate signing a CIG grant agreement this year could be subjected to senseless delay. No Administration since 1993 has failed to sign a single CIG grant agreement in the first year: we urge you not to set a new record by failing to sign CIG grant agreements for two years in a row.

Unnecessary delays are not only frustrating; they are economically short-sighted. Transit is an excellent investment. Every $1 invested in transit generates $5 in long-term economic value. Conversely, failing to deliver on long-promised transit investment carries serious economic consequences. Project sponsors and taxpayers will end up footing the bill for delay-induced cost increases. The construction workforce and the broader transportation supply chain are left waiting for critical job-creating investments. In the interim, people have fewer choices to get around their community. The impact of trips not taken to work, to school, or to the doctor undermines economic growth.

Transportation policy is generally bipartisan, and we are proud of this reputation. Through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, Congress re-committed to a multimodal federal transportation program. Every year, Congress reiterates a bipartisan commitment to CIG through the annual appropriations process. We stand ready and willing to continue making robust federal investments in infrastructure on the scale that our country desperately needs. However, any effort to impede or hinder CIG projects does serious harm to the bipartisan coalition that supports federal infrastructure investment. Congress must be confident that the CIG program will be executed in accordance with the law. Any delay or hindrance in delivering CIG projects further undermines our confidence that this Administration will faithfully execute the law.

Many of us represent communities with CIG projects that are currently impacted or could soon be impacted by your agencies’ actions. We request that you immediately advance the two stalled projects in California and Massachusetts into Engineering and prevent further program obstruction or delays. Please respond in writing, not later than August 18, 2026, with your timeline to advance the two projects into the next phase of CIG. Going forward, we request that you expeditiously approve projects that are eligible for a Full Funding or Small Starts Grant Agreement, including the 11 projects seeking grant agreements later this year. Investing in transit projects through the CIG program is essential to building a transportation system that works for everyone.

title: Senator Schmitt’s Bipartisan Bill to Construct Memorial Honoring EMS Professionals Passes U.S. Senate, Heads to President’s Desk
text:
U.S. SENATE — Today, U.S Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) celebrated the passage of his bipartisan bill to extend the National Emergency Services Memorial Foundation’s authority to construct a national memorial in Washington, D.C. paying tribute to the heroism, courage, and enduring sacrifice of Emergency Medical Services (EMS) professionals who have fallen in the line of duty and honoring those who continue to serve. This extension gives the Foundation additional time to complete the memorial, ensuring that EMS professionals are permanently recognized in our nation’s capital with the respect they deserve.

“This isn’t about politics—it’s about honor. EMS professionals in Missouri, and across the United States work tirelessly, often putting themselves in harm’s way for the communities they serve. Thanks to this bipartisan legislation, the United States is keeping our promise that their fallen brothers and sisters, their courage, and their sacrifices are permanently dignified with a monument deserving of the heroism they’ve shown,” said Senator Schmitt. “I’m proud to have led this effort to ensure that future generations of Americans will never forget the brave men and women who ran towards danger, not away from it.”

The original bill, titled the National Emergency Medical Services Commemorative Work Act, was signed into law by President Trump in 2018 and authorized the National Emergency Medical Services Memorial Foundation to establish a commemorative work on federal land in D.C. within seven years of enactment. Instead of using taxpayer dollars, the memorial is fully funded by Foundation, with any surplus funds returned to the federal government once the project is complete.

Senator Schmitt led this bipartisan legislation alongside Senator Chris Coons (D-DE) to extend the authorization’s deadline, which expired in 2025, through 2032.

Senators Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-LA), Cynthia Lummis (R-WY), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and John Hickenlooper (D-CO) co-sponsored this legislation. A companion bill in the House of Representatives was led by Rep. Richard Hudson (R-N.C.) and Rep. Stephen Lynch (D-Mass.).

The bill was endorsed by the National Association of Emergency Medical Technicians (NAEMT), the American Ambulance Association (AAA), and the International Association of EMS Chiefs (IAEMSC).

Read the full bill HERE.

Statements of Support:

“Our country’s paramedics, EMTs and emergency medical service professionals provide patients with life-saving medical care and deserve to be recognized with a memorial in our Nation’s Capital. We profoundly appreciate the successful efforts of Senators Schmitt and Coons in steering the passage of legislation to reauthorize the National EMS Memorial. With this victory, we now look forward to the next steps in making the memorial a reality,” said Jamie Pafford-Gresham, President of American Ambulance Association.

“This is great news. We are thankful for Senator Schmitt’s and Senator Coons’ strong leadership and support in our effort to reauthorize the National EMS Memorial Foundation. This reauthorization allows us to continue the important work to establish a permanent memorial in the nation’s capital to honor the commitment, service and sacrifice of all of us in EMS. It is an honor to serve our fellow Americans, and we are proud to have maintained their trust as we work through the next steps in the processes outlined in the Commemorative Works Act,” said Bob Morley, President of the National Emergency Medical Service Memorial Foundation.

“NAEMT applauds Senator Chris Coons (D-DE) and Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) for securing passage of a foundational bipartisan bill (S. 2546/H.R. 2196) extending the deadline for the National Emergency Medical Services Memorial Foundation to establish a national memorial in Washington, D.C. honoring America’s EMS professionals. This critical extension ensures the nation’s EMS workforce — whose courage, sacrifice, and service have protected communities for generations — receives the long-overdue recognition it deserves in the nation’s Capital. Every year, more than 850,000 EMS professionals respond to over 30 million emergency calls and care for approximately 22 million patients nationwide, often at the most critical moments in people’s lives. As a cornerstone of the nation’s emergency response system, EMS personnel stand on the front lines of public safety and national preparedness, responding without hesitation to local emergencies, terrorist attacks, natural disasters, and other large-scale crises. Serving in both the public and private sectors as career and volunteer providers, these men and women are an indispensable part of America’s healthcare system, homeland security infrastructure, and national security readiness. Their unwavering commitment to saving lives deserves permanent recognition and honor,” said Chief Chris Way, President of the National Association of Emergency Medical Technicians (NAEMT).

“Our country’s paramedics, EMTs and emergency medical service professionals provide patients with life-saving medical care and deserve to be recognized with a memorial in our Nation’s Capitol. We profoundly appreciate the successful efforts of Senators Schmitt and Coons in steering the passage of legislation to reauthorize the National EMS Memorial. With this victory, we now look forward to the next steps in making the memorial a reality,” said Jamie Pafford-Gresham, President of the American Ambulance Association.

title: FOLLOWING HIS PUSH, SCHUMER ANNOUNCES NATIONAL PARK SERVICE RELEASES OPERATING FUNDS TO BUFFALO’S THEODORE ROOSEVELT INAUGURAL NATIONAL HISTORIC SITE
text:
Schumer Called On NPS To Release Congressionally-Approved Funds When Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural National Historic Site Was The Last Site To Receive Annual Operating Budget

Following his push, U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer today released a statement announcing that the National Park Service (NPS) has released this year's annual federal funds for Buffalo’s Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural Site. Schumer said this funding is vital so the site can cover its bills, pay staff, and ensure the public can continue to access one of Western New York’s treasured historical sites.

“The Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural Site holds a special place in the hearts of Buffalonians. That’s why, when I found out it was the only unit in the entire National Park System that had not received its funding, I called on the NPS to release it immediately. Today, I’m proud to announce that the NPS heeded my call and has released the funding,” said Senator Schumer. “As the home of the place where President Roosevelt took the oath of office to become our 26th president, and where President McKinley tragically died, Buffalo plays a critical role in the story of a presidency that reshaped the country. As we celebrate America’s 250th birthday this year, I will keep fighting to ensure New York’s rich history is accessible to the public for generations to come.”

Earlier this month, Schumer called on the NPS to release the site’s funds without further delay and asked why this site was the only NPS site without its annual federal funding and what the NPS will do to ensure a delay like this never happens again.

title: SCHUMER, GILLIBRAND, RILEY ANNOUNCE $6.5 MILLION FOR ITHACA TOMPKINS INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT TO BUILD NEW SNOW REMOVAL EQUIPMENT FACILITY
text:
Lawmakers Explain That, As We Prepare For Winter, It Is Important To Ensure Our Airports Have Infrastructure Needed To Keep Passengers And Equipment Safe

Schumer Has Long History Of Delivering For Ithaca Tompkins International Airport, Providing Critical Fed Funding For Key Infrastructure Upgrades Including New Boarding Bridge, Snow Removal, Emergency Vehicles, High-Tech Baggage Screening System, And More
