title: Van Hollen Joins Hirono, Colleagues, in Raising Alarms About Increased Naturalization Fees
text:
Today, U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) joined Senator Mazie K. Hirono (D-Hawaii), a senior member of the Senate Committee on the Judiciary who is a Naturalized Citizen, and 10 of their Democratic Senate colleagues in pressing the Trump Administration on their recent proposed rule to increase naturalization fees and remove reduced fee options and fee waivers for those attempting to become citizens. In a letter to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) Director Joseph B. Edlow, the senators raised alarms about how the proposed fee increases would limit citizenship for thousands of immigrants.

“USCIS’s actions have repeatedly increased the burden of and difficulty in obtaining U.S. citizenship,” wrote the senators. “Naturalization is a critical pathway to immigrant integration, civic engagement, and democratic participation, yet your agency’s actions represent a significant departure from these values.”

Under the Trump Administration’s proposed rule, immigrants seeking U.S. citizenship would face hundreds of dollars of fee increases, up to 80 percent more. Immigrants seeking a hearing on naturalization proceedings would also face an up to 83 percent fee increase. Additionally, the proposed rule eliminates preexisting reduced-fee options and fee waivers, designed to help immigrants achieve citizenship no matter their financial status. In their letter, the senators highlighted how the proposed rule burdens the pathway to citizenship without providing clear guidance about how access will be preserved for immigrants who are unable to meet the increased financial threshold.

“While your agency asserts that the increased fees are necessary to recover the full cost of adjudicating naturalization applications and to support enhanced screening and vetting measures, it fails to address the increased fees’ deterrent effect on eligible applicants, particularly those from low-income communities,” the senators continued.

Despite the Trump Administration’s consistent claims that it supports legal immigration, the senators highlighted how the naturalization fee increase will have the opposite effect. In addition to the proposed fees, UCSIS has also increased the difficulty of the civics test required to become citizens and eliminated the Citizenship Integration and Grant Program designed to help immigrants navigate the process.

In their letter, the senators demanded prompt responses to explain the agency’s methodology when electing to increase naturalization fees, the anticipated impact of these fee increases on lawful permanent residents’ abilities to become naturalized citizens, and the changes in the naturalization process that necessitated the increased fees.

The letter was also signed by Senators Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Dick Durbin (D-Ill.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), and Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.).

The full text of the letter is available here and below.

Dear Director Edlow:

We write regarding the proposed rule issued by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) on June 23, 2026. That proposed rule would substantially increase naturalization fees and eliminate the reduced-fee option and fee waivers. These changes will place U.S. citizenship out of reach for many low-income lawful permanent residents who are otherwise eligible to naturalize.

Under the proposed rule, an applicant seeking U.S. citizenship would face fee increases of up to 80 percent and up to an 83 percent increase for a hearing on a decision in naturalization proceedings. The proposed rule would also eliminate both the reduced-fee option and the fee-waiver provision for non-military applicants. While your agency asserts that the increased fees are necessary to recover the full cost of adjudicating naturalization applications and to support enhanced screening and vetting measures, it fails to address the increased fees’ deterrent effect on eligible applicants, particularly those from low-income communities. The proposed rule does not demonstrate that USCIS considered applicants' reliance interests, evaluated reasonable alternatives that would preserve access to naturalization, or adequately justified why naturalization applicants should bear the costs of expanded adjudicatory processes.

USCIS’s actions have repeatedly increased the burden of and difficulty in obtaining U.S. citizenship. In addition to these proposed fees, your agency increased the difficulty of the civics test that individuals must take to become citizens. You also eliminated the Citizenship and Integration Grant Program that helps immigrants navigate the process. Naturalization is a critical pathway to immigrant integration, civic engagement, and democratic participation, yet your agency’s actions represent a significant departure from these values.

To fulfill our Congressional oversight responsibilities, we respectfully request that you provide written answers to the following questions by August 25th:

What analysis did your agency conduct regarding the impact of moving from an ability-to-pay framework to a strict beneficiary-pays model? Please include any analysis your agency conducted on the broader public benefits of naturalization, the equity implications, and how these factors were weighed in establishing the proposed fees.

What analysis did your agency conduct regarding the anticipated impact of the proposed fee increases on low-income communities? Please include any estimates of how many otherwise eligible lawful permanent residents may be unable to apply for naturalization or may delay filing as a result of the fee increases. Please also provide any assessment of the impacts on legal service providers, community-based organizations, and other stakeholders assisting applicants with the naturalization process.

What specific pre- and post-approval screening and vetting processes are needed by the agency for naturalization adjudications that necessitated the increased fees? Please also include the following:

The authority requiring such processes, including whether the additional processing is required by a specific Executive Order, statute, or policy change within the agency;

Whether and how these processes are authorized to be funded through Immigration Examinations Fee Account (IEFA) funds;

The costs associated with each process;

Whether those costs are directly attributable to individual naturalization adjudications; and

What alternatives were considered by the agency before proposing the fee increases.

What USCIS personnel responsible for naturalization adjudication and processing have been terminated, reassigned, or otherwise removed since January 2025? Of that number, how many positions have been refilled? Please also detail any reductions in USCIS funding or resources related to application processing, backlog reduction, or naturalization adjudications since January 2025.

We should not price citizenship outside the reach of immigrants; instead, we should explore ways to encourage individuals to fulfill the American Dream. If you have any questions, please reach out to my staff.

title: Whitehouse, Grassley Issue Statement on Treasury Department’s Final Rule Dismantling Key Element of Corporate Transparency Act
text:
Whitehouse & Grassley helped pass groundbreaking law to prevent abuse of U.S. incorporation laws

Washington, DC – U.S. Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) and Chuck Grassley (R-IA) today released the following statement on the U.S. Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s (FinCEN’s) decision to permanently exempt over 99 percent of entities previously required to report their beneficial ownership information under the Corporate Transparency Act (CTA). Congress passed the CTA on a strongly bipartisan basis to clamp down on criminals and foreign enemies hiding assets from U.S. law enforcement, national security officials, and tax authorities. The CTA is widely considered the most important anti-money laundering law in decades.

“The Treasury Department’s final rule exempting U.S. based companies from the Corporate Transparency Act’s reporting requirements undermines the clear intent of the law. The Act gave the federal government needed tools to address criminal activity like human trafficking, terrorist financing, drug distribution, sanctions evasion, and more without unduly burdening legitimate commercial entities. This decision is an unfortunate one that fails to use all available tools to protect Americans and crack down on illicit financial schemes.”

The CTA was designed to play an important role in protecting national security and public safety by providing law enforcement and national security officials with the names of the true owners (“beneficial ownership information”) of U.S. corporations and other legal entities. This information facilitates the government’s efforts to combat various forms of illicit finance carried out through shell and front companies.

In March 2025, the Treasury Department announced that it would not enforce the CTA’s beneficial ownership information reporting rule when it comes to U.S. citizens or domestic reporting companies, and would issue a new proposed rulemaking that would narrow the scope of the rule to foreign reporting companies only. A few weeks later, the Department published an interim final rule eliminating reporting requirements for more than 99 percent of corporations and LLCs that were previously required to report, as directed by Congress. This week’s final rule makes permanent the sweeping exemptions and deletes all beneficial ownership information data that domestic companies had already submitted.

Whitehouse and Grassley were the original sponsors of the TITLE Act, the precursor to the Corporate Transparency Act. The CTA passed as part of the FY2021 National Defense Authorization Act after more than a decade of bipartisan congressional deliberation, and was supported by a wide range of government, anti-corruption groups, human rights organizations, faith communities, financial institutions, and real estate organizations.

title: Wyden, Colleagues Demand State Department Process Student Visas Without Delays
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Ron Wyden said today he has joined Senate colleagues to express concern about the lack of student and exchange visitor visa appointments in time for the start of the academic year in Oregon and nationwide.

Wyden and his fellow senators demanded the Trump administration answer questions about delays processing these applications at U.S. embassies and consulates.

“We urge the State Department to ensure timely processing of F, M, and J student and exchange visitor nonimmigrant visas, consistent with the approach taken by administrations of both parties in the past, and to implement other measures to avoid diminishing U.S. competitiveness,” the senators wrote. “Specifically, we are hearing from constituents and stakeholders that no timely visa appointments are available for students at some embassies and consulates. This only exacerbates uncertainty about whether students’ visas will be processed in time for them to travel to the United States to begin their studies.”

The lawmakers highlighted the vital contributions international students make to universities and communities nationwide, including expanding opportunities for American students, generating economic activity, strengthening the U.S. workforce, and building international partnerships.

“International students are critical to the success of our universities, including contributing nearly $43 billion annually to local communities and supporting more than 355,000 American jobs during the 2024-2025 academic year. Even though international students make up only six percent of the total higher education population, their enrollment creates opportunities for American students,” the senators continued. “International students also improve our national security by fostering global relationships, cross cultural understanding, and long-lasting diplomatic ties. These benefits are at risk if visa processing delays persist.”

The senators urged the State Department to ensure the timely review and processing of student and exchange visitor visas, extend interview waivers for vetted returning student applicants, provide sufficient staffing for visa processing, and improve transparency and engagement with stakeholders. The senators also requested an explanation within 30 days about the causes of the delays and the measures being implemented to ensure student and exchange visitor visa applications are processed in a timely manner moving forward.

title: Barrett Hears About Agriculture, Education, and Transportation During Week of Meetings Across Mid-Michigan
text:
Lansing, Mich. — Congressman Tom Barrett (MI-07) this week met with hardworking mid-Michiganders in agriculture, education, and transportation to hear from them about the issues that matter to their families and local businesses.

Throughout the week, Barrett toured local farms, held a roundtable discussion on free and fair agricultural trade, learned about research on crops and mobility technology at Michigan State University, visited a tutoring center, and hosted U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy for conversations about infrastructure and transportation.

“Meeting directly with mid-Michiganders, seeing their work firsthand, and hearing about their needs is the most important part of my job,” said Barrett. “This week, I appreciated listening to farmers, educators, scientists studying crop diseases and developing vehicles, local transportation leaders, and other hardworking residents. These helpful and informative discussions enable me to better represent the people of our communities and make sure their voices are heard in Washington.”

On Monday, Barrett visited Certain League Farms in Williamston and met with Mike and Roseann Bills, who raise asparagus, sunflowers, corn, horses, and puppies. The Billses have a daughter with special needs, and they founded the farm with a vision to offer adults with special needs the opportunity to reach their full potential and work a job that gives them dignity and purpose.

Barrett then visited the Plant Pathology Field Laboratory at Michigan State University and met with scientists who are conducting critical research to help farmers across mid-Michigan and the United States manage and mitigate crop diseases.

On Tuesday, Barrett met with Michigan farmers and agricultural industry leaders at AgroLiquid in St. Johns for a roundtable discussion hosted by Farmers for Free Trade. They discussed trade policy and priorities for the administration’s negotiations around extending the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA).

Barrett then attended AgroExpo, an annual outdoor farm show in St. Johns, where he met with local residents participating in the event. AgroExpo brought together farmers, manufacturers, and others to make connections, showcase their work, and continue advancing the future of Michigan agriculture.

Barrett next attended Michigan State University’s Mobility Summit in East Lansing. He met with educators, students, and other researchers and addressed attendees about his work to invest in infrastructure and promote innovation that will ensure Michigan’s universities and industries continue leading in developing the next generation of transportation technology. He also highlighted the federal investment in autonomous vehicle research he secured on behalf of MSU.

On Wednesday, Barrett visited Sylvan Learning of Brighton, where Jessica and George Rollins shared about the tutoring and support their educators provide for local students.

On Thursday, Barrett welcomed U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy to Lansing for a discussion with local transportation and infrastructure leaders, a tour of the Capital Region International Airport, and a visit to Dean Transportation.

On Friday, Barrett toured Two Sparrows Farm in Eaton Rapids, where Dan and Whitney Belprez raise livestock. Their first-generation family farm is especially focused on providing healthy meat and milk to mid-Michigan families.

title: Bilirakis to Host Affordable Housing Fair in Pasco County
text:
-Event will connect residents with resources and information to help make housing more affordable-

PASCO COUNTY, FL – Congressman Gus Bilirakis will host an Affordable Housing Fair on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. to connect Pasco County residents with resources, programs, and information aimed at helping families navigate the rising cost of housing and homeownership.

“Whether you are looking to purchase your first home, struggling with rising housing, electric or insurance costs, or simply trying to find an affordable place to live, I want to make sure you know about the resources that may be available to help,” said Congressman Bilirakis. “Housing affordability continues to be one of the most significant challenges facing families in our community. I am committed to pursuing solutions at the federal level while also bringing resources directly to the people I represent.”

Bilirakis has worked alongside local leaders to secure federal investments that expand affordable housing opportunities and support some of the community’s most vulnerable residents. These investments include:

$7.2 million for affordable senior housing in West Pasco, helping expand housing options for seniors, many of whom are living on fixed incomes.

$4 million for Magnolia Oaks, a new affordable housing community designed to serve at-risk Veterans.

$4 million for Vincent House’s innovative housing initiatives, which support adults living with serious mental illness and help provide greater stability and independence.

Beyond these local investments, Bilirakis has championed bipartisan legislation to address the housing affordability crisis on a national level. He has supported measures including the Saving the American Dream Act, the More Homes on the Market Act, and, most recently, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which has become law. Together, these commonsense reforms seek to address some of the underlying factors driving housing costs by increasing the supply of affordable housing, reducing unnecessary regulatory barriers that make construction more expensive, lowering barriers to renting and purchasing a home, and expanding opportunities for homeownership.

“Housing affordability affects every generation,” Bilirakis said. “Whether you are a senior on a fixed income, a Veteran returning home, a first-time homebuyer, or a family struggling with rising insurance costs, we have to pursue practical solutions that address both the immediate pressures families are facing and the long-term factors driving housing costs higher.”

Recognizing that Florida’s property insurance crisis is placing additional pressure on homeowners, Bilirakis has also introduced legislation that would provide a $10,000 federal tax credit for Florida homeowners to help offset the skyrocketing cost of property insurance.

Additionally, Bilirakis supported $585 million in federal disaster assistance for Pasco County to help families and communities recover from recent devastating hurricanes. These resources are helping homeowners rebuild, repair damaged properties, and strengthen homes and communities against future disasters. Bilirakis is also a proud co-sponsor of the HELPER Act, legislation designed to help teachers, law enforcement officers, firefighters, and other critical community workers overcome one of the biggest barriers to homeownership: the cost of a down payment. The measure would help these essential workers afford to live in the communities they serve.

“Families should not have to choose between paying their insurance premium, putting food on the table, or keeping a roof over their heads,”Bilirakis continued. “There is no single solution to the housing affordability crisis, which is why we need to attack the problem from every angle. We need to build more housing, remove unnecessary barriers that increase costs, help more existing homes come onto the market, address Florida’s property insurance crisis, and make it easier for hardworking families and essential workers to achieve the American Dream of homeownership. This Affordable Housing Fair is another important part of that effort. It is about making sure our neighbors have access to practical information and resources that can help them right now, while I continue fighting for long-term solutions in Congress.”

Residents interested in learning more about affordable housing initiatives and programs that may be available to assist them are encouraged to attend.

title: Ciscomani Wraps Up District Work Week Focused on Delivering Results for Arizona’s Sixth District
text:
Tucson, AZ - U.S. Representative Juan Ciscomani today wrapped up another busy week of back-to-back events in Arizona’s 6th Congressional District, highlighting the federal funds he’s secured for critical community projects, meeting with constituents and speaking at a naturalization ceremony for new American citizens.

The congressman saw firsthand how the funds he’s secured through the congressional Community Project Funding program will benefit Huachuca City, Benson, and Marana by supporting key public safety, health care and transportation projects.

He also met with students from underserved communities who received scholarships from the Lapin Sunshine Foundation and presented certificates to recipients of the American Dream Inspirational Educator Awards at the Casa Grande Union High School District.

"The best part of the job is meeting and connecting with constituents and hearing directly from the people I have the privilege of representing," said Rep. Ciscomani. "From spending time in Huachuca City, Benson, and Marana to discuss the critical funding preliminarily secured for their communities, to attending community events in Sierra Vista, Casa Grande, and Oro Valley to celebrate the exceptional people that make up our district, this work week was especially productive. From my first day in office, I have focused on delivering real results for Arizona’s Sixth District through means such as Community Project Funding and meaningful partnership with local leaders and groups. I’m grateful for the opportunity to hear directly from the people of our district, and I look forward to continuing to turn their priorities into results."

Rep. Ciscomani has preliminarily secured $1.3 million for Huachuca City Fire Department, $2 million for Benson Hospital, and $3 million for improvements to the Marana Traffic Interchange. Each project would greatly benefit the surrounding communities and provide much-needed support by responding to unique local needs and priorities.

As the only member of the Arizona delegation who is an appropriator, Rep. Ciscomani has fought to secure critical funding for local communities throughout his time in Congress. The funding he has preliminarily secured for Huachuca City, Benson, and Marana are among a total of $42.7 million for 20 Community Project Funding (CPF) requests for Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27), building on the $60 million he secured for 28 CPFs between FY24 and FY26.

Read more about the funding secured by the congressman in FY24 and FY26 HERE and HERE.

This week, the congressman also attended Pinal Partnership’s monthly breakfast to discuss federal funding and toured the Chiricahua Community Health Center in Benson, which plays a vital role in delivering critical health care to the local rural community. Additionally, he connected with local business leaders at the 2026 SPARK Business Summit.

To round out the week, Rep. Ciscomani attended a naturalization ceremony in Tucson, where he shared his story of becoming a United States citizen 20 years ago and his experience of the American Dream. He also spent time with some of our nation’s most distinguished veterans, The Friday Pilots.

The congressman is grateful for the many productive and meaningful conversations had throughout this district work week and looks forward to continuing his partnership with these local leaders and organizations as he works to deliver tangible results for Arizona’s 6th District.

title: Crow Demands Answers from Pentagon about Conditions Aboard USS Abraham Lincoln
text:
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a former paratrooper and Army Ranger who serves on the House Armed Services Committee, is demanding answers from Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao on horrible conditions reported aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln. The aircraft carrier has been at sea for more than 260 consecutive days, breaking the record for most consecutive days at sea in modern U.S. naval history. Disturbing reports have emerged about food shortages, broken toilets, lack of basic supplies, and limited port access. Reports also indicate major mental health challenges among sailors, including multiple attempts to jump overboard.

Crow was joined in the letter to Cao by Congressman Joe Courtney (D-CT) and 50 other House Democrats.

“The strain being put on our sailors and their families is completely unacceptable. It’s not only hurting the health and well-being of our servicemembers, it's affecting military readiness and making us less safe,” said Congressman Crow. “Donald Trump has shown time and time again that he does not care about our servicemembers. The President owes our servicemembers, their families, and the American people a plan to end his reckless war with Iran.”

Crow, Courtney, and their colleagues wrote that the challenges with the USS Lincoln “have become a pattern in the Administration’s handling of its war against Iran… The reported conditions on the Lincoln…leave both Congress and the public concerned that the Department is not adapting quickly enough to the conditions in the CENTCOM area of responsibility, nor taking the appropriate steps to mitigate the continued challenges in our fleet.”

They call on Cao to explain measures being taken to ensure the safety of sailors, the effects caused by resource strain, and the communication from the Department that families of those aboard can anticipate, among other issues. They also ask Cao to clarify whether the Department considers there to be a food shortage or chronic hygiene issues aboard the Lincoln.

Crow has repeatedly condemned Trump’s illegal war of choice in Iran. His War Powers Resolution with Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal (D-WA) to disapprove of the war recently passed the U.S. House, and Crow continues to lead legislation to prohibit federal funding for the war. As someone from a working class family who served three combat tours in Iraq and Afghanistan, Crow has seen firsthand the toll forever wars have cost servicemembers and hardworking Americans.

A PDF of the letter can be found here, with full text appearing below:

Dear Secretary Cao:

We write to express deep concern for the personnel and material readiness of the USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) and request information on the ship’s deployment and future. The Lincoln and her crew have been deployed for more than 8 months, twice extended and still performing at a high level under constant combat conditions. The carrier deployed from San Diego on November 21, 2025, and was originally scheduled to return from deployment in May. Carrier crews are always prepared for extended deployments at sea due to potential operational requirements. However, this crew has been extended multiple times and is still deployed in a combat zone 3 months after their originally scheduled return date – with no anticipated redeployment date in sight. Furthermore, the Lincoln has reportedly only pulled into port twice since deploying, once in December 2025 and a second time for a one-day port call in July 2026. This 208-day period without pulling into port was a modern-day record and uncharted territory for a Navy aircraft carrier and her crew. We recognize the severe logistical challenges that come with operating in a warzone. We also note that these challenges, including the inability to make port calls as frequently and the increased mental strain on sailors in a war environment, should be foreseeable and actions should be taken to mitigate the effects to the extent possible.

Like the USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78) before it, the Lincoln’s extended deployment is accompanied by deeply troubling reports about sailors’ mental health and living conditions. These reports are not political conjecture; they come from sailors’ worried family members. Numerous sailors have reportedly attempted to jump overboard, in an escalation of challenges the Ford faced. In one instance, the wife of one of these sailors initially received a call from the carrier’s ombudsman but has not received more information from the Navy in the last few weeks. Other family members have sounded the alarm on food shortages or quality issues since April. These concerns reached fever pitch at an August 6 townhall in San Diego, where they were raised by family members of the Lincoln’s crew to Acting Secretary Cao and other Navy leadership. Navy leadership took the appropriate step in meeting to address families’ concerns, but there remains more to be done to ensure that the families and the public have faith that these sailors are being taken care of and that the Department is appropriately managing the fleet and its readiness for Operation Epic Fury.

The Ford and Lincoln’s successive overextended deployments and subsequent challenges have become a pattern in the Administration’s handling of its war against Iran. As of August 13, the USS George Washington (CVN-73) is reported to replace the Lincoln at some point in the future.3 The reported conditions on the Lincoln, following so soon after the reported conditions on the Ford, leave both Congress and the public concerned that the Department is not adapting quickly enough to the conditions in the CENTCOM area of responsibility, nor taking the appropriate steps to mitigate the continued challenges in our fleet. As such, we urge the Department to continue communicating with these sailors’ families and the appropriate congressional committees, and we respectfully request the following information:

What additional resources is the Department providing for sailors who are serving under more difficult conditions on extended deployments?

What additional measures are being taken to ensure the safety of sailors who may be struggling with their mental health while on extended deployment?

What measures did the Department take to mitigate the effects caused by foreseeable strain on standard replenishment procedures in a contested or combat environment?

What specific measures did the Department take to overcome unanticipated resource strains caused by adversaries in the CENTCOM AOR?

What methods of communication can family members and the public anticipate the Department will use to share information about conditions or other developments on board? Does the Department plan to use the same methods for future extended deployments for Operation Epic Fury, if applicable?

At time of writing, does the Department consider there to be a food shortage or chronic hygiene issues on the Lincoln during this stage of deployment?

What lessons learned, related to either personnel or material readiness from the extended deployment of the Ford, were put into practice to mitigate strain on the Lincoln personnel?

What new procedures, both for personnel and material readiness, can be informed by the extended deployments of the Ford and the Lincoln and how may they be implemented for a potential deployment of the George Washington or other carriers facing lengthy deployments?

What lessons learned, related to the Ford’s post-deployment, can be put into practice when the Lincoln returns for its maintenance availability?

If the George Washington shifts to CENTCOM to relieve the Lincoln, what are the Navy’s plans to maintain its current force posture in INDOPACOM?

title: Dingell, Bergman Co-Lead Letter Highlighting the Essential Role of Gift of Life Michigan
text:
U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and Jack Bergman (R-MI-01), alongside nine of their Michigan colleagues in the U.S. House, co-led a letter to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the Center for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) highlighting the essential role of Gift of Life Michigan. Gift of Life Michigan is the federally designated non-profit Organ Procurement Organization (OPO) serving Michigan. As CMS undertakes this year’s OPO recertification process, the lawmakers are urging the administration to consider the essential role Gift of Life Michigan and its nearly 400 staff statewide play in serving their communities and sustaining the systems that make life-saving organ, eye, and tissue donation and transplantation possible.

A copy of the letter can be found HERE and below:

Dear Secretary Kennedy and Administrator Oz:

We write as the congressional delegation representing Michigan to express our strong support for the recertification of Gift of Life Michigan, the federally designated non-profit Organ Procurement Organization (OPO) serving our state. As CMS undertakes this year’s OPO recertification process, we urge you to thoughtfully consider the essential role Gift of Life Michigan—and its nearly 400 staff statewide—play in serving our communities and sustaining the systems that make life-saving organ, eye, and tissue donation and transplantation possible.

Since its founding in 1971, Gift of Life Michigan has built deep and enduring relationships with hospitals, health systems, medical examiners, transplant centers, and local community leaders across the state. They have also developed a profound understanding of Michigan’s population, the regional healthcare and governmental landscape, and the unique cultural contexts that shape effective donation work—expertise that cannot be quickly recreated or replaced without significant disruption and added taxpayer expense.

During the current certification cycle, Gift of Life Michigan has increased the number of organs available for transplant by 29% and expanded the Michigan Organ Donor Registry by 1.2 million people through sustained public education and community outreach12. The organization has also grown youth education efforts from 3,700 to more than 38,000 students, per internal data. Additionally, according to data from the Michigan Department of Treasury and Michigan Department of State, Gift of Life Michigan worked with state legislators and the Secretary of State to make Michigan the first state in the nation to include a Donor Registry question on state income tax forms—an initiative that has already produced 38,000 new donor registrations since 2024.

Given Gift of Life Michigan’s decades of experience, strong performance, deep community partnerships, and critical role in ensuring access to donation and transplantation services, we urge CMS to provide full and fair consideration of the organization’s longstanding service and effectiveness.

Maintaining continuity with a well-established, community-rooted OPO is essential to preserving public trust, supporting donor families, and ensuring patients across Michigan and the nation continue to receive timely, high-quality, life-saving donation and transplant services.

title: Dingell Presses United States Postal Service on Mailing Disruptions
text:
U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) is demanding answers from the United States Postal Service (USPS) following delays of time-sensitive mail deliveries across Southeast Michigan. In a letter to Postmaster General David Steiner, Congresswoman Dingell highlighted the responsibilities of the USPS to ensure deliveries are received in a timely fashion and the recent failures of the department to deliver voting materials during the Michigan primary elections. The mail was not returned, they sat in mailboxes, and they were not picked up.

“These delayed deliveries left many Ann Arbor residents without their scheduled absentee ballots and political mail, limiting their time to vote before the statutory deadline and possibly preventing them from casting their ballots and receiving important candidate information. USPS has a responsibility to deliver the mail reliably and on time, especially when those delays can directly affect Americans’ ability to participate in our democracy," said Congresswoman Dingell.

Congresswoman Dingell ended the letter with a series of questions, including a request for future actions the USPS has put in place to ensure that a similar situation does not recur.

This effort follows an April letter to the Trump Administration demanding answers for similar mail delivery disruptions

A copy of the letter can be found HERE and below:

Dear Postmaster General Steiner:

This letter is regarding mail service disruptions in my district, particularly the delay of absentee ballots and political mail. The United States Postal Service (USPS) has a responsibility to remain accessible to all communities and ensure the delivery of essential mail, including bills, medications, legal documents, and urgent communications. The reliable delivery of time-sensitive mail is of the utmost importance.

I was alarmed to hear that on August 1, 2026, five carrier routes in Ann Arbor, Michigan, were left without assigned letter carriers, resulting in mail going undelivered. Just as concerning, USPS management failed to contact available employees to seek additional assistance in covering these routes, allowing the mail to remain untouched. Although employees are not required to work based solely on management’s outreach, failing to make any effort to find volunteers is unacceptable, particularly given that the state’s primary election was held on Tuesday, August 4, 2026. These delayed deliveries left many Ann Arbor residents without their scheduled absentee ballots and political mail, limiting their time to vote before the statutory deadline and possibly preventing them from casting their ballots and receiving important candidate information. USPS has a responsibility to deliver the mail reliably and on time, especially when those delays can directly affect Americans’ ability to participate in our democracy.

This incident is increasingly troubling, as I had raised concerns about persistent mail delays in Southeast Michigan in April of this year. One would expect the Postal Service to take these concerns seriously and to ensure that sufficient staffing and management procedures are in place to prevent similar failures. USPS plays a critical role in facilitating participation in our democratic processes, and I will continue to work to ensure my constituents have the reliable service they deserve.

I request clarity regarding this issue in my district and would like written responses to the following questions:

Was USPS aware of the five carrier routes in Ann Arbor, Michigan not receiving mail on August 1, 2026?

title: Congressmen Davis and Finstad Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Give States Flexibility to Respond to Local Employment Needs
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Congressmen Don Davis (NC-01) and Brad Finstad (MN-01) introduced the H.R. 10085, Lifelong Learning Act, which would update the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) to distribute additional resources to workforce training programs that address current talent shortages by upskilling active employees and reconnecting individuals to the job market.

“Across eastern North Carolina, employers are looking for skilled workers while hardworking people are seeking opportunities to grow, earn more, and build lasting careers close to home,” said Congressman Davis. “The Lifelong Learning Act gives our local workforce boards greater flexibility to help businesses train and retain employees, prevent layoffs, and reconnect more North Carolinians with the workforce. Strengthening our talent pipeline will help rural communities compete, attract new investment, and grow our regional economy.”

“Developing our workforce is critical to the success of our communities and economy. I am proud to join Congressman Davis in introducing the Lifelong Learning Act, which would give our local Workforce Development Boards increased flexibility to meet local needs, invest in incumbent worker and transitional job training, and equip individuals with essential workforce training and skill development, ultimately connecting them with more in-demand jobs,” said Congressman Finstad.

The Lifelong Learning Act updates WIOA guidelines, allowing Local Workforce Development Boards (LWDBs) to:

Utilize up to 30 percent of their Adult and Dislocated Worker budget for Incumbent Worker Training (IWT), which helps employers equip current employees with in-demand skills that expand career opportunities and avert layoffs. IWT programs have been crucial in helping LWDBs respond to broad labor market issues, such as increased automation since the COVID-19 pandemic. WIOA currently limits LWDBs from investing more than 20 percent of their budget for IWT programs.

Expand the allowable cap for transitional job training opportunities from 10 to 15 percent, allowing LWDBs to offer more programs aimed at recruiting individuals back into the labor force. This includes programs for justice-involved individuals, young adults transitioning out of foster care, and those who have inconsistent work histories.

Allow LWDBs to serve as the one-stop operators in local workforce areas to provide an integrated and coordinated system for the delivery of workforce development programs and services tailored to local needs. WIOA includes a requirement that LWDBs identify and select a one-stop operator via a competitive process.

The bipartisan Senate companion bill, S. 3870, was introduced this past February by Senators Gary Peters (MI), Ted Budd (NC), and John Hickenlooper (CO).

title: DOWNING VISITS DRY-REDWATER REGIONAL WATER AUTHORITY, HIGHLIGHTS PROGRESS ON H.R. 8745
text:
SIDNEY, MT. – Congressman Troy Downing (MT-02) joined members of the Dry-Redwater Regional Water Authority Board in Sidney to discuss progress on H.R. 8745, his legislation to authorize construction of the Dry-Redwater Rural Water System.

During the meeting, Downing updated board members on the bill’s status in the House and discussed the federal authorization process, project timelines, and next steps for advancing the legislation through Congress.

Congressman Downing with the Dry-Redwater Regional Water Authority Board

“Eastern Montana has waited far too long for clean and reliable water,” said Congressman Downing. “The Dry-Redwater Regional Water Authorization Act will help move this critical project forward and deliver the infrastructure these communities need. I appreciate the work of the Dry-Redwater Regional Water Authority and will keep working to get this bill across the finish line.”

H.R. 8745 would authorize construction of the Dry-Redwater Rural Water System, serving communities in Dawson, Garfield, McCone, Prairie, and Richland counties. These areas have historically faced poor water quality.

The proposed system would include a water treatment plant, more than 1,300 miles of pipeline, 116 miles of electrical lines, 12 pump stations, and six storage tanks.

Read the bill textHERE.

Background

Downing introduced H.R. 8745 in May 2026. Companion legislation was introduced in the U.S. Senate by Senators Steve Daines and Tim Sheehy.

The Dry-Redwater Rural Water System is designed to expand access to clean and reliable water across eastern Montana and provide long-term infrastructure for rural communities in the region.

title: Figures Announces $8.5 Million to Fix Runway at the Montgomery Airport
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Shomari C. Figures (AL-02), a member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, announced that over $8.5 million in federal funding has been awarded for renovations and improvements at the Montgomery Regional Airport.

The funding will help strengthen core airport infrastructure while enhancing safety and operational efficiency. These improvements are critical to ensuring the airport can meet current needs, maintain compliance with federal standards, and support continued growth in passenger travel and business activity.

title: Finstad Joins House Ag Committee Chairman Thompson at Agribusiness Luncheon
text:
ROCHESTER, MN – Today, Congressman Brad Finstad (MN-01) joined House Committee on Agriculture Chairman Glenn “GT” Thompson (PA-15), local farmers, and stakeholders from southern Minnesota’s agriculture community at the Steele County Agribusiness Luncheon hosted by Linder Farm Network in Owatonna. Finstad. “Today’s luncheon gave us the opportunity to discuss how we can continue defending and supporting our producers. title: Reps. Finstad, Fischbach, House Ag Committee Chairman Thompson Hold Roundtable Discussions in Mankato

title: Rep. Fischbach Introduces the Hardworking Seniors Act
text:
Washington, DC - This week, Congresswoman Michelle Fischbach (MN-07) introduced the Hardworking Seniors Act to allow our seniors to continue contributing to Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) while covered under Medicare Part A.

"Hardworking seniors are currently barred from contributing to tax-advantaged Health Savings Accounts just because they are receiving Medicare," said Rep. Fischbach. "I am excited to introduce the Hardworking Seniors Act to help America's working seniors continue to make these contributions and receive the tax benefits that go with them."

The Hardworking Seniors Act received support from several outside organizations:

A letter of support from the Employers Council on Flexible Compensation (ECFC) stated, "Allowing HSA contributions for working seniors would give them a flexible, tax advantaged tool to prepare for these costs, strengthening the financial security and reducing the long term burden on those with fixed incomes. ECFC supports your introduction of legislation to allow working senior to continue to have access to HSAs."

"Thank you very much for introducing the important, hardworking seniors legislation to allow working seniors of large employers with qualifying High Deductible Health Plans to contribute to a Health Savings Account while on their employer's health plan," said Daniel Perrin, Founder of HSA Coalition. "This is a key step forward to allowing those on public health plans to be eligible for a Health Savings Account."

title: Rep. Foushee Introduces Legislation to Reduce Medical Waste and Advance Sustainability in Health Care
text:
DURHAM, NC (August 14, 2026) — Yesterday, Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04) introduced the Sustainable Hospitals Act, legislation directing the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to study whether certain medical devices currently designated for single use could be safely reprocessed and reused.

“Every year, our health care system throws away enormous amounts of material, and we should be looking for smart, safe ways to reduce that waste,” said Congresswoman Valerie Foushee. “If we can safely reprocess and reuse certain devices, we can cut medical waste, lower costs, and make our health care system more sustainable. I’m proud to introduce the Sustainable Hospitals Act to take a closer look at this opportunity while keeping patient safety at the center.”

Hospitals and health care systems generate significant amounts of medical waste, while also facing pressure to control costs and make the most effective use of limited resources. Reprocessing certain medical devices may offer an opportunity to reduce waste and expenses, but any expansion of reuse must be grounded in rigorous safety standards, quality controls, and infection prevention practices.

“Duke Health is committed to delivering expert care in a way that is also fiscally and environmentally responsible. We support efforts to identify opportunities to reduce waste without compromising patient safety, and we believe this legislation establishes the right framework, grounding any expansion of single-use device reprocessing in rigorous FDA evaluation before it reaches the bedside." — Duke University Health System.

The Sustainable Hospitals Act would specifically direct HHS to examine:

Existing FDA pathways for reprocessing single-use devices, including where current regulations are sufficient and where barriers may exist;

The role of FDA-cleared third-party reprocessors compared with in-house hospital reprocessing;

The operational feasibility, including sterile processing capacity, staffing, equipment, chain of custody, tracking, and quality assurance;

Potential financial and environmental benefits, including waste reduction and cost savings, as well as additional labor, capital, and compliance costs; and

Liability and accountability issues if a reprocessed device fails or contributes to patient harm.

The study would also require consultation with hospitals, supply-chain leaders, infection prevention organizations, sterile processing professionals, clinicians, industry representatives, the FDA, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.

Within one year of enactment, HHS would be required to report its findings to Congress, including a list of the single-use devices that may have potential for safe reuse and recommendations for programs and activities to facilitate such reuse. Those recommendations could include the use of FDA-cleared reprocessors, appropriate cleaning and sterilization technologies, quality-assurance and tracking systems, and infection-prevention controls.

title: Golden statement on Trump’s new push to offshore Navy shipbuilding
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Jared Golden (ME-02) released the following statement in response to President Donald Trump’s latest effort to build American warships in foreign shipyards:

“I don’t know how we’re supposed to take any soaring ‘America-first’ language from this administration seriously when it appears to be bound and determined to send American shipbuilding jobs overseas and, now, to sell American shipyards to foreign corporations. Luckily, the House has already given bipartisan support to my language to block this short-sighted offshoring scheme, and the Senate is poised to do the same. Congress must take seriously its job to protect national security and American jobs.”

BACKGROUND:

Golden successfully amended this year’s National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) to explicitly prohibit the appropriation of federal funds to build American ships overseas. The House passed the NDAA, with Golden’s language to protect American shipbuilding, in July.

Golden’s amendment was in response to a Navy Shipbuilding Plan released by the Pentagon earlier this year, which called for offshoring the production of some warships, or parts of warships, in overseas yards.

Maine’s 2nd Congressional District is home to scores of shipbuilders employed at Bath Iron Works who build DDG-51 Destroyers, which Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has called the “workhorse” of the US naval fleet.

title: Congressman Vicente Gonzalez Secures $2 Million in Federal Funding for the City of Donna’s Multi-Purpose Sports Complex
text:

Donna, Texas – Today, Congressman Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34), joined by Mayor David Moreno and officials from the City of Donna, delivered $2 million in Fiscal Year 2026 Community Project Funding he secured for Phase Two construction of the Donna Multi-Purpose Sports Complex. Specifically, the funds will be used to develop the South side of the park with new recreational amenities, including a covered basketball pavilion, playground area, dog park, restrooms, workout stations, and a market walk for community events and vendors.

I want to thank U.S. Congressman Vicente Gonzalez for his tireless work in securing federal funding for Donna. title: Congressman Hamadeh Honored to Introduce the Mueller-Keating Memorial Highway Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - Congressman Abe Hamadeh (AZ-08) is honored to announce the introduction of the Mueller-Keating Memorial Highway Act, which designates a section of I-17 to honor Kayla Mueller and Charlie Keating.

The Mueller-Keating Memorial Highway Act will honor the lives of “Arizona’s Angel” Kayla Mueller and Chief Special Warfare Operator (SEAL) Charles H. Keating IV, who embody Arizona’s dual legacy of humanitarian courage and combat sacrifice in the fight against ISIS.

The Mueller-Keating Memorial Highway will begin in Prescott, Kayla’s hometown, and end in Phoenix, Charlie’s hometown.

Congressman Hamadeh introduced the legislation on August 13 in advance of what should have been Kayla’s 38th birthday on August 14.

Chief Keating was the third U.S. servicemember killed in Operation Inherent Resolve. “Combined Joint Task Force - Operation Inherent Resolve was formed in 2014 to reclaim land stolen by ISIS in Iraq and Syria, dismantle the group’s network, and protect the population from its violence and influence.” [1]

Kayla was abducted by terrorists while leaving a Doctors Without Borders hospital in Aleppo, Syria, in 2013. She was held captive for 18 month and killed by ISIS militants, including then-ISIS leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi.

Congressman Hamadeh, a former U.S. Army Intelligence Officer, took his oath of office while honoring the life of Kayla by using her family’s Bible during the ceremony in Washington, D.C. He was joined by his family and Kayla's parents, Carl and Marsha Mueller.

In August 2025, Congressman Hamadeh made an unprecedented trip from Jerusalem to Damascus to meet with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa and Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani to discuss the Congressman's continuing eﬀorts to bring Kayla’s body home and advance the Peace Through Strength agenda.

“Operation Inherent Resolve demanded both military force and humanitarian resolve, and this designation recognizes the distinct, yet complementary roles our beloved Arizonans played in that effort,” stated Congressman Hamadeh. “We can never forget the victims of ISIS and these two Americans that faced that evil with faith and courage.”

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Introduces GATE Act to Protect U.S. National Laboratories from Foreign Adversaries
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) introduced the Guarding American Technology from Exploitation (GATE) Act, legislation to strengthen security at U.S. National Laboratories by restricting access for nationals of China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and Cuba. The legislation is the House companion to legislation introduced by Senator Tom Cotton (R-AR).

“America’s National Laboratories are home to some of the most sensitive and valuable research in the world, and the same countries working to steal American technology should not have routine access to the facilities developing it,” said Congressman Harrigan. “China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea have spent years targeting American innovation to close the technological gap with the United States. The GATE Act puts a clear safeguard around critical American research while preserving access when our own counterintelligence professionals determine it serves the national interest.”

“Scientists from our adversaries like Russia and China should be nowhere near our national laboratories,” said Senator Tom Cotton. “Foreign nationals in our country’s most sensitive labs pose a clear threat to our national security and should end immediately.”

The GATE Act prohibits covered foreign nationals from accessing National Laboratory facilities, information, or technology as visitors or long-term assignees, while exempting U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents. The legislation allows the Secretary of Energy to grant a waiver only after consultation with Department of Energy intelligence officials and senior FBI counterintelligence officials, and only when the benefits to the United States outweigh the national security and economic risks.

The legislation also requires the Department of Energy to notify Congress within 30 days of granting a waiver and disclose the individual’s country of origin, the timeline of the decision, and the specific justification for allowing access. Congressman Harrigan will continue working to protect American research and intellectual property and prevent foreign adversaries from exploiting taxpayer-funded innovation.

title: Harshbarger Applauds Recent HHS Crackdown on Sex-Rejecting Procedures for Children
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger (R-TN) released the following statement praising a series of recent actions by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to protect children from sex-rejecting procedures, including a report exposing fraudulent billing practices that led to referrals of hospitals and clinics to the Department of Justice (DOJ) and HHS Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG), and a new Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) rule ending federal Medicaid and Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) funding for these procedures.

“Families trust physicians with their children's care, and this week's revelations show that trust was betrayed in the worst possible way. HHS's report exposes an industry that turned vulnerable, healthy children into a cash cow business, using fraudulent diagnosis codes to bill nearly $120 million while inflicting permanent damage on children who deserved protection, not to be used for profit,” said Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger. “Every child is a precious gift from God, made exactly as He intended, and no doctor, no hospital, and no insurance company has the right to convince a child otherwise in order to add to their bottom line. I am grateful CMS is finally cutting off every taxpayer dollar that funded this abuse, and I will not rest until Congress passes my STOP Act and TRUTH in Coverage Act so this industry can never prey on another child again.”

BACKGROUND:

HHS Report on Fraudulent Billing Practices

A new HHS report titled "Wolves in White Coats: How Doctors and Hospitals Pushed and Profited from the Fraud of 'Gender Medicine'" found that financial incentives drove hospitals nationwide to treat physiologically healthy children as "captive patients," billing nearly $120 million for sex-rejecting procedures on minors since 2019 and covering more than 5,500 surgeries and 8,500 courses of hormones or puberty blockers.

The report identified nearly $50 million in insurance claims for puberty blockers billed using vague or inaccurate endocrine disorder diagnosis codes instead of an accurate diagnosis, and nearly $11 million in claims for patients ages 13-17 billed under a precocious puberty diagnosis that does not typically apply at that age. In a separate case cited in the report, Texas Children's Hospital previously paid a $10 million settlement with the Texas Attorney General and the U.S. Department of Justice to resolve fraud allegations involving false diagnosis codes used to bill Medicaid for these procedures, agreeing as part of that settlement to establish the nation's first Detransition Clinic to provide free care for patients recovering from these interventions.

The report also found that the Biden administration actively promoted and expanded access to these procedures through executive orders, HHS civil rights guidance, CMS insurance mandates, and federal employee health benefits, pressuring hospitals and insurers to cover them for minors.

Following the report's release, Vice President JD Vance, as chairman of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, and HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. referred hospitals and clinics identified in the report to the DOJ and the HHS-OIG, respectively, for possible violations of federal law.

CMS Rule Ending Medicaid and CHIP Funding

Separately, CMS finalized a rule this week ending federal Medicaid and CHIP funding for sex-rejecting procedures on children and youth. The rule takes effect Oct. 13, 2026, allows a tapering-off period of up to six months for children currently on hormone therapy, and does not affect coverage of mental health services.

Harshbarger’s Efforts to Protect Children from Sex-Rejecting Procedures

In April, Harshbarger introduced theSafeguarding the Overall Protection of Minors (STOP) Actalongside Sen. Roger Marshall (R-KS). The bill bans gender transition procedures on minors, imposes civil penalties of at least $100,000 per violation collectible by the Attorney General, and creates a private right of action allowing victims or their families to sue for damages in federal court. It also establishes the Victims of Gender Transition Procedures Compensation Fund in the U.S. Treasury to support those recovering from these procedures, funded by civil penalties collected from offenders.

In July, Harshbarger introduced the Treatment and Restoration Uniformity and Transparency in Health Coverage (TRUTH in Coverage) Act. The bill requires health insurance plans that cover sex-rejecting procedures to also cover restorative care for patients who suffer complications, adverse outcomes, or seek to restore healthy bodily function, applying the same coverage terms, deductibles, and cost-sharing rules to both.

In December 2025, Harshbarger joined HHS Secretary Kennedy, CMS Administrator Dr. Oz, and other senior HHS officials for a press conference announcing federal actions to protect children from sex-rejecting procedures, including a declaration that these interventions do not meet professionally recognized standards of care and proposed CMS rules restricting Medicare and Medicaid coverage of them.

title: Comisionado Residente y 25 congresistas exhortan a la Gobernadora que solicite declaración de emergencia federal por crisis de agua.
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández lideró una carta junto a 25 congresistas urgiendo a la gobernadora Jenniffer González-Colón a solicitar sin más demora al presidente Donald Trump una declaración de desastre mayor ante la crisis de agua que afecta a Puerto Rico. Bajo la ley federal Stafford, corresponde a la Gobernadora solicitar formalmente al Presidente una declaración de desastre mayor.

Una declaración de desastre mayor podría permitir el acceso a asistencia de FEMA para municipios y entidades públicas, ayuda para individuos y familias afectadas, y préstamos por desastre de la Administración de Pequeños Negocios (SBA) para hogares y negocios elegibles. También podría proveer fondos para cubrir costos de respuesta a la emergencia, reparar infraestructura pública afectada, movilizar asistencia federal directa y financiar medidas para fortalecer la infraestructura y reducir el impacto de futuras emergencias.

“Puerto Rico enfrenta una crisis de agua que ya no puede atenderse con medidas temporales. Más de 180,000 hogares están bajo racionamientos de hasta 48 horas, y durante demasiado tiempo cientos de miles de personas han sufrido interrupciones en el servicio,” escribieron el Comisionado Residente y los congresistas. “La Gobernadora es quien debe solicitar esta declaración al Presidente, y debe hacerlo sin más demora para que podamos movilizar toda la asistencia federal disponible. El pueblo de Puerto Rico no puede seguir esperando.”

La carta, liderada por el Comisionado Residente, contó con el respaldo de 25 miembros del Congreso, reflejando un creciente apoyo en Washington al reclamo para movilizar recursos federales adicionales ante la crisis de agua en Puerto Rico. Esta semana, la Asociación de Alcaldes también apoyó el reclamo del comisionado residente.

La carta fue firmada por el demócrata de mayor rango del Comité de Recursos Naturales, Jared Huffman (CA-02), el demócrata de mayor rango del Comité de Seguridad Nacional, Bennie Thompson (MS-02), y el senador Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), junto a los congresistas Sam Liccardo (CA-16), Jim Costa (CA-21), Luz Rivas (CA-29), Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), Norma Torres (CA-35), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Darren Soto (FL-09), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Rob Menendez (NJ-08), Nellie Pou (NJ-09), Gabe Vasquez (NM-02), Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Daniel Goldman (NY-10), Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Ritchie Torres (NY-15), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Seth Magaziner (RI-02), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34) y Emily Randall (WA-06).

“Seguiré trabajando con los congresistas y alcaldes para obtener más recursos para ayudar a la gente a superar esta emergencia y para que la AAA rinda cuentas por su mala administración.” dijo el Comisionado Residente.

Como parte de esos esfuerzos, la semana pasada presentó un plan de cinco pasos para atender la emergencia, que incluye una declaración federal, asistencia inmediata para las comunidades afectadas y medidas para fortalecer la infraestructura de agua de Puerto Rico. Además, esta semana el Comisionado Residente y líderes congresionales con jurisdicción sobre Puerto Rico, solicitaron a la Oficina de Rendición de Cuentas del Gobierno federal (GAO) una investigación sobre el estado del sistema, el uso de fondos federales y la respuesta de las agencias federales.

###

Hernández Leads 25 Members of Congress in Calling on Governor to Request Major Disaster Declaration Over Water Crisis

WASHINGTON, DC — Congressman Pablo José Hernández of Puerto Rico led 25 members of Congress in a letter urging Governor Jenniffer González-Colón to request, without further delay, that President Donald Trump issue a major disaster declaration in response to Puerto Rico’s ongoing water crisis. Under the federal Stafford Act, the Governor is responsible for formally requesting a major disaster declaration from the President.

A major disaster declaration could provide access to FEMA assistance for municipalities and public entities, assistance for affected individuals and families, and Small Business Administration (SBA) disaster loans for eligible households and businesses. It could also provide funding to cover emergency response costs, repair affected public infrastructure, mobilize direct federal assistance, and support measures to strengthen infrastructure and reduce the impact of future emergencies.

“Puerto Rico is facing a water crisis that can no longer be addressed through temporary measures. More than 180,000 households are under water rationing of up to 48 hours, and for far too long hundreds of thousands of people have experienced service interruptions,” wrote the lawmakers. “The Governor is the one who must request this declaration from the President, and she must do so without further delay so that we can mobilize all available federal assistance. The people of Puerto Rico cannot afford to wait any longer.”

This letter, spearheaded by Congressman Hernández and signed by 25 members of Congress, underscores growing support in Washington for efforts to mobilize additional federal resources in response to Puerto Rico’s water crisis. This week, the Asociación de Alcaldes de Puerto Rico (Puerto Rico Mayor's Association) also announced its support for the Resident Commissioner’s effort.

The letter was signed by the House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (CA-02), House Homeland Security Committee Ranking Member Bennie Thompson (MS-02), and Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), along with Sam Liccardo (CA-16), Jim Costa (CA-21), Luz Rivas (CA-29), Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), Norma Torres (CA-35), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Darren Soto (FL-09), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Rob Menendez (NJ-08), Nellie Pou (NJ-09), Gabe Vasquez (NM-02), Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Daniel Goldman (NY-10), Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Ritchie Torres (NY-15), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Seth Magaziner (RI-02), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34), and Emily Randall (WA-06).

“I will continue working with members of Congress and mayors to secure additional resources to help people through this emergency and to hold the Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority (AAA) accountable for its mismanagement,” said Hernández.

As part of those efforts, last week he introduced a five-step plan to address the emergency, including a federal disaster declaration, immediate assistance for affected communities, and measures to strengthen Puerto Rico’s water infrastructure. In addition, this week Hernández and congressional leaders with jurisdiction over Puerto Rico issues requested that the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) investigate the condition of the island’s water system, the use of federal funds, and the federal government’s response to the crisis.

title: Hudson Helps Secure New Verizon Cell Service Near Moore County Airport
text:
SOUTHERN PINES, NC –U.S. Representative Richard Hudson (NC-09), Chairman of the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology, announced Verizon has activated a new cell site near Moore County Airport, improving service for Verizon customers in the surrounding area.

“Folks in Moore County have told me loud and clear they need better cell service, and I’m glad we’re seeing results,” said Rep. Hudson. “When Mayor Clement raised these concerns, I brought Verizon to Moore County to see the problems firsthand. I appreciate Verizon following through and getting this site online, and I’ll keep working with providers to improve service across our community.”

The new service comes just weeks after Hudson visited the site near Moore County Airport with Verizon officials and Southern Pines Mayor Taylor Clement as part of his push for better cell service across the county.

Background

In July, Hudson brought Verizon officials to Moore County to see areas with poor cell service firsthand and hear directly from Mayor Clement about problems residents, businesses, and visitors were experiencing.

title: Republican Reps. Steve Scalise, John James visit Temple Israel in show of support for Jewish community
text:
A top member of Congress visited Michigan on Thursday to show support to the Jewish community following an attempted mass casualty attack that happened in March.

House Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-LA) visited Temple Israel in West Bloomfield. The congregation was the target of an attack by a gunman who rammed his truck, loaded with fireworks and gasoline, into the building and began shooting. The attack failed in part because the vehicle became jammed and the attacker was unable to get out of the burning vehicle, and he shot himself.

Around 140 children and staff were reportedly in the building at the time of the attack; had the attacker been able to exit the vehicle, the incident likely would have been far worse.

Scalise is the second highest-ranking member of the U.S. House of Representatives, behind just the Speaker of the House. He was joined at Temple Israel by Rep. John James, who represents parts of Oakland and Macomb counties in Congress.

James co-sponsored the Jewish American Security Act (H.R. 9211), which would help protect members of the Jewish community and other faith groups. One of the ways it would do that is by authorizing a significant increase in funding for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program that supports security at synagogues and other at-risk nonprofits.

“I appreciate Leader Scalise coming here to see the site of the attack first-hand, and to talk with community leaders,” said James, R-Shelby Township. “To have a top member of Congress visit signals that we are treating the rise in threats seriously, and that this is an urgent national concern.”

James immediately spoke in support of the congregation following the failed attack.

James also visited Israel in Nov. 2023, following the Oct. 7 terrorist attack in which Hamas militants raped and murdered innocent civilians, many of them young people peacefully enjoying a music festival.

“There is a sickness in a certain segment of our population that reacted to the Oct. 7 terrorist attack with sympathy for the attackers, and which has spent the past few years irrationally targeting members of the Jewish community here in Michigan with hateful words and actions,” James said. “I fought extremists in Iraq; we cannot let that kind of violent thinking take root here in Michigan. Everyone should be able to live and worship in peace.”

title: Kaptur Applauds Additional Investment Of $289,597 For Northwest Ohio Airports
text:
Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, announced that two Northwest Ohio airports will receive United States Department of Transportation Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) awards for critical upgrades and improvements. The Defiance County Regional Airport Authority will receive $192,887 for pavement reconstruction, while the Put-in-Bay Township Port Authority will receive $96,710 for an airport-wide obstruction survey.

“Ohio’s strong aviation history shines bright across our Great Lakes region, and it is a privilege to build upon it by investing in local airport innovation and expansion,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). “Creating partnerships between Federal agencies and our local communities is vital to Northwest Ohio’ continued success. Working together to deliver these awards makes our airports safer and more efficient for all aviation staff, customers, and the businesses that rely on them. Together we are creating a standard of excellence that will help our region thrive for all the generations to come.”

Called Northwest Ohio’s “gateway to business and community,” Defiance County Memorial Airport has been undergoing many improvements over recent years to enhance its infrastructure. Today’s $192,887 investment will help the airport complete the final phase of reconstructing 1,091 square yards of East Apron pavement that has reached the end of its useful life. The Put-in-Bay Airport is located on South Bass Island and services both small commercial carriers and private aviators carrying freight or vacationers to the area. Its $96,710 award will help the airport conduct an airport-wide obstruction survey for the purpose of collecting detailed aeronautical and environmental data. Comprehensive data will make landing and takeoff safer and can help with future airport planning.

These new federal investments build on previous awards to airports across our Northwest Ohio region in recent years. In July of this year, Congresswoman Kaptur secured over $3.67 Million for Toledo-area airports and over $7.8 Million for three Northwest Ohio regional airports, including Erie-Ottawa International Airport, Toledo Executive Airport, and Fulton County Airport. On May 18th, Congresswoman Kaptur announced a $1.4 Million Award for Eugene F. Kranz Toledo Express Airport. On May 12th, 2026, Congresswoman Kaptur announced over $1 Million in federal investment for infrastructure improvements at Williams County Regional Airport, Defiance Memorial Airport, and Sandusky County Regional Airport.

title: Kean Hosts Eagle Scout and Girl Scout Gold Award Event
text:
(August 14, 2026) READINGTON, NJ – Yesterday, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) held his third Eagle Scout and Girl Scout Gold Award Event. Scouts from New Jersey's 7th Congressional District who achieved the rank of Eagle Scout or completed their Girl Scout Gold Award in 2025 and 2026 were invited to attend. Family, Scoutmasters and other adult scout leaders from across the district were also welcome to join the celebration with their Scouts.

Eagle Scout is the highest rank attainable in the Boy Scouts of America organization. To become an Eagle Scout, one must earn a total of 21 merit badges and demonstrate scout spirit, service, and leadership. This includes an extensive service project that scouts plan, organize, lead, and manage.

The Girl Scout Gold Award is the highest and most prestigious achievement in Girl Scouting, requiring Seniors and Ambassadors in grades 9–12 to complete a rigorous, sustainable community service project of at least 80 hours. They must identify a community issue, research its root cause, build a team of volunteers and community experts, and create a sustainable, long-lasting solution.

“Very few receive the rank of Eagle Scout or earn the Girl Scout Gold Award, and those who do deserve to be recognized for this achievement,” said Congressman Kean. “Through their generosity and creativity, they are laying the groundwork for lives that will be directed by the values of volunteering, leadership and civic duty, which will impact the world around them in distinct and impactful ways.”

“As an Eagle Scout myself, I was pleased to participate in Congressman Kean’s Scout recognition ceremony, where I had the opportunity to say a few words and introduce him,” said Eagle Scout and Readington Township Committeeman Adam Mueller. “Congressman Kean has been a consistent and genuine supporter of Scouting in our district. His commitment to recognizing the hard work, leadership, and service of our Scouts strengthens these programs and the young people who benefit from them. We’re fortunate to have a representative who understands the value of Scouting and actively invests in its success.”

“Being an Eagle Scout takes years of commitment, leadership, and hard work. It is a challenge that most kids, even Scouts, do not achieve,” said Eagle Scout Christopher Forzani. “Because of this, it was an honor to learn about the Eagle Projects of other local Scouts and to meet Congressman Tom Kean, who gifted each Scout a flag that had been flown over the Capitol.”

“I appreciate Congressman Kean and his staff hosting this event to recognize those who have earned the highest awards in Scouting,” said Girl Scout Gold Award recipient Faith Feldman. “It was really cool to receive a flag that has been flown at the US Capitol.”

The event honored 20 Eagle and Girl Scouts who represented all six counties in New Jersey’s 7th Congressional District. More than 55 people attended this event, including parents, grandparents, siblings, and adult scout leaders.
